problem.passage:
Third in line at the ticket counter, Mira watched the clerk hand the elderly farmer ahead of her a fare card stamped with the posted price. For the German couple who stepped up next, however, he quoted a figure nearly double the one printed on the same card. The clerk, a thin man who kept a pencil tucked behind one ______ never once glanced up at the fare board hanging above his window, as though he had long since memorized two different sets of prices.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Third in line at the ticket counter, Mira watched the clerk hand the elderly farmer ahead of her a fare card stamped with the posted price. For the German couple who stepped up next, however, he quoted a figure nearly double the one printed on the same card. The clerk, a thin man who kept a pencil tucked behind one ______ never once glanced up at the fare board hanging above his window, as though he had long since memorized two different sets of prices.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ear and hummed softly between customers,
ear and hummed softly between customers;
ear and hummed softly between customers—
ear and hummed softly between customers
problem.explanation: "a thin man ... customers"는 주어 "The clerk"를 설명하는 비필수 동격 어구이고, 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어와 동사 "never once glanced"가 이어진다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 두 독립절을 나누는 부호인데, 그러면 주어와 동사가 갈라지고 앞부분은 완전한 절이 되지 못한다. C의 대시는 동격 어구를 묶을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫아 부호가 서로 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 부호가 없어서 동격 어구가 어디서 끝나는지 알 수 없고, 동사 앞에서 삽입구가 끝나지 않은 채 남는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a thin man ... customers" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "The clerk." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "never once glanced," which is why A is correct. B's semicolon is used to separate two independent clauses, but here it would split the subject from its verb and leave an incomplete clause before it. C's dash can set off an appositive, but this one opened with a comma, so closing it with a dash gives you mismatched punctuation. D has no closing punctuation, so the appositive never ends before the verb and runs straight into the main clause.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A woman waiting at a railway station ticket counter realizes the clerk systematically overcharges foreign passengers while local fares remain unchanged

hardJudge.note: "The clerk, a thin man ... customers, never once glanced up" — 쉼표로 연 비필수 동격 어구를 쉼표로 닫는 구조로 A가 정확함. 삽입구 범위 파악과 여는 부호와의 짝 맞추기라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, C(대시)는 동격 어구를 묶을 수 있다는 부분적 근거가 있으며 B·D도 그럴듯하여 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 오류 없음. 지문은 독창적으로 보임.

advisory.note: A long appositive containing a relative clause and a compound verb (kept ... and hummed) pushes the closing comma far from where the phrase opens, so a test taker has to find the opening comma and then match it. The dash option (C) and the no-punctuation option (D) are believable distractors, so this fits medium difficulty.

problem.passage:
From the gallery of the lighthouse, Elias Marr had watched the Halvard, a rust-streaked freighter owned by the Brennick Shipping Company and flying a flag he did not recognize, slip past the warning buoys four times that month______ he entered the hour, the bearing, and the state of the tide in his logbook, pressing so hard that the nib tore the paper.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: From the gallery of the lighthouse, Elias Marr had watched the Halvard, a rust-streaked freighter owned by the Brennick Shipping Company and flying a flag he did not recognize, slip past the warning buoys four times that month______ he entered the hour, the bearing, and the state of the tide in his logbook, pressing so hard that the nib tore the paper.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , each time,
: and each time,
each time
; each time,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격 수식어(a rust-streaked freighter ... recognize)를 지나 'Elias Marr had watched ... that month'로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'he entered ...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있고, 도입 부사구 each time 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍을 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)다. B는 콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙였는데, 이런 조합은 표준 문장부호 규칙에 맞지 않는다. C는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: Once you look past the long appositive (a rust-streaked freighter ... recognize), the text before the blank is a complete independent clause ending with "that month." The text after the blank, "he entered ...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, and a comma can follow the introductory phrase "each time," so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice. B puts the conjunction "and" after a colon, and that combination doesn't follow standard punctuation conventions. C has no punctuation between the two clauses at all, which makes it a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A lighthouse keeper observes a shipping company's vessel repeatedly entering restricted waters despite posted warnings, documenting each violation in his logbook

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞(긴 동격구 포함 'Elias Marr had watched ... that month')과 뒤('he entered ...')가 모두 독립절이므로 세미콜론+도입구 쉼표인 D가 유일하게 적합. A는 comma splice, B는 콜론 뒤 and 조합으로 비표준, C는 run-on. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 긴 동격 수식어를 지나 절 구조를 파악해야 하고 A·B가 부분적으로 그럴듯해 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구 때문에 앞 독립절의 경계를 찾는 단계와, 'each time'이 어느 절에 붙는지 판단하는 단계가 필요하므로 medium에 맞음. A는 'each time'이 앞 절을 수식하는 것처럼 읽혀 그럴듯한 함정이고, B도 콜론을 써서 구조적으로 그럴듯함. D 외에는 정답이 될 수 있는 선택지가 없음.

problem.passage:
Madame Okonjo had watched Teodor's bow arm for three years, and she knew its habits as well as her own. Now, in the second week of October, the wrist that had once floated loosely at the frog had stiffened into a rigid hinge, exactly the kind of correction favored by Viktor Halas, a teacher across town known for drilling his pupils through hour after hour of relentless scale exercises______ did not need to ask where her student had been spending his Saturday mornings.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Madame Okonjo had watched Teodor's bow arm for three years, and she knew its habits as well as her own. Now, in the second week of October, the wrist that had once floated loosely at the frog had stiffened into a rigid hinge, exactly the kind of correction favored by Viktor Halas, a teacher across town known for drilling his pupils through hour after hour of relentless scale exercises______ did not need to ask where her student had been spending his Saturday mornings.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: . She
, she
she
; and she
problem.explanation: 'Now, in the second week ... scale exercises'는 주어 'the wrist'와 동사 'had stiffened'를 갖춘 독립절이고, 그 끝에는 Viktor Halas를 꾸미는 긴 동격구가 붙어 있다. 'she did not need to ask...'도 새로운 독립절이므로 두 절은 마침표로 나눠야 하고, 그래서 정답은 A이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 'and'를 함께 써서 관례에 맞지 않는다. 세미콜론은 그것만으로 절을 잇거나, 쉼표+and를 써야 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The section from "Now, in the second week" through "scale exercises" is an independent clause. Its subject is "the wrist," its verb is "had stiffened," and it ends with a long appositive phrase describing Viktor Halas. "She did not need to ask..." is a second independent clause, so the two need to be split into separate sentences, and A is correct. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D pairs a semicolon with the conjunction "and," which isn't conventional. You should use either a semicolon alone or a comma plus "and."

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A conservatory violin instructor notices a promising student's technique regressing after the student begins private lessons with a competing teacher across town

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 명확히 옳음(두 독립절을 마침표로 분리). B(comma splice), C(run-on)는 확실한 오답. 다만 D('; and she')는 실제 SAT에서 거의 오답 선택지로 쓰지 않는 논쟁적 형태로, 내부 쉼표가 많은 이 문장에서는 스타일 가이드상 허용될 수 있어 정답 유일성이 약간 흔들림. 보다 안전한 오답(예: ', and' 없이 ', which' 등)으로 교체를 권고. 난이도는 긴 문장에서 절 경계를 찾는 과정이 필요하여 medium에 적합하나, B·C가 비교적 쉽게 배제되는 편.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 옳다. 다만 앞 절 내부에 쉼표가 많아 D('; and')도 일부 스타일 기준에서는 허용될 수 있으므로 약한 모호성이 있다. SAT 관례상 D는 오답으로 처리되므로 판정은 유지한다. 긴 동격구 때문에 절의 경계를 찾기 어렵다는 점이 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
For six years, Marisol had told herself that Dr. Hale's crowded appointment book was simply a sign of his reputation: patients trusted him, so they kept coming back. Now, laying out scalers on a tray in the next room, she heard him on the phone booking three crowns for Mr. Okafor, whose X-rays she had studied that very morning and found free of decay. ______ the comforting explanation she had leaned on for so long no longer seemed to hold, and her hands went still above the tray.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: For six years, Marisol had told herself that Dr. Hale's crowded appointment book was simply a sign of his reputation: patients trusted him, so they kept coming back. Now, laying out scalers on a tray in the next room, she heard him on the phone booking three crowns for Mr. Okafor, whose X-rays she had studied that very morning and found free of decay. ______ the comforting explanation she had leaned on for so long no longer seemed to hold, and her hands went still above the tray.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Consequently,
For example,
Likewise,
problem.explanation: 마리솔은 충치가 없는 엑스레이를 직접 확인했는데 의사가 크라운 세 개를 예약하는 것을 듣는다. 빈칸 뒤의 '오랫동안 믿어 온 설명이 더는 성립하지 않는다'는 이 발견에서 나온 결과이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 앞 내용과 대조되는 듯하지만 빈칸 뒤 문장은 바로 앞의 발견을 뒤집는 게 아니라 그 발견에서 나온 것이다. C는 빈칸 뒤 문장을 앞 내용의 예시로 보는데, 그 문장은 사례가 아니라 결론이다. D는 비슷한 사건을 하나 더 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말이지만 그런 내용이 이어지지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Marisol hears Dr. Hale book three crowns for a patient whose X-rays she checked herself and found free of decay. The sentence after the blank says her long-held explanation no longer holds, and that follows directly from what she just heard, so B is correct. A may seem to fit because there is a contrast in the passage, but the second sentence doesn't push back against her discovery. It comes out of it. C would make the second sentence an example, but it's actually a conclusion. D signals that a similar point is being added, and the second sentence doesn't add anything parallel.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A dental hygienist overhears her employer scheduling patients for unnecessary procedures while she prepares cleaning instruments in the next room

hardJudge.note: 직접 검산: 빈칸 앞은 '충치 없는 환자에게 크라운 3개 예약'이라는 발견, 빈칸 뒤는 '오랜 설명이 더는 성립하지 않음'이라는 결과 → 인과 전환어 Consequently(B)가 유일하게 논리적. A는 지문 전체의 '과거 믿음 vs 현재 발견' 대조 때문에 훑어 읽으면 끌리는 매력적 오답이며, C·D는 예시/병렬 내용이 없어 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 오답 중 강한 유인 선택지는 A 하나이고 C·D는 비교적 약하지만, 서사 맥락 파악 + 전환 관계 판단의 두 단계가 필요하므로 medium 범위로 판단. 저작권·사실 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 인과 관계가 분명하다. 지문에 '오래 믿어 온 설명'과 '새로 알게 된 사실'의 대조가 깔려 있어 훑어 읽으면 A(Nevertheless)를 고르기 쉽다. C와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 최소한 말은 되므로 medium 난이도로 볼 수 있다.

problem.passage:
During registration week, Ms. Okafor stood at the back of the gymnasium and watched families line up at the counseling table. A banner above the table read "Advanced Placement: Every Student Belongs," and the principal had repeated the slogan at the morning assembly, promising that no one would be turned away from the new AP biology course. ______ when the Delgado twins, whose father had come straight from his shift at the feed mill, asked for the AP forms, the counselor smiled, suggested they "start with something more manageable," and slid two general science sheets across the table.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: During registration week, Ms. Okafor stood at the back of the gymnasium and watched families line up at the counseling table. A banner above the table read "Advanced Placement: Every Student Belongs," and the principal had repeated the slogan at the morning assembly, promising that no one would be turned away from the new AP biology course. ______ when the Delgado twins, whose father had come straight from his shift at the feed mill, asked for the AP forms, the counselor smiled, suggested they "start with something more manageable," and slid two general science sheets across the table.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In practice,
For instance,
As a result,
Likewise,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 학교가 모든 학생에게 AP 과정을 열어 두겠다고 공식적으로 약속했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 상담 교사가 저소득층 쌍둥이를 실제로는 일반 과목으로 유도하는 장면이다. 따라서 공식적인 말과 실제 행동의 차이를 드러내는 A가 정답이다. B는 쌍둥이 장면이 구체적 장면이라 그럴듯해 보이지만, 이 장면은 약속을 보여 주는 사례가 아니라 약속과 모순되는 장면이다. C는 약속 때문에 학생을 돌려보내는 결과가 생겼다는 인과 관계가 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다. D는 앞의 내용과 비슷한 내용이 이어진다는 뜻인데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 반대 방향의 내용이다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence gives the school's official promise that every student is welcome in AP courses, and the next sentence shows the counselor quietly steering low-income twins away from AP. A is correct because it signals the gap between what was officially said and what actually happens. B might look tempting because the twins' scene is specific, but that scene contradicts the promise rather than illustrating it. C would mean the promise caused students to be turned away, which isn't a logical cause-and-effect relationship. D signals that something similar is coming next, but the counselor's action goes in the opposite direction from the slogan.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A rural schoolteacher watches administrators systematically discourage low-income students from advanced placement course enrollment during registration week

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(공식 약속: 아무도 돌려보내지 않겠다)과 뒤 문장(상담 교사가 실제로 AP에서 일반 과목으로 유도)은 '말 vs. 실제'의 대조 관계이므로 "In practice,"가 유일하게 논리적임. B는 뒤 장면이 구체적 사례처럼 보여 부분적 유혹이 있으나 약속과 모순되는 장면이므로 배제됨. C는 인과 관계 불성립, D는 유사성 표지로 방향이 반대. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 빈칸 뒤 소문자 "when"은 쉼표 포함 전환어 형식에 부합. 지문은 독창적 서사로 저작권 의혹 없음. 단순 'However'가 아닌 '실제로는'이라는 뉘앙스를 문맥에서 파악해야 하고 B가 유의미한 오답으로 기능하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 공식 약속과 실제 행동의 대비는 정독해야 파악된다. 'For instance'는 구체적 장면 때문에 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉬운 강한 오답이다. C와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 중간 난이도로 볼 수 있다.

problem.passage:
Ines had threaded films at the Halcyon for eleven years, and she knew the rhythm of a reel change the way other people know their own heartbeat. So when the second reel of the Saturday feature ran out a good four minutes before the cue marks she expected, she frowned and reached for the distributor's invoice taped beside the projector. The company charged the Halcyon by the minute of footage delivered, and the sheet listed the film at its full advertised length. Over the next week she timed every print that came through the booth, and each one fell several minutes short of the running time printed on its bill. ______ the cinema had been paying, week after week, for scenes that never reached its screen.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Ines had threaded films at the Halcyon for eleven years, and she knew the rhythm of a reel change the way other people know their own heartbeat. So when the second reel of the Saturday feature ran out a good four minutes before the cue marks she expected, she frowned and reached for the distributor's invoice taped beside the projector. The company charged the Halcyon by the minute of footage delivered, and the sheet listed the film at its full advertised length. Over the next week she timed every print that came through the booth, and each one fell several minutes short of the running time printed on its bill. ______ the cinema had been paying, week after week, for scenes that never reached its screen.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In contrast,
Consequently,
For example,
Nevertheless,
problem.explanation: 회사는 전달된 필름의 분량(분)만큼 요금을 매겼는데, 실제 필름은 청구서에 적힌 상영 시간보다 매번 몇 분씩 짧았다. 이 두 정보를 합치면, 극장이 받지도 못한 장면 값을 내 왔다는 것이 그 결과이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 청구서와 실제 필름이 대비되는 것처럼 보여 끌리지만, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용과 대조되는 것이 아니라 그로부터 나오는 결론이다. C는 마지막 문장이 구체적으로 보여 끌리지만, 앞 주장의 사례가 아니라 앞 증거를 요약한 결론이다. D는 앞 내용에도 불구하고 뜻밖의 결과가 나온다는 뜻이 되는데, 과다 청구는 앞 내용에서 예상되는 결과다.
problem.explanationEn: The company charged by the minute of footage delivered, but every print was several minutes shorter than the length on its bill. When you put those two facts together, it follows that the cinema paid for scenes it never got, so B is correct. A is tempting because the invoices and the actual reels don't match, but the last sentence isn't contrasting with what came before; it's the conclusion drawn from it. C is tempting because the last sentence sounds specific, but it isn't an example of an earlier claim; it sums up the evidence. D would signal a surprising outcome "despite" the facts, but the overbilling is exactly what those facts lead you to expect.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A film projectionist at an independent cinema realizes the distribution company has been billing them for incomplete reels of movies

Because the text sets an outward promise against the hidden truth, C is correct, since it signals that contrast between appearance and reality. A presents the polite letter as the cause of the private meetings, but those meetings had "already" taken place, so the cause and effect run the wrong way. B is used to emphasize or support the previous point, but this sentence undercuts the promise. D adds a similar example, but the sentence that follows is the opposite of the promise, not something similar to it.

Marguerite understood at once what the difference might cost him, and she knew Hale would read her transcript before anyone else did. ______ she recorded the testimony exactly as it was spoken, the word "red" included.

options: Even so,
Therefore,
Similarly,
For example,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 증언이 고용주 Hale에게 불리할 수 있고 Hale이 속기록을 먼저 읽는다는 점, 즉 기록을 망설이거나 바꿀 압박 요인을 제시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 그녀가 "red"까지 그대로 기록했다는 내용이므로, 압박을 인정한 뒤 뒤집는 양보 전환어 A가 정답이다. B는 정확한 기록이 직업상 당연해 보여 그럴듯하지만, 앞 문장의 내용(Hale에게 미칠 손해와 그의 검토)은 정확히 기록할 이유가 아니라 오히려 망설일 이유이므로 인과 관계가 성립하지 않는다. C는 두 행동이 서로 비슷하다는 뜻인데, 상황을 이해한 것과 기록한 것은 같은 종류의 행동이 아니다. problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence lists pressures on Marguerite: the testimony could hurt her employer, Hale, and he will read her transcript first. These are reasons she might hesitate or change the record. The next sentence says she recorded everything exactly anyway, so the text needs a transition that admits that pressure and then reverses it, which makes A correct. B is tempting because recording testimony accurately sounds like what a stenographer should do, but the pressures in the previous sentence don't cause her accuracy; if anything, they push against it. C would mean the two actions are alike, but understanding the risk and recording the testimony aren't parallel actions. D doesn't work because her recording isn't an example of the sentence before it.

In The Quiet Margin, Dana Okafor learns that Veralin caused no side effects in any of the patients who took it during trials.
problem.explanation: 목표는 Dana가 무엇을 발견하는지 설명하는 것이다. C는 회사가 어지럼증과 메스꺼움이라는 부작용을 의사용 요약에서 숨겼다는 사실을 Dana가 알게 된다고 정확히 진술하므로 정답이다. A는 Dana의 직업과 판매 제품만 소개할 뿐 발견한 내용은 없다. B는 발견 이후 Dana가 내려야 할 결정을 말할 뿐, 무엇을 발견했는지는 밝히지 않는다. D는 부작용이 전혀 없었다고 하여 메모 내용과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain what Dana discovers. Choice C does this correctly: it says she learns that her company hid trial results showing dizziness and nausea. Choice A only describes her job and the drug she sells, so it never mentions a discovery. Choice B describes the decision Dana faces after her discovery, but it doesn't say what she found. Choice D contradicts the notes, which say many patients did have side effects.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Pharmaceutical sales representative learns company concealed moderate side effects in clinical trial data when marketing new medication

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 메모 3·4(내부 보고서의 부작용, 요약에서 누락)를 종합해 '발견 내용'을 정확히 진술한다. A는 배경 정보, B는 발견 이후의 결정, D는 메모와 정면 모순으로 각각 전형적 오답 유형이며 규칙(목표=발견 내용)만 알면 즉시 배제 가능하다. 가상의 소설·작가로 저작권 문제 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. easy 적합.

advisory.note: C의 'hid'와 'caused'는 메모의 '요약에서 빠졌다'와 '부작용이 있었다'를 조금 더 강하게 바꿔 말한 표현이지만, 허용 범위 안에 있다. D는 메모와 정면으로 모순되므로 다소 쉽게 배제된다. 그래도 easy 수준에는 적합하다.

problem.question: The student wants to explain why the chairs in the story want something taken away. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Mara Ellison, who wrote "The Quiet Shelf" in 2019, worked as a library assistant for six years before publishing fiction.

problem.explanation: 목표는 학과장들이 연구를 없애려는 '이유'를 설명하는 것이다. D는 그 연구가 학과장들의 학과가 지원하는 실험실의 결과와 모순된다는 이유를 제시하므로 정답이다. A는 작가의 경력만 다루어 목표와 관계없다. B는 주인공의 직업과 작가의 경력만 연결할 뿐 이유를 말하지 않는다. C는 학과장들이 무엇을 요구했는지는 말하지만 왜 그러는지는 빠져 있다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain the reason the chairs want the study removed. D does this by stating that the study contradicts findings from a lab their departments fund, so D is correct. A only gives facts about the author's career, which have nothing to do with the goal. B links the main character's job to the author's past but gives no reason. C tells you what the chairs ask for, but it leaves out why they ask for it.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — University librarian observes department chairs quietly pressuring her to remove published research contradicting their funded laboratory's competing findings

hardJudge.note: 목표(학과장들이 연구 제거를 원하는 '이유' 설명)에 대해 D만이 노트 4의 원인(학과가 지원하는 실험실 결과와의 모순)을 제시함. A·B는 작가 경력/주인공 직업만 다루고, C는 요구 내용만 있고 이유가 없어 전형적 오답으로 적절. 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 가상 작품으로 저작권 문제 없음. 단일 규칙(목표-정보 일치)으로 풀리는 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 사소한 점: D는 노트의 'ask'를 'pressure'로 바꿔 표현해 약간 과장되었으나 정답 판정에는 영향이 없다. 목표가 '이유'이므로 because 절이 있는 D만 답이 되며, 오답들은 전형적인 오답 유형이다.

In Mara Ellison's "The Quiet Room," funeral director Walter Pruitt works in a small town modeled on the one where the author grew up.

problem.explanation: 목표는 이야기의 중심 갈등을 설명하는 것이다. A는 동업자가 유족에게 방부 처리에 대해 거짓말을 하면서도 정상 요금을 받았다는 사실을 Walter가 알게 되는 사건을 제시하므로 갈등이 드러난다. B는 배경의 출처만 말하고, C는 동업 관계만 소개할 뿐 문제 상황이 없다. D는 출판 연도만 알려 주므로 갈등과 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to describe the story's central conflict. A does this because it presents the problem Walter faces: he finds out that his partner has been lying to grieving families about embalming while still charging them full price. B only tells you where the setting came from. C introduces the partnership but leaves out any problem. D gives only the publication year, so it says nothing about the conflict.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Funeral director learns business partner misrepresenting embalming procedures to grieving families while charging standard service rates

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 완료: 노트의 4·5번 항목(거짓 방부 처리 고지 + 정상 요금 청구)을 결합해 중심 갈등을 정확히 서술한다. B(배경 출처), C(동업 관계 소개), D(출판 연도)는 모두 노트 사실과 일치하지만 '갈등'을 담지 않아 목표 불일치로 배제되며, 전형적 오답 유형(사실은 맞지만 수사적 목표 미충족)이다. 한국어·영어 해설 결론·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움, 한글 혼입 없음. 가상 작가·작품이므로 저작권 문제 없음. 명시적 목표 한 가지로 바로 풀리는 easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: A만 문제 상황(동업자의 기만과 과금)을 제시. 오답은 배경, 인물 관계, 출판 정보로 전형적인 오답 유형이며 한 단계 판단으로 걸러진다. 'full price'는 'standard service rate'를 적절히 바꿔 쓴 표현이다.

problem.passage:
Marisol had worked the night console at Bellweather Cab for eleven years, and she knew the city's streets the way some people know old hymns. When the new routing memo arrived, she read it twice: rides paid with county assistance vouchers were to be sent the long way, over the Calder Bridge and back, while riders paying by credit card got the direct line. Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold, ______ the voucher rides on tonight's board had already been flagged in red.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Marisol had worked the night console at Bellweather Cab for eleven years, and she knew the city's streets the way some people know old hymns. When the new routing memo arrived, she read it twice: rides paid with county assistance vouchers were to be sent the long way, over the Calder Bridge and back, while riders paying by credit card got the direct line. Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold, ______ the voucher rides on tonight's board had already been flagged in red.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the night shift grew quieter as she saw that every one of
Marisol realized that every one of
Marisol's console displayed that every one of
the memo itself showed her that every one of
problem.explanation:
분사구문 'Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold'에서 메모를 스크롤하고 커피가 식어 가던 사람은 Marisol이다. 따라서 콤마 뒤 주절의 주어는 Marisol이어야 한다. 정답은 B이다.
A: 주어 'the night shift'는 수식어와 상관없는 명사다. 야간 근무 시간이 메모를 스크롤할 수는 없다. 뒤에 she가 나오지만 주절 주어가 아니므로 수식 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
C: 'Marisol's console'은 Marisol의 이름이 들어가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 사람이 아니라 사람에게 딸린 기기를 주어로 삼은 경우다. 스크롤하는 것은 콘솔이 아니라 사람이다.
D: 'the memo'는 단수 동사 showed와 수일치가 맞고 문장도 완전하지만, 메모가 스스로를 스크롤할 수는 없다. 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상이다.
problem.explanationEn:
The introductory phrase "Scrolling through the memo a third time as her coffee went cold" describes Marisol, since she is the one scrolling through the memo while her coffee cools. That means the subject of the main clause right after the comma has to be Marisol. The answer is B.
A: The subject, "the night shift," has nothing to do with the modifier, because a work shift can't scroll through a memo. "She" does show up later in the sentence, but it isn't the subject of the main clause, so the modifier still doesn't attach to Marisol.
C: "Marisol's console" looks tempting because it contains her name. But the subject is the console, a device that belongs to her, not Marisol herself. A person scrolls, not a console.
D: "The memo" agrees with "showed," and the sentence is complete. However, the memo can't scroll through itself, so the modifier can't logically describe it.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구문 'Scrolling through the memo...'의 논리적 주어는 Marisol이며, B만이 주절 주어를 Marisol로 둔다. 오답 A/C/D는 모두 단수 주어·완전한 문장이라 수일치로는 가려낼 수 없고, 특히 C의 'Marisol's console'은 소유격으로 이름을 포함시켜 피수식어와의 범주 차이(사람 vs 기기)를 추론해야 하는 함정으로 기능한다. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음. 지문이 서사체로 다소 길지만 SAT 형식 범위 내.

advisory.note: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 Marisol이고, 정답 B가 이와 맞는다. C의 소유격 함정(Marisol's console)과 A의 종속절 속 she 함정은 의미상 주어 추론을 요구한다. 선택지 동사가 모두 과거형이라 수일치로는 정답을 가를 수 없다. 오답 3개 모두 문법적으로 완전한 문장이다.

problem.passage:
Ruth Okafor had measured the Halvorsen lot twice, and both times the developer's planned tower rose nine stories above what the zoning code allowed. She said nothing at the hearing, only watched the five council members raise their hands to grant the variance. Later, scanning the campaign finance filings in her cramped office, she confirmed what she had suspected: the members who had voted to waive the height limit ______ accepted generous contributions from Halvorsen Partners only a week before the vote.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Ruth Okafor had measured the Halvorsen lot twice, and both times the developer's planned tower rose nine stories above what the zoning code allowed. She said nothing at the hearing, only watched the five council members raise their hands to grant the variance. Later, scanning the campaign finance filings in her cramped office, she confirmed what she had suspected: the members who had voted to waive the height limit ______ accepted generous contributions from Halvorsen Partners only a week before the vote.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: had; in fact,
had. In fact,
had, in fact
had, in fact,
problem.explanation: 정답 D. 빈칸 앞의 'the members who had voted to waive the height limit had'는 주어와 조동사만 있고 본동사가 없어서 완전한 절이 아니다. 본동사 'accepted'는 빈칸 뒤에 나온다. 따라서 'in fact'는 두 독립절 사이의 경계가 아니라 한 절 안(조동사와 본동사 사이)에 들어간 삽입어구이므로 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩 짝지어 찍어야 한다. A: 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 세미콜론을 썼다. 세미콜론 앞이 'had'로 끝나는 불완전한 절이라 쓸 수 없다. B: 같은 착각으로 마침표를 찍어 'the members ... had.'라는 문장 조각(fragment)을 만든다. 마침표 뒤를 독립 문장처럼 읽고 싶게 만드는 함정이다. C: 삽입어 앞에만 쉼표가 있고 뒤에는 없어서 쉼표가 비대칭이다. 삽입어구는 양쪽 쉼표로 감싸야 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The answer is D. Look at what comes before the blank: "the members who had voted to waive the height limit had." This has a subject and a helping verb, but its main verb, "accepted," only appears after the blank. So this is not a complete clause. That means "in fact" doesn't sit between two independent clauses. It's an interrupter inside one clause, placed between "had" and "accepted," and it needs a pair of commas around it. A is wrong because it treats the interrupter as a boundary between clauses and uses a semicolon. A semicolon needs a complete clause on each side, and "...had" isn't one. B makes the same mistake with a period, which leaves a fragment ending in "had." C is wrong because it puts a comma before "in fact" but not after it. An interrupter has to be set off with commas on both sides.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산: 'had, in fact, accepted'는 과거완료 조동사 had와 본동사 accepted 사이에 삽입어가 들어간 구조로, 양쪽 쉼표가 맞다. A(세미콜론)·B(마침표)는 'the members ... had'가 불완전하고 뒤쪽 'accepted ...'에 주어가 없어 양쪽 모두 조각이 되므로 오답. C는 비대칭 쉼표. 해설도 이 구조를 정확히 설명한다. 다만 체크리스트 4(콤마 스플라이스 오답)는 없다 — 본 설계상 독립절이 하나뿐이어서 콤마 스플라이스 오답을 만들 수 없는 구조이므로, 이 항목은 미충족이나 문항 자체의 결함은 아니다. hard 적합성: 'had'가 소유동사처럼 완전한 절로 읽히는 함정 위에 조동사-본동사 분리를 인식해야 하므로 inserted_modifier_vs_clause_discrimination 사고가 실제로 요구된다.

advisory.note: 정답 D(had, in fact, accepted)가 맞다. 빈칸 앞이 조동사 had로 끝나 본동사가 없으므로 in fact는 절 경계가 아니라 절 안에 들어간 삽입어다. 오답 A와 B는 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각하게 만드는 함정이고, 관계절 안의 had voted가 주절처럼 보이도록 설계되어 추가 판단이 필요하다. 다만 체크리스트 4번을 충족하지 못한다. 오답 중에 콤마 스플라이스(쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 것) 선택지가 없다. 빈칸 앞에 독립절이 없는 구조라 원리적으로 만들 수 없고, 대신 세미콜론·마침표 오답이 그 역할을 맡고 있다.

problem.passage:
The radiator in the rented room ticked through the night, and the single lamp threw Ilse's shadow across a stack of earlier versions she had inherited from another translator. Her assignment had seemed simple: polish the final English text of a shipping contract. Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath, ______ that every penalty for late delivery had been quietly reduced, always in favor of the same client.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The radiator in the rented room ticked through the night, and the single lamp threw Ilse's shadow across a stack of earlier versions she had inherited from another translator. Her assignment had seemed simple: polish the final English text of a shipping contract. Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath, ______ that every penalty for late delivery had been quietly reduced, always in favor of the same client.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Ilse realized
Ilse's pencil annotations revealed
the radiator's steady ticking made clear
the inherited versions showed
problem.explanation:
정답 A. 문장 앞의 분사구 "Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath"는 조항을 나란히 놓고 소리 내어 읽는 행동을 묘사한다. 그러니 주절의 주어는 그 행동을 실제로 하는 사람, 곧 Ilse여야 한다. 주어를 Ilse로 두면 수식어가 올바르게 연결된다.
B: Ilse의 연필 메모(그녀가 만든 산출물)는 Ilse와 관련은 있지만 사람이 아니라 사물이다. 메모가 조항을 나란히 놓거나 소리 내어 읽을 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다.
C: 라디에이터 소리는 지문에 나오기는 하지만 수식어가 묘사하는 행동과 아무 관계가 없는 명사다.
D: "versions showed"는 주어와 동사의 수가 맞고 문장 형태도 완전하다. 하지만 이 버전들은 비교되는 대상일 뿐, 스스로 비교하고 읽는 주체가 될 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is A. The opening phrase, "Setting each Portuguese clause beside its English counterpart and reading both aloud under her breath," describes things a person does: lining up the clauses and reading them aloud. The subject of the main clause has to be the one doing those things, which is Ilse. "Ilse realized" makes the phrase attach correctly.
B is wrong because Ilse's pencil annotations are something she produced, not Ilse herself. Notes can't set clauses side by side or read aloud, so the modifier dangles.
C is wrong because the radiator's ticking is mentioned in the passage, but it has nothing to do with the action the phrase describes.
D is tempting because "versions showed" agrees in number and forms a complete sentence. But the versions are the things being compared. They can't do the comparing or the reading.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구 "Setting ... and reading both aloud under her breath"의 행위 주체는 사람(Ilse)뿐이며 A만 적합. B는 소유격 함정(Ilse's pencil annotations)으로 Ilse라는 이름이 포함되어 있어 단순 키워드 매칭으로는 걸러낼 수 없고, C·D는 지문에 등장하는 사물 명사로 구성되어 의미적 연결 판단을 요구한다. 네 선택지 모두 과거시제·문법적으로 완전하여 수일치/시제로는 변별 불가. 해설은 각 오답의 탈락 이유를 정확히 서술하며 모순 없음. 지문은 창작 서사로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 Ilse이다. B는 소유격 함정(Ilse's)으로, Ilse와 관련은 있지만 사물이다. C와 D도 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이다. 모든 선택지가 단수/복수 동사와 맞게 짝지어져 있어 수일치만으로는 정답을 가를 수 없다. 의미적 연결을 추론해야 하는 문항이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Last Sort" is a short story by Delphine Arceneaux.
- Its protagonist, Ruth Hadley, is a retired postal worker who sorted mail at the Caddo Junction facility for thirty-two years.
- In one scene, Ruth attends a community meeting where a regional official proposes closing the facility.
- During his slide presentation, the official refers to the facility only as "redundant capacity."
- Throughout the meeting, Ruth remembers the facility through the names on the envelopes she handled there, such as the families who received letters from soldiers overseas.
- At the story's climax, Ruth stands up and recites the facility's delivery routes from memory.

The student wants to highlight the difference between how the person behind the plan and the main character each view the building. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Last Sort" is a short story by Delphine Arceneaux.
- Its protagonist, Ruth Hadley, is a retired postal worker who sorted mail at the Caddo Junction facility for thirty-two years.
- In one scene, Ruth attends a community meeting where a regional official proposes closing the facility.
- During his slide presentation, the official refers to the facility only as "redundant capacity."
- Throughout the meeting, Ruth remembers the facility through the names on the envelopes she handled there, such as the families who received letters from soldiers overseas.
- At the story's climax, Ruth stands up and recites the facility's delivery routes from memory.
problem.question: The student wants to highlight the difference between how the person behind the plan and the main character each view the building. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the official proposes closing the Caddo Junction facility at a community meeting, he presents his plan in a slideshow that calls it "redundant capacity."
Whereas Ruth Hadley sorted mail at the Caddo Junction facility for thirty-two years, at the story's climax she stands and recites its delivery routes from memory.
Whereas the official reduces the Caddo Junction facility to "redundant capacity," Ruth Hadley recalls it through the names of the families whose letters passed through her hands there.
Whereas the official calls the Caddo Junction facility "redundant capacity," Ruth Hadley warns the meeting that closing it would put hundreds of her former coworkers out of work.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 목표는 폐쇄를 제안하는 사람(관리)과 주인공(Ruth)이 시설을 어떻게 보는지 대비하는 것이다. C는 두 개의 서로 다른 사실, 즉 관리가 시설을 "redundant capacity"라고만 부른다는 점과 Ruth가 봉투에 적힌 이름들을 통해 시설을 기억한다는 점을 결합해 비인격적 관점과 개인적 관점을 대비시킨다.
A(한쪽 사실만 담음): 관리 쪽 정보만 있어 Ruth의 관점이 빠져 있다. 'Whereas' 구문을 썼지만 실제로는 대비가 이루어지지 않으므로 목표를 절반만 달성한다.
B(목표와 무관한 결합): 두 사실을 결합했지만 둘 다 Ruth에 관한 것이다(32년 근무, 배달 경로 암송). 관리의 관점이 없어 요구된 대비가 성립하지 않는다.
D(노트에 없는 내용 추가): 대비 구조는 갖췄지만, Ruth가 수백 명의 실직을 경고한다는 내용은 노트에 없다. 노트에서 Ruth는 이름과 기억을 통해 시설을 떠올릴 뿐이므로 사실을 왜곡한 문장이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: Your goal is to contrast how the man proposing the closure (the official) and the protagonist (Ruth) each see the facility. C combines two separate facts from the notes. The official refers to the facility only as "redundant capacity," while Ruth remembers it through the names of the families whose letters she sorted. Putting these together sets an impersonal view against a personal one.
A gives only one side. Every detail is about the official. Even though the sentence uses "Whereas," it never contrasts him with Ruth, so it meets only half the goal.
B combines two facts, but both are about Ruth: her thirty-two years at the facility and her reciting the routes. Without the official's view, the required contrast doesn't happen.
D uses the right contrast structure but adds something the notes never say. Ruth doesn't warn that hundreds of coworkers will lose their jobs. The notes only say she remembers the facility through names, so D misrepresents the story.

hardJudge.note: C는 관리의 비인격적 명명("redundant capacity")과 Ruth의 개인적 기억(봉투의 이름)을 결합해 목표(두 인물의 시설 인식 대비)를 정확히 충족. A는 관리 측 정보만, B는 Ruth 측 정보만(Whereas 구문의 가짜 대비), D는 노트에 없는 '수백 명 실직 경고' 추가. 노트의 Ruth 관련 사실 3개 중 '시설을 어떻게 보는가'를 드러내는 사실(이름 기억)을 골라야 하고, 클라이맥스 사실(경로 암송)을 담은 B가 유인 오답으로 기능해 medium 이상의 목표 범위 판단을 요구. 가상의 작품으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 맞고 해설도 정답과 맞으며 체크리스트 항목도 모두 충족한다. 다만 hard 문항으로 보기에는 어렵다. 전형적인 medium 수준의 비교형 문항이다. A·B는 한쪽 관점만 담고 있고, D에는 노트에 없는 내용이 들어 있어 쉽게 제거된다. 남는 C도 'whereas'에 두 인물의 관점을 대비시킨 형태라 바로 눈에 띈다. 또 같은 '관점' 차원에서 그럴듯한 오답이 없다. 예를 들어 관리의 관점과 Ruth의 경로 암송을 묶은 선택지가 있었다면, 경로 암송 장면이 '어떻게 보는가'를 직접 보여 주는지 따져야 했을 것이다. 그런 선택지가 없어서 hard 특성에서 말하는 정밀한 목적 범위 조정이 실제로 요구되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Tray" is a short story by the writer Lena Marsh, published in 2019.
- Its protagonist, Ruth Okafor, is a dental hygienist at a small suburban practice.
- While laying out scalers and mirrors in a side room, Ruth hears her employer, Dr. Halvorsen, booking healthy patients for root canals and crowns they do not need.

The student wants to introduce the story's central moral dilemma to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

problem.question: The student wants to introduce the story's central moral dilemma to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Lena Marsh's "The Tray," Ruth Okafor counts the scalers and mirrors on her tray again and again in a side room of a small suburban dental practice.
Lena Marsh's 2019 short story "The Tray" follows a dental hygienist named Ruth Okafor and her life at a small suburban practice, told in a prose style that critics have praised.
Lena Marsh's 2019 short story "The Tray" has drawn praise from critics for its spare, clinical prose, which suits its setting in a small suburban dental practice.

In Lena Marsh's 2019 short story "The Tray," dental hygienist Ruth Okafor overhears her employer booking healthy patients for needless procedures and must decide whether to speak up—a choice the story leaves unresolved.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 낯선 독자에게 작품(작가·제목)을 소개하면서 갈등의 핵심, 즉 불필요한 시술 예약을 엿들은 주인공이 신고할지 고민하고 결말이 열려 있다는 점을 담았다.
A: 세부 사항이 지나치다. 도구를 반복해서 세는 행동만 있고, 왜 그러는지(엿들은 비리)가 빠져 있어 딜레마가 드러나지 않는다.
B: 범위가 지나치게 넓다. 작품 전체를 두루 소개하지만 윤리적 갈등이 무엇인지는 말하지 않는다.
C: 엉뚱한 항목을 강조했다. 비평가들이 칭찬한 문체에 초점을 맞춰 딜레마와 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. The goal is to introduce the story's central moral dilemma to readers who don't know the story. D names the work, then lays out the dilemma: Ruth overhears unnecessary procedures being booked and must decide whether to speak up. It also notes that the story leaves her choice unresolved.
A is too narrow. It keeps only one detail, Ruth counting her instruments, and leaves out why she does it, so the dilemma never shows up.
B is too broad. It gives a general overview of the story and its praised prose but never says what the moral conflict is.
C focuses on the wrong note. It's about the critics' view of Marsh's prose style, which has nothing to do with the dilemma.

hardJudge.note: 목표(낯선 독자에게 중심 도덕적 딜레마 소개)가 명확하며, 정답 D는 작가·제목·배경(직업)과 핵심 갈등(엿들은 비리, 신고 여부, 열린 결말)을 여러 노트에서 종합해 하나의 문장으로 통합함. A는 세부 행동만 나열해 지나치게 구체적, B는 윤리적 갈등 없이 작품 전체를 두루뭉술하게 소개해 지나치게 포괄적, C는 문체에 초점을 맞춰 목표와 무관. 해설은 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 허구의 작품·작가라 저작권 문제 없고 노트 내 사실 모순도 없음. 난이도는 단순 복잡성이 아니라 정보 위계 설정(배경 vs 핵심)과 여러 노트의 통합 판단에서 비롯됨.

advisory.note: 정답만 '도덕적 딜레마'를 직접 언급하고(엿들은 비리+신고 여부+미해결 결말), 오답 셋은 딜레마가 아예 빠져 있어 키워드만 맞춰 봐도 바로 고를 수 있다. 전형적인 medium 수준의 소개형 문항이다. 여러 메모를 종합하긴 하지만 정답과 경쟁할 만한 오답이 없어서 범위 조정 판단이 실제로 요구되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Teodora Vance's 2019 novel The Registration Window is set in a small high school in rural Kentucky.
- In the novel's central scene, teacher Ruth Abernathy watches during registration week as counselors tell students who receive free lunches that the AP Chemistry section is "full," then quietly enroll other students in it.
- The novel states that eleven of the twelve students turned away from the course came from low-income families.
- Literary scholar Marcus Hale argues that the scene may be modeled on Vance's years teaching in eastern Kentucky; Vance has neither confirmed nor denied this.
- A 2021 analysis of online reader reviews found that about 60% of reviewers described Ruth as complicit rather than heroic.

The student wants to describe what happens in the scene and present Hale's unverified claim about its origins, giving each the degree of confidence the notes support. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Teodora Vance's 2019 novel The Registration Window is set in a small high school in rural Kentucky.
- In the novel's central scene, teacher Ruth Abernathy watches during registration week as counselors tell students who receive free lunches that the AP Chemistry section is "full," then quietly enroll other students in it.
- The novel states that eleven of the twelve students turned away from the course came from low-income families.
- Literary scholar Marcus Hale argues that the scene may be modeled on Vance's years teaching in eastern Kentucky; Vance has neither confirmed nor denied this.
- A 2021 analysis of online reader reviews found that about 60% of reviewers described Ruth as complicit rather than heroic.
problem.question: The student wants to describe what happens in the scene and present Hale's unverified claim about its origins, giving each the degree of confidence the notes support. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In The Registration Window, counselors falsely tell low-income students that AP Chemistry is full while enrolling others, a scene that scholar Marcus Hale suggests Vance may have based on her own years teaching in eastern Kentucky.

In The Registration Window, counselors falsely tell low-income students that AP Chemistry is full while enrolling others, a scene that scholar Marcus Hale has shown Vance based on her own years teaching in eastern Kentucky.

In The Registration Window, counselors appear possibly to discourage some low-income students from AP Chemistry, a scene that scholar Marcus Hale suggests Vance may have based on her own years teaching in eastern Kentucky.

In The Registration Window, counselors falsely tell low-income students that AP Chemistry is full while enrolling others, a scene that about 60% of reviewers suggest Vance may have based on her own years teaching in eastern Kentucky.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 장면의 사건(상담교사들이 저소득 학생들에게 반이 '찼다'고 말하고 다른 학생은 등록시킴)은 소설 속에서 실제로 일어나는 일이므로 단정적으로 서술해야 한다. 반면 Hale의 자전적 근거 주장은 Vance가 확인하지 않았으므로 'suggests ... may have'처럼 잠정적으로 표현해야 한다. A는 두 가지를 모두 충족한다.
B: 'has shown'은 확인되지 않은 Hale의 추측을 입증된 사실처럼 과장한다.
C: 소설에 분명히 나오는 사건을 'appear possibly to discourage some'으로 불필요하게 약하게 줄여 말해, 확정적 사실을 잠정적인 것으로 축소한다.
D: 확실성 수준은 맞지만, 자전적 근거 주장을 독자 리뷰 분석(60%, 이는 Ruth에 대한 평가에 관한 것)과 혼동해 잘못된 출처를 내세운다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. The events of the scene really happen in the novel: counselors tell low-income students the course is "full" and then enroll other students. So these events should be stated directly. Hale's claim that the scene comes from Vance's own life has not been confirmed by Vance, so it should be framed tentatively ("suggests... may have"). A does both of these things.
Choice B is incorrect because "has shown" turns Hale's unconfirmed guess into a proven fact. That overstates it.
Choice C is incorrect because it weakens events that clearly occur in the novel ("appear possibly to discourage some"). This makes a definite plot fact sound uncertain when it isn't.
Choice D is incorrect because its level of certainty is fine, but it gets the source wrong. It credits the autobiographical claim to the reader-review analysis. That 60% figure is about how reviewers judged Ruth, not about where the scene came from.

hardJudge.note: 노트는 소설 속 사건(확정)과 Hale의 미확인 주장(잠정)을 함께 제시하며, A는 사건을 단정적으로, Hale의 주장을 'suggests ... may have'로 잠정적으로 서술해 목표에 정확히 부합한다. B는 'has shown'으로 확실성 과장, C는 'appear possibly to discourage some'으로 확정 사실을 축소, D는 독자 리뷰 분석(Ruth 평가에 관한 것)을 자전적 근거 주장의 출처로 오귀속한다. 해설은 각 오답의 결함을 정확히 짚고 있으며 수치·논리 모순 없음. 'low-income students'는 '무료급식 대상 학생'과 '12명 중 11명 저소득'이라는 노트 내용을 합리적으로 요약한 표현으로 허용 가능. 가상의 소설·학자이므로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음. 두 정보원의 확실성 수준을 각각 판별하고 출처 혼동 오답까지 걸러내야 하므로 단순 사실 선택형 medium 문항보다 추가 사고를 요구한다.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞고 해설도 일관됩니다. 다만 목표 문장이 "각각에 노트가 뒷받침하는 정도의 확신을 부여하라"고 판별 기준을 직접 알려 줍니다. 그래서 문제를 푸는 일이 B의 'has shown'과 C의 'appear possibly'라는 눈에 띄는 어휘 차이만 확인하는 수준으로 줄어듭니다. D는 출처를 잘못 붙인 것이 뻔해서 오답 매력이 거의 없습니다. 3번 항목(과잉 일반화 오답)은 엄밀한 의미의 과잉 일반화라기보다 확실성을 과장한 것인데(B), 레시피 취지에는 맞는다고 보았습니다. 노트 가운데 장소 정보, 12명 중 11명이라는 수치, 60% 리뷰 분석은 오답 재료로만 쓰였고, 여러 정보를 종합하거나 범위를 판단해야 하는 부담은 없습니다. 전형적인 medium 수준으로 판단합니다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In Mara Ilves's 2019 novel The Verbatim Record, Dorota Wysocki works as a court stenographer for attorney Henryk Lass.
- On the morning of a hearing, Lass submits a written summary to the judge stating that a witness spent the entire evening in question at home.
- That afternoon, Dorota records the same witness testifying that he left his house shortly after nine o'clock that evening.
- Court rules require Dorota to certify that her transcript is accurate word for word.
- The chapter ends with Dorota holding her pen above the certification line without signing.

The student wants to show how the two accounts of the witness's whereabouts set up the dilemma Dorota faces. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In Mara Ilves's 2019 novel The Verbatim Record, Dorota Wysocki works as a court stenographer for attorney Henryk Lass.
- On the morning of a hearing, Lass submits a written summary to the judge stating that a witness spent the entire evening in question at home.
- That afternoon, Dorota records the same witness testifying that he left his house shortly after nine o'clock that evening.
- Court rules require Dorota to certify that her transcript is accurate word for word.
- The chapter ends with Dorota holding her pen above the certification line without signing.
problem.question: The student wants to show how the two accounts of the witness's whereabouts set up the dilemma Dorota faces. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Mara Ilves's The Verbatim Record, stenographer Dorota Wysocki records a witness testifying that he left his house shortly after nine o'clock, and she must certify her transcript word for word.

In Mara Ilves's The Verbatim Record, stenographer Dorota Wysocki's employer tells the judge in a morning summary that a witness stayed home all evening, yet that afternoon she must transcribe the witness saying he went out shortly after nine.
In Mara Ilves's The Verbatim Record, stenographer Dorota Wysocki works for attorney Henryk Lass, and the chapter ends with her holding her pen above the certification line without signing.

In Mara Ilves's The Verbatim Record, stenographer Dorota Wysocki's employer knowingly lies to the judge that a witness stayed home all evening, so that afternoon she alters her transcript to hide the witness saying he went out after nine.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 오전에 고용주 Lass가 판사에게 낸 요약서(증인이 저녁 내내 집에 있었다)와 오후 증언(9시 직후 집을 나갔다)을 함께 담아 두 진술이 서로 모순된다는 점을 보여 준다. 그래서 고용주의 진술과 반대되는 내용을 기록해야 하는 Dorota의 딜레마가 드러난다.
A: 증언과 축자 인증 의무는 담았지만 Lass의 요약서가 빠져 있어서 무엇과 모순되는지가 드러나지 않는다. 목표를 절반만 달성한 문장이다.
C: 고용 관계와 서명을 망설이는 장면이라는 두 사실을 결합했지만, 두 진술 중 어느 것도 언급하지 않아 목표와 무관하다.
D: '고의로 거짓말했다'와 '기록을 변조했다'는 노트에 없는 내용이다. 노트에 따르면 Dorota는 아직 서명하지 않았을 뿐이므로 사실을 왜곡한 문장이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: This choice combines both accounts. In the morning, Lass's written summary tells the judge the witness stayed home all evening. In the afternoon, the witness testifies that he left shortly after nine. Putting these side by side shows the contradiction, which explains why Dorota faces a dilemma: she must record testimony that goes against her employer's summary.
A: This choice includes the testimony and the word-for-word rule but leaves out Lass's summary. Without it, the reader can't tell what the testimony contradicts, so the choice meets only half the goal.
C: This choice combines two facts from the notes, but they are the wrong ones: Dorota's job and her hesitation to sign. It never mentions either account of the witness's whereabouts.
D: The notes never say Lass lied on purpose or that Dorota changed her transcript. They only say she hasn't signed yet. This choice adds details that aren't in the notes and changes the facts.

hardJudge.note: B만이 오전 요약서(집에 있었다)와 오후 증언(9시 직후 외출)을 'yet'으로 대비시켜 두 진술의 모순과 기록 의무를 함께 담아 목표를 충족한다. A는 증언만(한쪽 사실), C는 진술을 전혀 언급하지 않음, D는 '고의로 거짓말'·'기록 변조' 등 노트에 없는 과잉 추론을 포함. 가상의 소설이라 저작권·사실 오류 문제 없음. 두 노트를 대비 관계로 통합하고 D의 과잉 일반화를 걸러내야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: B가 서로 모순되는 두 진술을 모두 담고 'yet'으로 대립 관계를 드러낸다. 그래서 목표에 맞는다. A는 인증 의무를 담고 있어 그럴듯하지만 진술이 하나만 들어 있다. D는 노트에 없는 고의성과 변조를 추론해 넣었다. B는 인증 의무를 명시하지 않았지만 '두 진술이 딜레마를 만든다'는 목표에는 충분하다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Ledger of the Marisol" is a 2019 short story by the fictional author Teodora Varga.
- Its protagonist, Ilse Brand, is a diver for a marine salvage company working the wreck of a cargo ship off the Azores.
- Ilse's dive log records that she brought up six crates of antique ship chronometers.
- The official wreck inventory her company files with the port authority lists no chronometers.
- Late one night, Ilse finds the same six crates entered, at high valuations, in a private ledger kept in her supervisor's office.
- The story ends with Ilse deciding whether to report the discrepancy.

The student wants to emphasize the discovery that sets the story's central conflict in motion. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Ledger of the Marisol" is a 2019 short story by the fictional author Teodora Varga.
- Its protagonist, Ilse Brand, is a diver for a marine salvage company working the wreck of a cargo ship off the Azores.
- Ilse's dive log records that she brought up six crates of antique ship chronometers.
- The official wreck inventory her company files with the port authority lists no chronometers.
- Late one night, Ilse finds the same six crates entered, at high valuations, in a private ledger kept in her supervisor's office.
- The story ends with Ilse deciding whether to report the discrepancy.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize the discovery that sets the story's central conflict in motion. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Teodora Varga's story, Ilse Brand's dive log records that she brought up six crates of antique ship chronometers from a cargo ship wrecked off the Azores.
In Teodora Varga's story, Ilse Brand, a salvage diver working a wreck off the Azores, recovers cargo, compares records, and ultimately must decide whether to report what she has learned.

In Teodora Varga's story, Ilse Brand finds that six crates of chronometers she recovered, absent from her company's official wreck inventory, appear at high valuations in her supervisor's private ledger.
In Teodora Varga's story, Ilse Brand faces a choice at the end: whether to report a discrepancy she has noticed in her salvage company's records.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 갈등을 일으키는 발견은 하나의 대비입니다. 공식 재고 목록에는 빠진 크레이트가 사적 장부에는 기록되어 있다는 점입니다. C는 공식 목록에 없다는 사실과 사적 장부에 있다는 사실을 모두 담아 그 발견 자체를 강조합니다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 다이빙 일지의 회수 기록만 담았습니다. 공식 목록 누락과 사적 장부 기재라는 대비가 없으므로 어떤 발견인지 드러나지 않습니다.
B(지나치게 포괄적): 이야기 전체 흐름을 요약할 뿐, 발견의 구체적 내용이 빠져 초점이 흐려졌습니다.
D(다른 항목 강조): 결말의 선택을 강조합니다. 이는 발견이 낳은 결과일 뿐, 갈등을 촉발한 발견 자체가 아닙니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: The discovery that starts the conflict is a contrast. The crates are missing from the official inventory but recorded in a private ledger. C includes both facts, the absence from the official inventory and the listing in the supervisor's ledger, so it puts the discovery itself in focus.
A is too detailed. It only says what Ilse's dive log shows. It leaves out the missing inventory entry and the private ledger, so the discovery never appears.
B is too broad. It summarizes the whole plot and never says what Ilse actually finds, so the choice loses its focus.
D highlights a different note, the story's ending. Ilse's final choice is a result of the discovery, not the discovery that sets the conflict in motion.

hardJudge.note: 목표(갈등을 촉발한 '발견' 강조)가 명확하며, 정답 C는 다이빙 일지·공식 재고 누락·사적 장부 기재라는 세 노트를 하나의 대비로 종합해야만 도출된다. A는 회수 사실만(과도 구체), B는 전체 줄거리 개관(과도 포괄), D는 발견의 결과인 결말 선택을 강조하는 초점 이탈 오답으로 역할 분담이 분명하다. 작가·작품이 허구로 명시되어 저작권·사실 오류 문제 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 배제 근거를 모순 없이 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 '공식 목록에 없음'과 '사적 장부에 있음'이라는 세 메모를 합쳐 발견 자체를 드러낸다. A는 지나치게 구체적이고 B는 지나치게 포괄적이다. D는 결말(결과)에 초점을 둔 그럴듯한 오답이다. 다만 'discovery'라는 단어가 C의 'finds'와 바로 이어져 단서가 다소 노출된다.

problem.passage:
In three weeks of meetings, not one of the department chairs mentioned Dr. Okafor's article by name; when Mara raised it herself, Professor Hale only smiled and asked about the weather in her hometown. Yet each meeting, however it began, drifted toward the same topic: the "outdated holdings" crowding the third-floor stacks, beginning, as it happened, with the very journal volume in which Okafor had challenged the chairs' grant-funded laboratory. ______ Mara understood that the chairs' careful silence about the article was not indifference but the request itself, phrased so that no one could ever be said to have made it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In three weeks of meetings, not one of the department chairs mentioned Dr. Okafor's article by name; when Mara raised it herself, Professor Hale only smiled and asked about the weather in her hometown. Yet each meeting, however it began, drifted toward the same topic: the "outdated holdings" crowding the third-floor stacks, beginning, as it happened, with the very journal volume in which Okafor had challenged the chairs' grant-funded laboratory. ______ Mara understood that the chairs' careful silence about the article was not indifference but the request itself, phrased so that no one could ever be said to have made it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Taken together,
Even so,
Indeed,
Meanwhile,
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 지문에는 상반돼 보이는 두 관찰이 나온다. (1) 학과장들은 논문을 한 번도 직접 언급하지 않는다. (2) 그런데도 대화는 늘 그 논문이 실린 학술지 권호를 '낡은 소장 자료'로 치우는 이야기로 흘러간다. 마지막 문장은 이 두 관찰을 함께 놓고 내린 결론이다. 침묵 자체가 압력이었다는 것이다. 따라서 두 관찰을 종합하는 'Taken together,'가 가장 논리적이다.
B 'Even so,': 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 오답이다. 결론은 두 번째 관찰을 뒤집지 않고 오히려 그것에 기대고 있으므로 양보·대조 관계가 아니다.
C 'Indeed,': 바로 앞 문장(대화가 해당 권호로 흘러감)만 강조·심화하는 전환어로, 한쪽 관찰만 반영한다. 결론의 핵심은 첫 번째 관찰인 '침묵'에 있으며, 결론은 두 관찰을 합쳐야 나온다.
D 'Meanwhile,': 동시에 일어난 다른 사건을 잇는 시간 전환어다. 마지막 문장은 별개의 사건이 아니라 앞 내용에서 끌어낸 깨달음이므로 종합 결론과 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. The passage gives two observations that seem to point in opposite directions. First, the chairs never mention Okafor's article. Second, every meeting still drifts toward clearing out the very volume that contains it. The final sentence draws a conclusion that needs both facts: the silence itself was the pressure. "Taken together," signals that kind of combined conclusion.
B ("Even so,") treats the two observations as a simple contrast. But the conclusion doesn't push back against the previous sentence. It builds on it.
C ("Indeed,") only reinforces the sentence right before it, so it reflects one observation. The conclusion depends just as much on the chairs' silence from the first sentence.
D ("Meanwhile,") marks something happening at the same time. Mara's realization isn't a separate event. It's an inference drawn from what came before.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 (1) 논문을 직접 언급하지 않는 침묵과 (2) 그럼에도 대화가 늘 해당 학술지 권호의 폐기로 흘러가는 관찰을 'Yet'으로 대립시키고, 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 합쳐 '침묵 자체가 요청'이라는 함축적 결론을 끌어낸다. 'Taken together,'가 유일하게 종합 결론을 표시하며, 'Even so'는 결론이 앞 내용을 뒤집지 않으므로 부적합, 'Indeed'는 직전 문장만 강조해 새로운 추론 도입에 부적합, 'Meanwhile'은 시간적 병렬이라 부적합. 해설은 각 오답의 결함을 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음. 허구적 인물·상황으로 저작권 우려 없음. 난이도는 길이가 아니라 두 상반 관찰의 종합과 '침묵=요청'이라는 추상적 관계 파악에서 온다.

advisory.note: 두 관찰은 '언급하지 않는 침묵'과 '그 논문이 실린 권호를 치우자는 대화로 흘러감'이다. 마지막 문장은 둘을 합쳐서 침묵 자체가 요청이었다는 함축적 결론을 끌어낸다. 그래서 'Taken together'만 맞다. 'Even so'는 표면적인 대조에 끌리게 만드는 매력적 오답이다. 'Indeed'는 바로 앞 문장만 강조하는 오답이다. 'Meanwhile'는 시간 관계라서 맞지 않는다. 정답은 하나로 정해지고, 해설도 정답과 일치한다.

problem.passage:
Marguerite had stood in the queue long enough to watch a dozen tickets change hands. The clerk was slow, and twice he miscounted the change for an elderly farmer, apologizing each time with a flustered smile. Yet when a German couple and, later, two Canadian students reached the window, he quoted fares nearly double those on the posted board, while every local traveler paid exactly the printed price. ______ the inflated fares were no slip of a tired hand: the clerk was choosing whom to cheat.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Marguerite had stood in the queue long enough to watch a dozen tickets change hands. The clerk was slow, and twice he miscounted the change for an elderly farmer, apologizing each time with a flustered smile. Yet when a German couple and, later, two Canadian students reached the window, he quoted fares nearly double those on the posted board, while every local traveler paid exactly the printed price. ______ the inflated fares were no slip of a tired hand: the clerk was choosing whom to cheat.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
Nevertheless,
Evidently,
Meanwhile,
problem.explanation:
정답 C(Evidently): 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 관찰(외국인 승객에게만 두 배 요금을 부르고 현지인은 정가)을 근거로 Marguerite가 내리는 결론이다. 강조점은 결과(비싼 요금) 자체가 아니라 '고의성'이며, '관찰한 증거로 보아 분명히'라는 추론을 나타내는 Evidently가 이 흐름에 맞다.
A(Similarly): 농부에게 거스름돈을 잘못 계산한 실수와 이어 보면 그럴듯해 보인다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 비싼 요금이 실수와 '같은 종류'가 아니라 일부러 한 일이라고 말하므로, 둘을 비슷한 것으로 묶는 전환어는 핵심 강조점과 어긋난다.
B(Nevertheless): 서툰 실수와 고의적 사기 사이에 대비가 있는 것은 맞다. 그러나 바로 앞 문장은 결론을 뒷받침하는 증거이지 결론과 반대되는 내용이 아니므로, 대조를 나타내는 접속어는 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다.
D(Meanwhile): 같은 시간에 일어난 다른 장면을 잇는 말이다. 마지막 문장은 새로운 사건이 아니라 앞 관찰에서 이끌어낸 판단이므로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
C (Evidently) is correct. The last sentence is a conclusion Marguerite draws from what she has just seen: foreign travelers are quoted double fares, while every local pays the printed price. The point isn't the high fares themselves but the clerk's intent. "Evidently" signals "judging from this evidence, it is clear that," so it fits.
A (Similarly) is tempting because it seems to connect back to the miscounted change for the farmer. But the final sentence says the overcharges are NOT honest slips like that one. Grouping the two as similar goes against the passage's main point.
B (Nevertheless) picks up on a real contrast between clumsy mistakes and deliberate cheating. However, the sentence right before the blank is evidence that supports the conclusion, not something that works against it. A contrast transition gets the relationship wrong.
D (Meanwhile) introduces a separate event happening at the same time. The final sentence isn't a new event. It's a judgment drawn from the earlier observations.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 '서툰 실수(거스름돈 오계산)'와 '외국인에게만 선택적 바가지'라는 두 정보를 제시하고, 마지막 문장은 후자를 근거로 고의성을 추론하는 결론이므로 Evidently가 유일하게 적합. A는 부수적 사실(실수)에 끌리는 오답, B는 앞 문장의 'Yet'에 끌려 대조로 오인하게 하는 방향 오류 오답, D는 시간적 병렬 오답으로 레시피 구조를 충족. 'no slip of a tired hand'가 앞의 실수 서술을 명시적으로 배제하는 구조를 읽어내야 하므로 정보 선별과 증거→결론 추론이 실제로 요구됨. 해설도 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 서툰 실수(거스름돈)와 외국인에게만 선택적으로 부풀린 요금이라는 두 관찰을 종합해야 고의성이라는 결론에 이르고, 그 결론에 맞는 Evidently를 고를 수 있다. Similarly는 부수적 사실인 실수와 이어지는 함정, Nevertheless는 논리 방향이 틀린 대조어다. 앞 문장의 Yet 때문에 대조어가 그럴듯해 보이는 점도 변별력을 높인다.

problem.passage:
When Teodor spotted Ines across the main gallery of the provincial museum on opening night, he crossed the room at once, kissed her on both cheeks, and asked warmly about her daughter, her new teaching post, even her elderly cat. Yet in twenty minutes of conversation he never once mentioned the river-sediment survey the two of them had worked on for four years before he left it unfinished. Whenever the talk drifted toward hydrology, he turned to admire a case of bronze brooches. ______ Ines understood that his warmth was no sign that he had forgotten the survey but a carefully built fence around it: the more attentive he was to everything else, the more clearly the abandoned project stood at the center of the evening, untouched.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When Teodor spotted Ines across the main gallery of the provincial museum on opening night, he crossed the room at once, kissed her on both cheeks, and asked warmly about her daughter, her new teaching post, even her elderly cat. Yet in twenty minutes of conversation he never once mentioned the river-sediment survey the two of them had worked on for four years before he left it unfinished. Whenever the talk drifted toward hydrology, he turned to admire a case of bronze brooches. ______ Ines understood that his warmth was no sign that he had forgotten the survey but a carefully built fence around it: the more attentive he was to everything else, the more clearly the abandoned project stood at the center of the evening, untouched.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: For instance,
Indeed,
Nevertheless,
Thus,
problem.explanation:
정답 D(Thus,): 지문에는 겉보기에 서로 맞지 않는 두 관찰이 나온다. 하나는 테오도르가 이네스의 사생활까지 살갑게 챙긴다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 두 사람의 공동 연구 이야기만은 끝까지 피한다는 점이다. 마지막 문장은 이 두 관찰을 함께 놓고 이끌어 낸 결론이다. 따뜻함 자체가 연구를 둘러친 '울타리'라는 것이다. 따라서 앞의 내용에서 결론을 도출하는 Thus가 알맞다.
A(For instance,): 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 구체적인 예가 아니라 해석이자 결론이므로 종합 결론과 관계없는 전환어다.
B(Indeed,): 회피라는 한쪽 관찰만 보고 '실제로 더 피했다'는 강조로 읽은 경우다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 회피를 강조하는 데서 그치지 않고, 따뜻함과 회피를 하나로 엮어 해석한다.
C(Nevertheless,): 따뜻함과 회피가 서로 반대라는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 경우다. 이네스의 깨달음은 두 관찰에도 '불구하고' 생긴 것이 아니라 두 관찰 '때문에' 생긴 것이다.
problem.explanationEn:
The correct answer is D, "Thus." The passage gives two observations that seem to pull against each other. First, Teodor is very warm and asks about every part of Ines's life. Second, he carefully avoids their abandoned survey. The last sentence is a conclusion Ines draws from both observations together: his warmth is itself a fence around the project. "Thus" signals a conclusion that follows from what came before, so it fits.
A, "For instance," doesn't work because the final sentence isn't an example of the previous sentence. It's an interpretation.
B, "Indeed," only picks up the avoidance. It reads the last sentence as simply stressing that Teodor avoided the topic, but the sentence actually ties his warmth and his avoidance into one insight.
C, "Nevertheless," treats the two observations as a plain contrast. Ines doesn't reach her conclusion in spite of what she saw. She reaches it because of what she saw.

hardJudge.note: 따뜻함(관찰1)과 공동 연구 회피(관찰2)가 'Yet'으로 대립 제시되고, 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 '울타리' 비유로 종합한 결론이므로 Thus가 유일하게 타당. Indeed는 회피 강조만, Nevertheless는 표면 대조만 반영해 오답으로 기능. 해설의 각 오답 분석도 논리적으로 정확. 서사형 지문·결론 추론 구조가 전형적 medium(단순 인과/대조 연결)보다 추가 사고를 요구함.

advisory.note: 따뜻함과 회피라는 겉보기 대립을 '울타리'라는 해석으로 묶어야 Thus를 고를 수 있다. 표면적인 대조에 끌리면 Nevertheless라는 함정에 빠진다. Indeed는 회피에 대한 강조로 읽힐 여지가 조금 있지만, 마지막 문장은 결론을 내리는 성격이 분명해서 Thus가 가장 낫다.

problem.passage:
Every evening, Tomas opened his logbook and wrote down what he had seen from the lamp room. For the third time that week, the gray freighter had steamed straight into the shallow channel. The warning signs on the northern rocks ______ clearly that ships must stay out, yet the vessel never slowed. Tomas pressed his pen hard into the page and recorded the time: 6:42 p.m.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every evening, Tomas opened his logbook and wrote down what he had seen from the lamp room. For the third time that week, the gray freighter had steamed straight into the shallow channel. The warning signs on the northern rocks ______ clearly that ships must stay out, yet the vessel never slowed. Tomas pressed his pen hard into the page and recorded the time: 6:42 p.m.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: states
state
is stating
has stated
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'signs'이고, 'on the northern rocks'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사도 복수형이어야 하므로 B의 'state'가 정답이다. A의 'states'는 단수 동사라서 복수 주어와 맞지 않는다. C의 'is stating'과 D의 'has stated'도 단수 조동사(is, has)를 쓰므로 수 일치 규칙에 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "signs"; the phrase "on the northern rocks" just describes those signs. A plural subject needs a plural verb, so B, "state," is correct. A, "states," is a singular verb, so it doesn't agree with "signs." C, "is stating," and D, "has stated," also use singular helping verbs ("is" and "has"), so they break subject-verb agreement too.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A lighthouse keeper documents a shipping company vessel repeatedly entering restricted waters despite posted warning signs in his logbook

hardJudge.note: 주어 'signs'(복수) + 수식어 'on the northern rocks'(단수 'rocks'는 복수이나 근접 명사 혼동 유도) 구조로, 복수 동사 'state'만 수 일치에 맞음. A/C/D는 모두 단수형이라 규칙 하나로 배제됨. 해설 한·영 모두 정답·선택지 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 지문이 과거 시제 서사이나 표지판 내용은 현재에도 유효한 사실이므로 현재형 'state'가 허용되며, 선택지 중 과거형이 없어 정답 유일성에 문제 없음(다만 'stated'가 더 자연스러울 수 있다는 점은 참고). 난이도 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 signs와 동사의 수 일치를 묻는 문항이다. 전치사구 on the northern rocks가 rocks라는 복수 명사로 끝나서, 단수 오답이 함정으로 강하게 작동하지 않는다. 다만 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있으므로 easy 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Ines Varga, a cartographer, has just received the printed edition of her atlas of the river provinces.

Ines turned to plate fourteen and stopped. The border between Halden and the eastern marshes no longer followed the old riverbed she had traced from the 1841 survey; it now bent west, swallowing three villages. She had not drawn that line. Her editor, Mr. Corbin, insisted over the telephone that the change was a "routine correction" made by the engraver to match a newer government chart. But Ines suspected otherwise: she believed the publisher had moved the line deliberately, without ever looking at her survey notes, to suit the atlas's buyers in Halden.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ines's suspicion about the altered border?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Ines Varga, a cartographer, has just received the printed edition of her atlas of the river provinces.

Ines turned to plate fourteen and stopped. The border between Halden and the eastern marshes no longer followed the old riverbed she had traced from the 1841 survey; it now bent west, swallowing three villages. She had not drawn that line. Her editor, Mr. Corbin, insisted over the telephone that the change was a "routine correction" made by the engraver to match a newer government chart. But Ines suspected otherwise: she believed the publisher had moved the line deliberately, without ever looking at her survey notes, to suit the atlas's buyers in Halden.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ines's suspicion about the altered border?
options: The engraver who prepared plate fourteen had worked for the publisher for many years and had altered plates in earlier atlases at the editor's request.
A newer government chart of the region exists, and on it the border between Halden and the eastern marshes follows a course slightly different from the 1841 survey.
Ines's survey notes, including her tracings of the 1841 riverbed, were stored in the publisher's archive throughout the period when plate fourteen was being engraved.

The publisher's records show that Ines's survey notes were never removed from their sealed archive box, and a letter from Mr. Corbin to a Halden bookseller promises that the new edition will "show Halden as its readers expect."
problem.explanation: 이네스의 의심은 두 부분으로 이루어진다. 출판사가 그녀의 조사 노트를 보지 않았다는 것, 그리고 할든 구매자들에게 맞추려고 국경선을 의도적으로 옮겼다는 것이다. D는 노트가 봉인된 상자에서 한 번도 꺼내지지 않았다는 기록과 할든 독자의 기대에 맞추겠다는 편지를 함께 제시하므로 두 부분을 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 판각공이 예전에도 판을 수정한 적이 있다는 것만 보여 줄 뿐, 이번 수정의 동기나 노트를 보지 않았다는 점은 입증하지 못한다. B는 오히려 코빈의 '통상적 정정' 해명을 지지하며, C는 노트가 출판사 안에 있었다는 사실만 말할 뿐 실제로 참고했는지는 알려 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Ines's suspicion has two parts: the publisher never looked at her survey notes, and it moved the line on purpose to please buyers in Halden. Choice D supports both parts directly, since the notes were never taken out of their sealed box and Corbin's letter promises to show Halden "as its readers expect." Choice A only tells you the engraver had changed plates before; it shows neither the motive for this change nor that her notes were ignored. Choice B actually backs Corbin's claim that the edit was a "routine correction" based on a newer chart. Choice C only says the notes were at the publisher's office, which doesn't tell you whether anyone ignored them or consulted them.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A cartographer discovers her publisher altered territorial boundary lines on maps without consulting her original source materials or permission

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 의심의 두 요소(노트 미열람 + 할든 구매자 영합 동기)를 모두 직접 뒷받침하며 검산 결과 타당. A(과거 수정 전력)·C(노트의 소재)는 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하고, B는 코빈의 해명을 지지하는 역방향 오답으로 말이 됨. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 다만 D가 다른 선택지보다 눈에 띄게 길고 두 증거를 결합해 다소 두드러지는 점은 경미한 약점이나 medium 난이도 범위 내.

advisory.note: 의심의 두 요소(노트를 보지 않음 + 할든 구매자를 위한 의도적 변경)를 D만 모두 충족한다. A(동기 일부)와 C(노트 관련 일부)가 부분 근거 오답으로 기능하고, B는 반대 증거로 말이 된다. 다만 D가 눈에 띄게 길고 두 요소를 모두 담고 있어 정답 단서가 될 위험이 있다.

problem.passage:
In Delia Harrow's novel The Sorting Room, Wilma Ostrander, a retired postal clerk, attends a county meeting about a plan to close the rural mail sorting facility in Fenwick Hollow, where she worked for thirty-two years. Wilma sits in the back row and says little while officials present charts on cost savings. Some readers see her silent anger as grief for her own working life. Literary scholar Tomas Reyes argues instead that Wilma's opposition is mainly about the town, not about herself: she believes the facility's workers kept track of neighbors' needs in ways that no regional center could.

Which finding about the novel, if true, would most directly support Reyes's interpretation?
problem.stimulus: In Delia Harrow's novel The Sorting Room, Wilma Ostrander, a retired postal clerk, attends a county meeting about a plan to close the rural mail sorting facility in Fenwick Hollow, where she worked for thirty-two years. Wilma sits in the back row and says little while officials present charts on cost savings. Some readers see her silent anger as grief for her own working life. Literary scholar Tomas Reyes argues instead that Wilma's opposition is mainly about the town, not about herself: she believes the facility's workers kept track of neighbors' needs in ways that no regional center could.
problem.question: Which finding about the novel, if true, would most directly support Reyes's interpretation?
options: In a later scene, Wilma tells an official that the Fenwick clerks always knew which elderly residents had stopped collecting their letters and would send someone to check on them.
In a later scene, Wilma takes her old facility badge from a kitchen drawer after the meeting and holds it for a long time without speaking.
In a later scene, Wilma tells the officials that she gave thirty-two years to the facility and deserves more respect than a chart of numbers.
In a later scene, several Fenwick residents complain to Wilma that their packages will take longer to arrive once mail is sorted elsewhere.
problem.explanation: Reyes는 Wilma의 반대가 자신의 과거에 대한 슬픔보다는 시설 직원들이 이웃의 필요를 살폈다는 공동체적 이유에서 나온다고 본다. A는 Wilma가 직원들이 편지를 찾아가지 않는 노인을 알아채고 사람을 보내 확인했다고 말하는 장면이므로, 그녀의 관심이 마을 사람들의 안녕에 있음을 직접 보여 준다. B는 지난 직장 생활에 대한 개인적 그리움을 보여 주므로 오히려 Reyes가 반박하는 해석에 가깝다. C도 Wilma가 반대 의견을 말하기는 하지만 그 근거가 자신의 근속 기간과 존중받고 싶은 마음이라 개인적 동기를 드러낸다. D는 공동체가 입는 피해를 다루지만 불만을 말하는 사람이 다른 주민들이고 내용도 배송 속도뿐이어서 Wilma 자신의 동기나 이웃을 살피는 일에 대해서는 보여 주는 것이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Reyes claims that Wilma opposes the closure mainly because of what the town would lose, since the facility's workers kept track of neighbors' needs, and not because she is grieving her own career. Choice A shows Wilma pointing out that the clerks noticed when elderly residents stopped collecting their letters and sent someone to check on them, so it shows directly that her concern is for the community. Choice B shows private nostalgia for her working life, which fits the reading Reyes rejects. In choice C, Wilma does speak against the plan, but her reason is her own years of service and her wish for respect, so her motive is personal. Choice D is about harm to the town, but the complaint comes from other residents and only concerns delivery speed, so it tells you nothing about Wilma's motive or about neighbors looking out for one another.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A retired postal worker attends a community meeting proposing closure of the rural mail sorting facility where she worked thirty-two years

hardJudge.note: Reyes의 주장(마을 중심 동기 + 직원들이 이웃의 필요를 살핌)을 A가 두 요소 모두 직접 충족한다. B·C는 개인적 동기(반박 대상 해석)를 보여 주는 그럴듯한 오답이고, D는 공동체 피해를 다루지만 화자가 Wilma가 아니고 '이웃 살핌'과 무관해 비교 후 배제된다. 한·영 해설 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상의 작품·작가로 저작권 문제 없음. 두 단계 판단(동기 귀속 + 주장 내용 확인)이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 가상의 작품이다. A는 Reyes의 두 요소(마을, 이웃의 필요를 살핌)와 정확히 맞는다. B와 C는 개인적 동기라서 반대 해석을 뒷받침한다. D는 마을이 입는 피해라는 점에서 부분적으로 그럴듯하지만, 다른 주민들의 불만이라 Wilma의 동기를 보여 주지 못한다. 오답 중 그럴듯한 것은 C(반대 의견을 말함)와 D(공동체 피해)이며, 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Ilse Varga, a bookbinder, has just learned that her apprentice, Tomas, has been secretly selling her volumes to a rival shop across the river.

The books lay on the rival's counter in a neat stack, and Ilse knew them at once: her goatskin, her marbled endpapers. But the spines were bare of lettering, the headbands were missing, and on one the boards still showed pencil marks where she had meant to tool a border. "He let you have them like this," she said. The rival shrugged. "Cheaply, too." Ilse ran her thumb along an untrimmed edge and said nothing more.

A literary critic argues that Ilse is troubled less by the money she has lost than by the idea that work she had not finished is now out in the world, representing her craft.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?

A literary critic argues that Ilse is troubled less by the money she has lost than by the idea that work she had not finished is now out in the world, representing her craft.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Ilse sits up all night going through her ledger, adding up the sum she would have earned had the volumes been sold at her usual price.
Later in the story, Tomas gives Ilse every coin he received from the rival, but she will not speak to him until the volumes are bought back and completed at her bench.
