problem.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 일세가 잃은 돈보다 미완성 작품이 자신의 솜씨를 대표하게 된 점에 더 괴로워한다는 것이다. B에서는 돈을 모두 돌려받았는데도 책이 회수되어 완성될 때까지 화가 풀리지 않으므로, 돈이 아니라 미완성 상태가 핵심 문제임을 보여 준다. A는 일세가 잃은 수입에 매달리는 모습이므로 오히려 주장을 약화한다. C는 책의 품질에 대한 손님들의 반응일 뿐 일세의 감정을 드러내지 않는다. D는 도제 시절의 비슷한 잘못을 떠올리는 장면으로, 그녀가 무엇 때문에 괴로워하는지와는 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic claims Ilse cares less about the lost money than about her unfinished work standing for her craft in public. In B, Ilse gets all the money back and is still angry until the books are recovered and finished, which shows that the unfinished state, not the income, is what bothers her. A shows her focused on lost earnings, so it would actually weaken the claim. C describes how customers react to the books' materials and tells you nothing about Ilse's feelings. D brings up a similar mistake from her past, but it doesn't show what is troubling her now.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A bookbinder discovers her apprentice secretly selling unfinished leather-bound volumes to a competitor at discounted rates behind her back

hardJudge.note: B isolates the critic's contrast (money returned, anger persists until volumes are completed), directly supporting the claim. A weakens, C echoes passage details but addresses customers not Ilse, D is a plausible but irrelevant parallel. Korean and English explanations align on letters and reasoning. Original passage, no copyright concern. Requires linking the 'less X than Y' claim with a finding that controls for X—appropriate medium difficulty.

advisory.note: B는 비평가 주장의 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다. 돈을 전부 돌려받았는데도 화가 풀리지 않으므로 돈 문제가 아님을 보여 주고, 책을 되사서 완성해야 한다고 고집하므로 미완성 작품이 문제임을 보여 준다. 오답도 각각 그럴듯한 근거가 있다. A는 돈을 다루고(오히려 주장을 약화함), C는 작품이 솜씨를 대표한다는 점과 닿아 있고(하지만 일세의 감정은 드러나지 않음), D는 도제라는 소재와 연결된다. 그래서 medium 난이도에 맞다. 다만 A는 주장과 정반대라서 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Inés Varga, a meteorologist, has just presented flood-risk projections to a city planning board.

Inés clicked to the final map, where the riverside parcels glowed red, and waited. No one asked about the hundred-year floodplain or the storm-surge models she had spent the winter refining. The chair thanked her warmly, the way one thanks a child for a recital, and moved to the vote. Seven hands rose to approve the Harbor Commons towers. Driving home, Inés replayed the meeting. The board members had not looked confused or skeptical while she spoke; they had not looked at the screen at all. She began to suspect that her presentation had never been part of the decision—that the outcome had been fixed before she ever walked into the room.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Inés's suspicion?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Inés Varga, a meteorologist, has just presented flood-risk projections to a city planning board.

Inés clicked to the final map, where the riverside parcels glowed red, and waited. No one asked about the hundred-year floodplain or the storm-surge models she had spent the winter refining. The chair thanked her warmly, the way one thanks a child for a recital, and moved to the vote. Seven hands rose to approve the Harbor Commons towers. Driving home, Inés replayed the meeting. The board members had not looked confused or skeptical while she spoke; they had not looked at the screen at all. She began to suspect that her presentation had never been part of the decision—that the outcome had been fixed before she ever walked into the room.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Inés's suspicion?
options: The board's internal notes showed that several members privately agreed that the riverside parcels faced serious flood risk.
The board's financial records showed that the developer of Harbor Commons had contributed to the campaigns of most board members.
The board's approval paperwork showed that every member's endorsement of Harbor Commons had been recorded three days before the meeting.
The board's archives showed that members had approved projects in other flood-prone areas despite earlier warnings from consultants.
problem.explanation: 이네스의 의심은 회의 전에 이미 결과가 정해져 있었다는 것, 즉 시점에 관한 것이다. C는 회의 사흘 전에 모든 위원의 찬성이 이미 기록되어 있었음을 보여 주므로 그녀의 발표가 결정에 관여할 수 없었다는 점을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 위원들이 위험을 알고도 무시했다는 점은 보여 주지만, 결정이 미리 내려졌는지는 보여 주지 않는다. B는 찬성할 동기를 제시할 뿐 결정 시점은 입증하지 못하며, D는 과거의 행동 패턴일 뿐 이번 투표가 사전에 확정되었다는 증거는 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: Inés's suspicion is about timing: she thinks the outcome was settled before she presented. C shows that every member's endorsement had already been recorded three days before the meeting, so it directly supports the idea that her presentation never played a part in the decision. A shows that members knew about the risk and ignored it anyway, but it doesn't show that the decision was made ahead of time. B gives a possible motive for approving the project, not evidence of when the decision was made, and D describes a past pattern rather than showing that this particular vote was fixed in advance.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A meteorologist presents flood-risk projections to city planners who visibly ignore her data while approving construction in mapped danger zones

hardJudge.note: C가 '회의 사흘 전 찬성 기록'으로 결정 시점이 사전이었음을 직접 입증하여 정답 타당. A·B·D는 각각 위험 인지·동기·과거 패턴으로 부분적 근거를 가지나 '사전 확정'이라는 핵심 시점 요소를 뒷받침하지 못해 비교를 통해 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 자연스러움. 지문은 창작으로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음. 표준 medium 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: C는 '회의 전에 결과가 정해져 있었다'는 시점 요소를 직접 입증한다. B(동기)와 D(과거 패턴)는 그럴듯한 함정으로, 사전 확정을 시사하지만 입증하지는 않는다. A는 상대적으로 약한 오답이지만 말은 된다. 중간 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
The following text is from a short story. Ines, a dental hygienist, is setting up a treatment room.

Ines was laying out the scalers in their usual order when Dr. Pruett's voice came through the thin wall. "Put Mr. Adeyemi down for four crowns," he told the receptionist. "Upper left. Tell him it can't wait." Ines had cleaned Mr. Adeyemi's teeth only last week. She remembered a shallow stain on one molar and nothing more. She set down the mirror and pictured his radiographs, the pale outlines she had studied under the light. But she read films for tartar, she reminded herself, not for decay; she was not the one with the degree. She picked up the scalers and lined them up again, though they had been straight the first time.

A literary critic argues that Ines stays silent in this scene mainly because she doubts what she herself observed, not because she fears what might happen to her if she speaks up.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's argument?

A literary critic argues that Ines stays silent in this scene mainly because she doubts what she herself observed, not because she fears what might happen to her if she speaks up.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's argument?
options: Earlier in the story, Ines worries that her rent is going up and notes that Dr. Pruett's clinic is the only dental office in her small town that is hiring.
Later in the story, Ines tells her sister that Dr. Pruett once fired an assistant who questioned one of his treatment plans in front of a patient.
Later in the story, Ines looks at Mr. Adeyemi's radiographs again and notices the same shallow stain on the molar that she remembered from the cleaning.
Later in the story, Ines confronts Dr. Pruett only after a dentist at another clinic looks at the same radiographs and confirms that the teeth show no decay.
problem.explanation: 비평가는 Ines의 침묵이 자기 관찰에 대한 불신 때문이며, 보복에 대한 두려움 때문이 아니라고 주장한다. D는 다른 치과의사가 그녀의 관찰을 확인해 주자마자 Ines가 위험을 무릅쓰고 맞선다는 점을 보여 준다. 따라서 그녀를 막고 있던 것은 두려움이 아니라 자기 판단에 대한 의심이었다는 뜻이 된다. A와 B는 경제적 불안과 해고 위험을 부각하므로 오히려 '두려움' 해석을 뒷받침한다. C는 Ines의 관찰이 맞았음을 보여 줄 뿐, 그녀가 왜 침묵했는지는 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic argues that Ines stays quiet because she doubts her own observations, not because she fears consequences. D shows that Ines confronts Dr. Pruett as soon as another dentist confirms what she saw, even though speaking up is still risky. That means doubt about her own judgment, not fear, was what held her back. A and B point to money worries and the risk of being fired, so they actually support the fear explanation the critic rejects. C shows that Ines's observation was accurate, but it says nothing about why she stayed silent.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A dental hygienist overhears her employer scheduling patients for unnecessary procedures while she prepares instruments in the adjacent treatment room

hardJudge.note: 지문에서 Ines는 "she was not the one with the degree"라며 자기 판단을 의심하고 침묵한다. D는 외부 전문가가 그녀의 관찰을 확인하자 곧바로 맞선다는 사실을 제시해, 침묵의 원인이 두려움이 아니라 자기 의심이었음을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침한다. A·B는 비평가가 배제하는 '두려움' 해석을 지지하고, C는 관찰의 정확성만 보여 줄 뿐 침묵의 동기를 구분하지 못한다. 해설(한·영)은 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 자연스럽다. 두 가설을 구분하는 2단계 판단이 필요하고 C가 그럴듯한 부분적 오답으로 기능하므로 medium에 적합하다.

advisory.note: D는 두려움 요인이 그대로인 상태에서 확증만 생기자 행동이 바뀌므로 '의심' 가설을 직접 지지한다. A와 B는 반대 가설인 '두려움'을 지지하는 오답이다. C는 관찰이 옳았음을 보여 줄 뿐 침묵의 동기와는 무관하며, 겉으로는 그럴듯해 보이는 매력적인 오답이다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Teodoro cleans the pools at a municipal aquatic center, where the manager, Mr. Halvorsen, records the daily chlorine and pH readings.

Every morning Teodoro dipped the test strips himself, and every morning he watched them bloom the wrong color: pale where they should have been deep, the chlorine thin as a rumor. Then he would pass the office and see Halvorsen bent over the clipboard, writing the same tidy numbers he had written the day before. Teodoro told his sister that the manager was not careless but frightened—that Halvorsen invented the figures because he believed an honest report would cost him his job, not because he didn't understand what the strips meant.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Teodoro's interpretation of Halvorsen's behavior?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Teodoro cleans the pools at a municipal aquatic center, where the manager, Mr. Halvorsen, records the daily chlorine and pH readings.

Every morning Teodoro dipped the test strips himself, and every morning he watched them bloom the wrong color: pale where they should have been deep, the chlorine thin as a rumor. Then he would pass the office and see Halvorsen bent over the clipboard, writing the same tidy numbers he had written the day before. Teodoro told his sister that the manager was not careless but frightened—that Halvorsen invented the figures because he believed an honest report would cost him his job, not because he didn't understand what the strips meant.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Teodoro's interpretation of Halvorsen's behavior?
options: Halvorsen keeps a private notebook in his desk listing the true readings beside a note reading "If the county sees these, they replace me."
Halvorsen keeps a private notebook in his desk listing the readings he recorded, each copied neatly from the previous day's sheet.
Halvorsen keeps a private notebook in his desk listing the dates when the county last inspected the pool and found it acceptable.
Halvorsen keeps a private notebook in his desk listing the chlorine levels he believes are standard, several of which are well below the safe range.
problem.explanation: 테오도로는 Halvorsen이 수치의 의미를 이해하면서도 정직하게 보고하면 직장을 잃을까 두려워 수치를 꾸며낸다고 해석한다. A는 그가 실제 수치를 알고 있다는 점과 교체될까 두려워한다는 점을 함께 보여 주므로 해석의 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다. B는 조작 사실만 확인해 줄 뿐 동기는 보여 주지 못한다. C는 점검 기록일 뿐 두려움이나 이해 여부와 직접 연결되지 않는다. D는 Halvorsen이 안전 기준을 잘못 알고 있음을 시사하므로 '이해 부족이 아니다'라는 해석을 오히려 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: Teodoro's interpretation has two parts: Halvorsen understands what the readings mean, and he fakes them because he's afraid an honest report will cost him his job. Choice A supports both parts, since it shows he knows the true readings and fears being replaced. Choice B confirms only that he copies the numbers, which tells you nothing about why. Choice C records past inspections, but that has no direct connection to fear or understanding. Choice D suggests he misunderstands the safe levels, which actually weakens Teodoro's claim that ignorance isn't the cause.

hardJudge.note: A alone supports both components of Teodoro's interpretation (knowledge of true readings + fear of replacement). B confirms fabrication without motive, C is tangential, D weakens the 'not ignorance' claim. Korean and English explanations agree, letters match, no Korean in English text. Two-step reasoning required; distractors appropriately plausible for medium.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 해석의 두 요소(이해+두려움)를 모두 충족. B(조작만), D(이해 부족 시사로 약화)는 부분 근거형 오답으로 적절하고, C는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 말은 된다. medium에 적합.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Ines, a textile conservator at a city museum, has found traces of a synthetic heat-set adhesive on the backs of several tapestries. Professional conservation ethics guidelines forbid this adhesive because it cannot be fully removed later.

Ines spread her notebook across the worktable. For three weeks she had been recording every tapestry that came off the repair frames: its fibers, its date of departure for loan, and what she found when she turned it over. She did not think her colleagues were careless. Stitching a torn silk warp back onto its linen support could take a month of patient needlework, while wool, being sturdier, could be stitched far more quickly. And a piece that would not leave the building until next year gave everyone time. "They reach for the glue," she said quietly to the empty studio, "only when the silk and the calendar are both against them."

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ines's suspicion?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Ines, a textile conservator at a city museum, has found traces of a synthetic heat-set adhesive on the backs of several tapestries. Professional conservation ethics guidelines forbid this adhesive because it cannot be fully removed later.

Ines spread her notebook across the worktable. For three weeks she had been recording every tapestry that came off the repair frames: its fibers, its date of departure for loan, and what she found when she turned it over. She did not think her colleagues were careless. Stitching a torn silk warp back onto its linen support could take a month of patient needlework, while wool, being sturdier, could be stitched far more quickly. And a piece that would not leave the building until next year gave everyone time. "They reach for the glue," she said quietly to the empty studio, "only when the silk and the calendar are both against them."
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ines's suspicion?
options: Almost every tapestry with adhesive residue in Ines's notebook had silk warps and was due to be shipped within a month, while silk-warped tapestries with later departure dates had been repaired only by stitching.
Almost every tapestry with adhesive residue in Ines's notebook had silk warps, while silk-warped tapestries made up only about a third of all the pieces she recorded.
Almost every tapestry with adhesive residue in Ines's notebook was due to be shipped within a month, while pieces with later departure dates had been repaired only by stitching.
Almost every tapestry with adhesive residue in Ines's notebook had been repaired by the museum's newest staff members, while senior conservators' pieces had been repaired only by stitching.
problem.explanation: 이네스의 의심은 "실크와 일정이 둘 다 불리할 때만" 접착제를 쓴다는 것, 즉 실크 날실과 임박한 출고일이라는 두 조건이 함께 있을 때만 쓴다는 것이다. A는 접착제가 두 조건을 모두 갖춘 작품에 몰려 있다는 점을 보여 준다. 또한 실크라도 출고일이 먼 작품은 바느질로만 수선됐다는 대조가 있어서, 실크만으로는 충분하지 않고 일정 압박도 필요하다는 점까지 확인해 준다. 그래서 가설을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다. B는 실크라는 변수 하나만 다룬다. 출고일에 대한 정보가 없어서 일정 압박이 필요하다는 부분을 뒷받침하지 못한다. C는 출고일이라는 변수 하나만 다룬다. 섬유 종류에 대한 정보가 없어서 울 작품에도 접착제를 썼을 가능성이 남는다. D는 지문에 없는 제3의 변수인 직원 경력을 끌어온다. 이는 이네스의 가설과 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Ines suspects that her colleagues use the glue only when "the silk and the calendar are both against them." In other words, the tapestry must have silk warps AND be due to leave soon. Choice A supports this most directly. It shows that the adhesive appears on pieces that meet both conditions. It also shows that silk pieces with later departure dates were only stitched, so silk alone isn't enough; time pressure is needed too. Choice B looks only at fiber type. Without departure dates, it can't show that the deadline matters. Choice C looks only at departure dates. Without fiber information, it leaves open the possibility that quick-to-stitch wool pieces were glued too. Choice D brings in a third factor, staff experience, that Ines's suspicion never mentions, so it doesn't test her claim.

hardJudge.note: 가설은 '실크 날실 AND 임박한 출고일'이라는 두 조건의 결합("only when ... both")이며, A만이 두 변수를 동시에 반영하고 실크-먼 출고일 대조군까지 제시해 결합 조건의 필요성을 뒷받침한다. B(실크만), C(출고일만)는 각각 단일 변수 함정으로 매력적이며, D는 지문에 없는 직원 경력 변수를 도입. 사소한 한계로 A가 '울+임박 출고일' 대조군은 제공하지 않지만 상대적으로 가장 직접적인 지지라는 판정에는 영향 없음. 해설은 정답과 논리적으로 일치하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 가설은 '실크 AND 임박한 일정'이라는 두 조건이 모두 있어야 한다는 결합 조건이다. A만 두 조건을 함께 반영하고, 실크이지만 일정이 여유 있는 작품과 대조해 실크만으로는 부족하다는 점까지 보여 준다. B와 C는 한 변수만 반영한 매력적 오답으로, C는 '일정이 먼 작품은 바느질'이라는 대조까지 갖춰 A와 형태가 비슷하다. D는 지문 밖의 변수를 끌어온다. 울 작품 중 일정이 임박한 경우의 처리는 A에도 나오지 않지만, 상대 비교에서 A가 최선이라는 점은 분명하다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Ines Varga is a court stenographer whose employer, attorney Konrad Halvorsen, gave the judge a written summary of a witness's expected testimony that morning.

Ines's fingers kept moving even as the words landed. "The truck was already stopped when the light changed," the witness said. That was the opposite of what Halvorsen's summary claimed, the summary Ines herself had typed before dawn. She thought back to the noon recess: she had seen the witness at a corner table in the courthouse café across from Delia Marsh, counsel for the other side, the two of them leaning close over cold coffee. Now, keying the testimony line by line, Ines became convinced that whatever Marsh had said at that table was the reason the witness's story had changed.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ines's suspicion?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Ines Varga is a court stenographer whose employer, attorney Konrad Halvorsen, gave the judge a written summary of a witness's expected testimony that morning.

Ines's fingers kept moving even as the words landed. "The truck was already stopped when the light changed," the witness said. That was the opposite of what Halvorsen's summary claimed, the summary Ines herself had typed before dawn. She thought back to the noon recess: she had seen the witness at a corner table in the courthouse café across from Delia Marsh, counsel for the other side, the two of them leaning close over cold coffee. Now, keying the testimony line by line, Ines became convinced that whatever Marsh had said at that table was the reason the witness's story had changed.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ines's suspicion?
options: Several people in the café that day saw the witness and Marsh talking for nearly the whole noon recess, and some noticed that the witness looked troubled when she returned to the courtroom.

In a recorded exchange with a bailiff shortly before the recess, the witness repeated the account in Halvorsen's summary, and no other source of new information about the accident reached her between that exchange and her testimony.
The witness had asked to meet Marsh at the café because, days earlier, she had privately come to doubt the account she originally gave Halvorsen.
The night before the trial, the witness studied newly released traffic-camera photographs of the intersection, and those photographs contradicted Halvorsen's summary.
problem.explanation:
Ines는 증인이 점심시간에 상대측 변호인 Marsh와 만난 일과 증언이 바뀐 일이 함께 일어났다는 사실만 보고, 그 만남이 증언을 바꾼 원인이라고 추론한다. 이 인과 주장을 지지하려면 두 가지를 확인해야 한다. 증언이 정말 만남 이후에 바뀌었는지(인과 방향), 그리고 다른 원인이 없었는지(대안 설명)이다.
B(정답): 휴정 직전까지도 증인은 Halvorsen의 요약과 같은 진술을 했고, 그 뒤 증언하기 전까지 다른 새 정보를 접하지 않았다. 따라서 진술은 만남 이후에야 바뀌었고, 사이에 끼어든 다른 원인도 배제된다. 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다.
A: 두 사람이 오래 대화했고 증인이 심란해 보였다는 내용은 둘이 함께 있었다는 동시 발생 사실을 다시 확인할 뿐이다. 상관을 인과로 착각하게 만드는 오답이다.
C: 증인이 이미 마음을 바꾼 상태에서 만남을 요청했다면, 증언 변화가 만남의 원인이 된다. 인과 방향이 거꾸로이므로 Ines의 추측을 오히려 약화한다.
D: 전날 밤 본 교통 카메라 사진이라는 제3의 원인이 증언 변화를 설명할 수 있다. 그러면 Marsh와의 만남은 원인이 아닐 수 있다.
problem.explanationEn:
Ines sees two things happen together: the witness met opposing counsel Marsh at lunch, and her testimony changed. From that alone, she infers that the meeting caused the change. To support a causal claim like this, you need to know two things. First, did the change actually come after the meeting? Second, can other explanations be ruled out?
B (correct): Shortly before the recess, the witness still gave the account in Halvorsen's summary, and no other new information reached her before she testified. So the change came after the meeting, and no other cause could have stepped in between. This most directly supports Ines's suspicion.
A: Saying the two talked for a long time and the witness looked troubled only confirms that they were together. It treats correlation as causation.
C: If the witness had already changed her mind and then asked for the meeting, the change in her account caused the meeting, not the other way around. The causal direction is reversed, so this actually weakens Ines's suspicion.
D: The traffic-camera photographs she saw the night before are a third cause that could explain the change in testimony on their own. If so, the meeting with Marsh may not have been the cause at all.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 점심 만남과 증언 변화의 동시 발생만 제시하고 인과는 Ines의 추측으로만 나타남. B는 휴정 직전까지 원래 진술 유지(시간 순서 확립)+그 사이 다른 정보원 부재(대안 배제)로 인과 주장을 가장 직접 지지. A는 동시 발생 재확인(상관→인과 치환), C는 의심이 만남보다 선행(방향 역전, 약화), D는 교통 카메라 사진이라는 제3 원인(대안 설명). 해설은 정답·오답 논리를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 형식 적절, 원작 의심 없음.

advisory.note: B는 시간 순서(만남 직전까지는 원래 진술 유지)와 대안 원인 배제를 함께 갖춰서 정답으로 타당하다. 오답 A는 동시발생 재확인, C는 인과 방향 역전, D는 제3의 원인을 다룬다. D는 '무관한' 원인이라기보다 그럴듯한 대안 원인이지만 레시피 의도에는 부합한다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In this excerpt from a short story, Marisol Vega, manager of a small branch library, reads a memo from the city office. It tells her to cut new purchases for the Spanish, Tagalog, and Vietnamese shelves and to put that money into English titles. Marisol folds the memo and thinks, almost with relief, that the order may not be so bad: if the shelves her patrons rely on grow thin, they will be pushed toward English books, and the push might speed their way into the life of the city.

Text 2
In this excerpt from the same story, Marisol watches Mr. Tran, who visits every Tuesday, run his finger along the Vietnamese shelf. He finds nothing he has not already read and leaves without borrowing anything. The next week he does not come. Over the following month, Marisol notices that several of the regulars from the Tagalog and Spanish sections have also stopped coming. Their library cards sit unused, and nobody takes out the English books she bought.

Based on the texts, how would the scene in Text 2 most likely bear on Marisol's reasoning in Text 1?

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the scene in Text 2 most likely bear on Marisol's reasoning in Text 1?
options: It would confirm that reasoning, since it shows patrons turning away from the shelves that had stopped offering them anything new.
It would complicate that reasoning, since it shows that patrons were reading more English books than Marisol had realized.
It would undercut that reasoning, since it shows that patrons stopped using the library altogether instead of switching to English books.
It would leave that reasoning untested, since it shows only what Mr. Tran did and nothing about the other patrons.
problem.explanation: Text 1에서 Marisol은 모국어 서가가 빈약해지면 이용자들이 영어책으로 옮겨가 도시 생활에 더 빨리 적응할 것이라고 예상한다. Text 2에서 이용자들은 도서관에 아예 오지 않고, 새로 산 영어책도 아무도 빌리지 않으므로 그 예상이 어긋난다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A는 이용자들이 모국어 서가를 외면한 점은 맞지만, 그들이 영어책으로 옮겨가지 않았으므로 Marisol의 추론을 확인해 주지 않는다. B는 영어책을 아무도 빌리지 않았다는 내용과 반대이고, D는 다른 단골 여러 명도 발길을 끊었다는 서술을 놓쳤다.
problem.explanationEn: In Text 1, Marisol predicts that if the home-language shelves grow thin, patrons will move to English books and fit into city life faster. Text 2 shows the opposite: patrons stop coming to the library at all, and nobody borrows the new English books. That undercuts her prediction, so the answer is C. A is right that patrons turned away from the depleted shelves, but they never switched to English books, so the scene doesn't confirm her reasoning. B contradicts the detail that no one checked out the English books, and D ignores the fact that several other regulars also stopped coming.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A community library branch manager receives orders to reduce acquisitions for immigrant patron sections while expanding English-language collections

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 예측(모국어 서가 축소→영어책으로 이동)과 Text 2의 결과(도서관 이탈, 영어책 미대출)를 연결해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요. A는 '서가 외면'이라는 부분적 근거가 있고 D는 Mr. Tran만 보고 훑어 읽으면 선택할 수 있어 비교 배제 요구가 충족됨. B는 텍스트와 직접 모순되나 말은 된다. 해설 한·영 모두 정답 C와 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 창작 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: A는 부분적으로 맞는 근거(서가 외면)를 갖춘 그럴듯한 오답이고, D는 첫 문장만 훑어 읽은 경우를 노린 오답이다. B는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium 수준에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Dara Whitcomb's novel The Count, education coordinator Ines Ruiz watches a guard stack the week's algebra workbooks on a cart and wheel them back toward the property office twenty minutes before class. Ruiz concludes that the guard is acting alone, a petty man punishing her students out of personal spite, and she resolves to report him by name.

Text 2
A critic reviewing The Count notes that the novel quietly undercuts Ruiz's reading of the scene. Later chapters reveal a memo, signed by the warden's office months earlier, directing staff to "delay nonessential materials" whenever headcounts run long, an order the guard is simply carrying out as he was told. The workbooks vanish, the critic observes, because of a policy rather than a personality.

Based on the texts, how would the critic in Text 2 most likely respond to Ruiz's conclusion in Text 1?

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the critic in Text 2 most likely respond to Ruiz's conclusion in Text 1?
options: By arguing that Ruiz is right that the workbooks are being withheld but wrong to put the blame on one guard's motives
By arguing that Ruiz is right to report the guard because the memo makes him responsible for following the warden's order
By arguing that Ruiz is wrong to think the workbooks are being withheld at all, since the guard is only moving them for a headcount
By arguing that Ruiz is right about the guard's spite but wrong to think that reporting him will help her students

B는 메모를 언급하지만 비평가는 경비원을 책임자로 보지 않고 단지 지시를 따랐다고 하므로 틀리다. C는 headcount라는 지문 단어를 쓰지만 비평가는 교재가 보류된다는 사실 자체를 부정하지 않는다. D는 경비원의 악의를 인정하는데, 비평가는 바로 그 악의 해석을 부정한다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic in Text 2 agrees that the workbooks really are being kept from the students ("The workbooks vanish"), but traces this to a policy from the warden's office, not to one man's spite. So the critic would say Ruiz has the facts right but the cause wrong, which is choice A. Choice B brings up the memo, but the critic says the guard is just following orders and never treats him as the one to blame. Choice C uses the word "headcount" from the text, but the critic never says the materials aren't being withheld. Choice D accepts that the guard is spiteful, and that's exactly the reading the critic rejects.

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 비평가는 교재가 사라진다는 사실("The workbooks vanish", "delay nonessential materials")은 인정하면서 원인을 경비원 개인의 악의가 아닌 교도소장실 정책으로 돌리므로 A가 정확히 부합한다. problem.passage:
Text 1
In Teodora Vance's novel The Linen Floor, housekeeping supervisor Marisol Reyes notices a pattern while reviewing staffing charts late one night: rooms booked by guests with certain surnames consistently receive fewer attendants and shorter cleaning times. Vance presents this moment as a solitary revelation. The policy is buried so deeply in the hotel's scheduling software that only Marisol's unusual patience with numbers allows her to see what everyone else has missed.

Text 2
Readers often treat the spreadsheet scene in The Linen Floor as the novel's turning point, but Vance has carefully prepared for it. In earlier chapters, the room attendants joke bitterly about the "short-list floors," and an elderly attendant warns a new hire never to expect enough help on those rooms. When Marisol finally studies the charts, the numbers merely confirm what her staff have been telling her for months, in words she had chosen not to hear.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the characterization of Marisol's late-night review in Text 1?

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the characterization of Marisol's late-night review in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that the policy is well hidden but arguing that the hotel's managers, rather than its software, are mainly responsible for concealing it
By arguing that the pattern Marisol finds had long been recognized by the room attendants, so her review is less an insight of her own than a delayed acceptance of their account

A는 정책이 숨겨져 있다는 Text 1의 전제에 동의하는데, Text 2는 직원들이 이미 알고 있었다고 하므로 틀리다. C는 정책이 의도적이라는 점을 부정하는데, 두 글 어디에도 그런 근거가 없다. D는 이후의 대립 장면을 언급하지만 Text 2는 그런 장면을 다루지 않으며, Marisol의 능력이 핵심이라는 데 동의하지도 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 describes Marisol's discovery as a solitary revelation: she alone sees what everyone else has missed. Text 2 points out that the attendants already joked about the "short-list floors" and warned new hires, and it says the charts only confirmed what Marisol had "chosen not to hear." That makes B correct. A is wrong because it accepts Text 1's view that the policy is well hidden, while Text 2 says the staff already knew about it. C is wrong because neither text suggests the pattern is accidental. D is wrong because Text 2 never mentions a later confrontation, and it doesn't agree that Marisol's skill with numbers is what makes the scene work.

problem.stimulus: At the opening of the Harrowgate Regional Museum, Ilse found Tomas standing before the glass case of Bronze Age loom weights—the same weights the two of them had once spent three summers cataloguing for a book they never finished. When a curator approached to say how much she had admired their early article on the weights and to ask whether the longer study would ever appear, Tomas laughed, said that the canapés were vanishing fast, and steered the group toward the buffet. Ilse noticed that he did not glance back at the case, though he had been studying it intently a moment before. The ease of his conversation, she concluded, was ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: evidence that he had finally lost interest in the loom weights and no longer thought about the work they had shared.
a way of keeping the talk on safe, trivial ground so that the unfinished book would not have to be discussed.
a sign that he hoped the curator's question would persuade Ilse to resume the study with him.
proof that he resented the curator for praising an article that he considered minor.
problem.explanation: 토마스는 공동 연구 이야기가 나오자 카나페 얘기로 화제를 돌리고, 직전까지 유심히 보던 진열장을 다시 보지 않는다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면 그의 가벼운 대화는 미완성 책 이야기를 피하기 위한 수단이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 화제를 피한다는 점은 맞지만, 그가 진열장을 열심히 보고 있었다는 사실과 어긋난다. C는 큐레이터의 질문과 연결되지만 그는 그 질문을 피했으므로 재개를 바란다는 근거가 없다. D는 그가 화제를 돌린 것을 설명하려 하지만 큐레이터에 대한 원망이나 논문을 하찮게 여긴다는 근거는 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Tomas changes the subject to the canapés the moment the unfinished study comes up, and he stops looking at the case he had been studying closely just before. Put those two clues together and his easy chatter looks like a way to avoid talking about the book, so B is correct. A gets the avoidance right, but it doesn't fit the fact that he had been studying the case intently. C ties into the curator's question, but Tomas dodges that question, so nothing suggests he wants to restart the work. D tries to explain why he changes the subject, but the text gives no hint that he resents the curator or thinks the article is minor.

hardJudge.note: 직접 검산: 토마스가 큐레이터의 '긴 연구' 질문에 카나페로 화제를 돌리고, 직전까지 유심히 보던 진열장을 다시 보지 않는다는 두 단서가 결합되어 '미완성 책 논의 회피'라는 B를 뒷받침한다. A는 '흥미 상실'이 '유심히 보던' 서술과 모순, C는 질문을 회피했으므로 재개 희망과 상충, D는 원망·하찮게 여김의 근거 부재. 해설(한/영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 두 단서 연결이 필요하고 A·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

problem.explanation: 분사구문 'Having sorted the valley's mail by hand for thirty-two years'의 의미상 주어는 32년간 우편물을 분류한 사람, 즉 Marguerite이다. 따라서 주절 주어는 Marguerite여야 하며, C가 이를 정확히 주어 자리에 둔다. A: 분사구문 내용과 가장 가까워 보이는 무생물 명사 'sorting cases'를 주어로 삼아, 분류함이 우편을 분류했다는 뜻이 되는 현수 수식어다. B: 앞 문장의 배경 명사 'grange hall'을 주어로 삼아 강당이 우편을 분류한 것처럼 된다. D: 문법적으로 같은 사람 주어지만 'county official'은 우편을 분류한 인물이 아니어서 수식 관계가 틀어진다. Marguerite는 삽입구에만 숨어 있을 뿐이다.
problem.explanationEn: The opening modifier, "Having sorted the valley's mail by hand for thirty-two years," has to describe whoever comes right after the comma as the subject. The person who sorted the mail is Marguerite, so she must be the subject. Choice C does exactly that. Choice A makes the "sorting cases" the subject, which says the cases sorted the mail. They're a lifeless object that only seems connected to sorting. Choice B makes the "grange hall," a setting noun from earlier in the passage, the subject, which is illogical. Choice D uses a person as the subject, but it's the wrong one: the county official didn't sort the valley's mail. In both A and D, Marguerite shows up only inside a side phrase, so she never becomes the subject.

hardJudge.note: 분사구문 'Having sorted the valley's mail...'의 의미상 주어는 앞 문장에서 소개된 Marguerite이며, C만이 이를 주절 주어로 둔다. 세미콜론 뒤 'she could have recited...' 독립절 결합도 모든 선택지에서 동일하여 변별 요소가 수식어 주체 판별로 집중됨. A는 'sorting cases'(분류 행위와 의미상 인접한 무생물), B는 배경 명사 'grange hall', D는 사람 주어이지만 행위자가 아닌 'county official'로, 세 오답 모두 Marguerite를 삽입구에 넣어 착각을 유도하는 설계가 적절. 해설도 정답·오답 근거를 정확히 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: C가 정답이다. 분사구문의 행위자인 Marguerite가 주절 주어이고, 세미콜론 뒤에 독립절이 오므로 문장 구조도 맞다. 다만 사람이면서 우편을 분류한 인물을 주어로 둔 선택지가 C 하나뿐이다. D의 county official도 앞 문맥상 쉽게 배제된다. 오답에 삽입구('in Marguerite's memory', 'Marguerite saw', 'Marguerite noticed')를 넣어 길이를 늘렸지만, 전형적인 medium 수준의 현수 수식어 문항을 넘는 추적은 요구하지 않는다. A는 인접 명사 일치 오류가 아니라 의미 연관 명사를 고르게 하는 함정이어서 체크리스트 3번에는 맞지 않는다.

problem.passage:
Every Tuesday, Marisol Okafor pushed her squeaking cart down the corridor of C Block, carrying the same forty titles she had logged by hand the night before. This week, something was wrong with the count. The history and sociology shelf she had stocked on Monday afternoon held only three volumes by morning______ that nothing had been taken from the library, and the memo on her desk thanked her for her "continued diligence."

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Every Tuesday, Marisol Okafor pushed her squeaking cart down the corridor of C Block, carrying the same forty titles she had logged by hand the night before. This week, something was wrong with the count. The history and sociology shelf she had stocked on Monday afternoon held only three volumes by morning______ that nothing had been taken from the library, and the memo on her desk thanked her for her "continued diligence."
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , the warden's office insisted
; therefore, the warden's office insisted
, and however, the warden's office insisted
; nevertheless, the warden's office insisted
problem.explanation:
정답 D. 앞 절(선반에 책이 세 권만 남음)과 뒤 절(교도소장실은 아무것도 가져가지 않았다고 주장함)은 서로 맞지 않는 대조 관계다. 독립절 두 개를 세미콜론과 대조 접속부사 nevertheless로 이은 D가 문법과 논리 모두에 맞는다.
A: 독립절 두 개를 콤마 하나로만 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
B: 구두점 형식은 맞지만, therefore는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 책이 사라진 것이 '아무것도 가져가지 않았다'는 주장의 원인이 될 수 없으므로 논리가 맞지 않는다.
C: 등위접속사 and와 접속부사 however를 함께 써서 연결어가 중복된다. 게다가 and는 단순 나열을 뜻하므로 대조 관계와도 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice D is correct. The first clause says the shelf was nearly empty. The second says the warden's office claimed nothing had been taken. Those two ideas contrast. D joins the two independent clauses with a semicolon and the contrast word "nevertheless," so it is correct in both grammar and logic.
A creates a comma splice: it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
B has correct punctuation, but "therefore" signals cause and effect. The missing books don't cause the office's denial, so the logic is wrong.
C uses two connectors at once, "and" plus "however," which is redundant. Also, "and" signals simple addition, not contrast.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산: 앞 절(책이 3권만 남음)과 뒤 절(교도소장실은 아무것도 없어지지 않았다고 주장)은 명백한 대조이며, 세미콜론+nevertheless는 독립절 결합 형식으로 적합. A는 콤마 스플라이스, B는 형식은 맞으나 인과(therefore)로 논리 불일치, C는 and+however 연결어 중복. 형식이 올바른 B·D 중에서 의미 판단으로 골라야 하므로 단순 구두점 식별을 넘어 논리관계 선행 판단을 요구함. 다만 오답 구성(콤마 스플라이스/반대 접속사/중복)은 전형적인 패턴이라 난도 상승 폭은 중간 수준. 해설은 정답과 수치·논리적으로 일치하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞고 해설도 일관된다. 다만 구조가 전형적인 medium 문항과 같다. 대조 관계가 문맥에서 바로 드러나고, A(콤마 스플라이스)와 C(and+however 중복)는 형식만 봐도 걸러진다. 실제로 판단이 필요한 것은 B와 D 중 접속부사를 고르는 한 단계뿐이다. 그래서 hard 수준의 추가 사고는 부족하다고 본다.

problem.passage:
Mireille scrolled through the survey spreadsheet a third time. Her field notes recorded forty-one breeding pairs of marbled godwits in the wetland, but the report her supervisor had filed with the county listed only nine, low enough to strip the marsh of its protected status. When she raised the discrepancy, he barely looked up from his desk. "The numbers are whatever the board needs them to be," he said. That night, alone in the field office, she reopened the archived data files, compared each entry against her GPS logs, and ______ every altered count in red.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Mireille scrolled through the survey spreadsheet a third time. Her field notes recorded forty-one breeding pairs of marbled godwits in the wetland, but the report her supervisor had filed with the county listed only nine, low enough to strip the marsh of its protected status. When she raised the discrepancy, he barely looked up from his desk. "The numbers are whatever the board needs them to be," he said. That night, alone in the field office, she reopened the archived data files, compared each entry against her GPS logs, and ______ every altered count in red.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: marked
is marking
marking
had marked
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 빈칸은 주어 she의 세 번째 동사로, reopened, compared와 병렬을 이룬다. 서술 전체가 단순과거로 진행되고 "That night"의 같은 시점에 순서대로 일어난 동작이므로 단순과거 marked가 알맞다. B(is marking): 인용문 속 현재시제(are, needs)에 이끌린 선택이다. 인용문은 상사가 말한 직접화법일 뿐이고, 이를 감싸는 서술은 과거시제이다. C(marking): 병렬 항목 중 이것만 분사형이 되어 주어 she의 정형동사가 빠지고 구조가 무너진다. D(had marked): 앞의 "the report her supervisor had filed" 절의 과거완료와는 맞아 보이지만, 표시하는 동작은 파일을 다시 열고 비교한 뒤에 일어났으므로 그보다 앞선 시점을 나타내는 과거완료는 문맥과 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. The blank is the third verb in a series with the subject "she": she "reopened," "compared," and ___. The narration is in simple past, and all three actions happen in order on "That night," so the simple past "marked" keeps the series parallel and the tense consistent. B ("is marking") follows the present tense inside the supervisor's quotation ("are," "needs"). But that is his direct speech, and the narration around it stays in the past. C ("marking") turns only one item in the series into a participle, so "she" has no finite verb for that action and the parallel structure breaks. D ("had marked") seems to match the past perfect in "the report her supervisor had filed." But the marking happened after she reopened and compared the files, not before them, so the past perfect gives the wrong time order.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A(marked) 검산 완료: reopened, compared와 단순과거 병렬, "That night" 동일 시점의 순차 동작. B는 인용문의 현재시제(are, needs)에 유도되는 오답(체크리스트 3은 '인용문에 이끌린 시제'로 해석하여 충족 처리), C는 병렬 중 유일한 비정형, D는 앞의 had filed와 국소적으로 호응하나 사건 순서상 과거완료 불가. 해설의 인용·시제 언급 모두 지문과 일치. 인용문 시제 vs 서술 시제 분리, 사건 순서 판단, 병렬 유지라는 세 층위의 판단이 필요해 medium을 넘는다.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞음. 'reopened, compared, and ___' 3항 병렬이라 형태가 곧바로 정해짐. 현재시제 인용문과 과거완료 절이 방해 요소로 들어가 있지만, 바로 앞 병렬 동사만 봐도 풀리므로 문맥 전체를 추적할 필요가 없음. 결국 지문 길이를 빼면 전형적인 medium 수준의 병렬 문항임.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Venn's novel The Linden Ledger, editor Ruth Abernathy decides to hold her story about safety violations at the Corwin Mill. The mill's owners buy half the paper's ad space, and Ruth reasons that if the Ledger folds, the town loses its only paper. "A paper that survives can tell the truth next year," she tells her reporter. "A paper that dies tells nobody anything."

Text 2
In a short story by Theo Ashgrove, a weekly's publisher prints an account of injuries at the town cannery the same week the cannery cancels its advertising. Ashgrove's narrator observes that every week a paper stays quiet, readers learn what its silence costs and who can buy it. By the time such a paper is ready to speak, the narrator says, no one is listening.

Based on the texts, how would Ashgrove's narrator in Text 2 most likely respond to Ruth's reasoning in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Marisol Venn's novel The Linden Ledger, editor Ruth Abernathy decides to hold her story about safety violations at the Corwin Mill. The mill's owners buy half the paper's ad space, and Ruth reasons that if the Ledger folds, the town loses its only paper. "A paper that survives can tell the truth next year," she tells her reporter. "A paper that dies tells nobody anything."

Text 2
In a short story by Theo Ashgrove, a weekly's publisher prints an account of injuries at the town cannery the same week the cannery cancels its advertising. Ashgrove's narrator observes that every week a paper stays quiet, readers learn what its silence costs and who can buy it. By the time such a paper is ready to speak, the narrator says, no one is listening.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Ashgrove's narrator in Text 2 most likely respond to Ruth's reasoning in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that she is right to keep the paper alive, since a newspaper that closes can no longer report on anything in the town
By insisting that she should print the story at once, since a publisher's duty is to report injuries whatever happens to the advertising
By arguing that her real mistake is letting the mill buy so much ad space, since a paper should never depend on a single advertiser
By pointing out that her plan undermines itself, since staying quiet now would destroy the very credibility the paper needs if it is to report the truth later
problem.explanation: 정답 D: Text 2의 화자는 신문이 침묵할 때마다 독자가 그 침묵이 매수될 수 있다는 것을 알게 되고, 결국 말할 준비가 되었을 때는 아무도 듣지 않는다고 본다. 이 전제를 적용하면 '살아남은 신문이 내년에 진실을 말할 수 있다'는 Ruth의 논리는 스스로를 무너뜨린다. 지금의 침묵이 나중에 진실을 전할 때 필요한 신뢰를 없애기 때문이다. A: Ruth의 주장(Text 1)을 그대로 되풀이할 뿐 Text 2의 관점이 아니다. B: Text 2의 결론(기사를 실었다)만 반복한 것으로, Ruth의 '나중에 말하겠다'는 근거를 신뢰 상실의 논리로 반박하지 못한다. 게다가 Text 2는 이를 의무로 제시하지도 않는다. C: 광고주 한 곳에 대한 의존 문제는 Text 2가 다루지 않는 쟁점이다.
problem.explanationEn: D is correct. Ashgrove's narrator believes that each week a paper stays silent, readers learn that its silence can be bought, so by the time it finally speaks, no one is listening. Apply that idea to Ruth's reasoning that a paper that survives "can tell the truth next year," and her plan defeats itself: keeping quiet now destroys the trust the paper would need for its later reporting to matter. A just repeats Ruth's own argument from Text 1, so it doesn't reflect Text 2's view. B only restates what happens in Text 2 (the publisher prints the story). It doesn't answer Ruth's "speak later" reasoning with the narrator's point about lost credibility, and Text 2 never presents printing the story as a duty. C brings in an issue Text 2 never discusses: depending too heavily on one advertiser.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 언급하지 않으며, 정답 D는 Text 2 화자의 전제(침묵은 매수 가능성을 학습시키고, 나중에 말할 때 아무도 듣지 않는다)를 Ruth의 '살아남아 내년에 말하겠다'는 논리에 적용해야만 도출됨. A는 Text 1 반복, C는 본문 외 쟁점(단일 광고주 의존). B는 Text 2 발행인의 행동과 겉보기에 일치해 매력적인 오답이지만, '의무'라는 표현으로 강도를 과장하고 Ruth의 '나중에' 논리를 직접 반박하지 않아 D와 구분 가능. 해설은 정답과 오답 배제 이유를 정확히 뒷받침함. 가상의 작품으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: D는 Text 2의 전제(침묵은 신뢰를 잃게 해 나중에 아무도 듣지 않음)를 Ruth의 '살아남으면 내년에 말할 수 있다'는 논리에 적용해, 그 논리가 스스로를 무너뜨린다고 추론해야 하는 선택지다. B는 Text 2의 행동을 의무로 과잉 일반화한 강도 함정이고, A는 Text 1을 되풀이하며, C는 본문에 없는 쟁점을 끌어온다. 형식과 정답 모두 문제없다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Mara Okafor's novel The Bite Registration, dental lab technician Dolores Varga opens a tray of crowns labeled as solid zirconia, the costly material her employer bills insurers and patients for, and finds cheaper metal-based crowns instead. Okafor describes the grayish edge of each crown in close detail, and critic Hal Brennan notes that someone with Dolores's twenty years at the bench would know at a glance what she is holding. For Brennan, this is why the six weeks she then spends saying nothing make the novel a study in workplace cowardice: she sees the fraud plainly and chooses to look away.

Text 2
Critic Ines Albarrán points out that the chapter right before the tray scene has Dolores's employer announcing a "new supplier with a slightly different finish." The weeks that follow are not empty, either. Dolores starts a private notebook in which she records order numbers, weighs crowns on the lab scale, and compares them with invoices, crossing out guesses as she rules them out. Okafor, Albarrán argues, turns these weeks into a slow, uncertain investigation. Readers may still judge Dolores's final choices harshly, but the early silence belongs to someone who is not yet sure what she has found.

Based on the texts, which part of Brennan's reading in Text 1 would Albarrán in Text 2 most likely take issue with?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Mara Okafor's novel The Bite Registration, dental lab technician Dolores Varga opens a tray of crowns labeled as solid zirconia, the costly material her employer bills insurers and patients for, and finds cheaper metal-based crowns instead. Okafor describes the grayish edge of each crown in close detail, and critic Hal Brennan notes that someone with Dolores's twenty years at the bench would know at a glance what she is holding. For Brennan, this is why the six weeks she then spends saying nothing make the novel a study in workplace cowardice: she sees the fraud plainly and chooses to look away.

Text 2
Critic Ines Albarrán points out that the chapter right before the tray scene has Dolores's employer announcing a "new supplier with a slightly different finish." The weeks that follow are not empty, either. Dolores starts a private notebook in which she records order numbers, weighs crowns on the lab scale, and compares them with invoices, crossing out guesses as she rules them out. Okafor, Albarrán argues, turns these weeks into a slow, uncertain investigation. Readers may still judge Dolores's final choices harshly, but the early silence belongs to someone who is not yet sure what she has found.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which part of Brennan's reading in Text 1 would Albarrán in Text 2 most likely take issue with?
options: The idea that Dolores understands what the substituted crowns mean the moment she sees the tray
The idea that the novel as a whole should be read as a portrait of cowardice at work
The idea that the employer charges insurers and patients for zirconia crowns
The idea that Okafor pays close attention to the physical details of Dolores's work
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Brennan의 '비겁함' 결론은 Dolores가 쟁반을 보는 순간 사기임을 알아차렸다는 가정("know at a glance", "sees the fraud plainly")에 기대고 있다. Albarrán은 '새 공급업체' 발표와 확인 작업을 기록한 노트를 근거로, 그 몇 주 동안 Dolores가 아직 확신하지 못했다고 보므로 바로 이 가정을 정면으로 겨냥한다.
B: 결론 자체를 고른 오답이다. Albarrán은 독자가 Dolores의 마지막 선택은 여전히 가혹하게 평가할 수 있다고 인정한다. 그녀가 무너뜨리는 것은 결론이 기대는 전제이지, 소설 전체에 대한 평가가 아니다.
C: 부수적인 세부를 고른 오답이다. 청구 방식은 두 비평가 모두 문제 삼지 않는 배경 설정이다.
D: Text 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분이다. Albarrán도 무게 측정, 송장 대조 같은 작업 묘사에 기대어 논지를 펼친다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. Brennan's claim that the novel is about cowardice depends on an assumption: that Dolores recognizes the fraud right away. He says she would "know at a glance" and that she "sees the fraud plainly." Albarrán challenges exactly this point. She cites the employer's "new supplier" announcement and Dolores's notebook of checks to show that Dolores is not yet sure what she has found.
Choice B is wrong because it names Brennan's conclusion, not the assumption under it. Albarrán even grants that readers may still judge Dolores's final choices harshly. Her target is the premise the conclusion rests on.
Choice C is wrong because the billing practice is background that neither critic disputes.
Choice D is wrong because Albarrán agrees with it. Her own argument relies on Okafor's detailed scenes of weighing crowns and comparing invoices.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(비겁함 연구)과 근거(한눈에 알아봄, 사기를 명백히 봄)를 분리해 제시하고, Text 2는 '새 공급업체' 발표와 노트·저울·송장 대조라는 구체 근거로 그 전제(즉시 인지)만을 겨냥하며, 마지막 선택은 가혹히 평가할 수 있다고 양보해 결론 자체(B)에는 직접 반대하지 않는다. A가 명확한 정답이며 B는 결론/전제 혼동, C는 공통 배경, D는 Text 2가 오히려 기대는 부분으로 오답 기능이 뚜렷하다. Albarrán이 Brennan에게 어떻게 반응할지는 명시되지 않아 스스로 추론해야 하고, B를 배제하려면 양보 문장의 강도를 정확히 읽어야 하므로 hard 특성 충족. 허구 작품·비평가로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: Albarrán이 직접 겨냥하는 대상은 'know at a glance'라는 가정이므로 정답 A는 타당하다. B는 결론이고 Albarrán이 부분적으로 양보하는 지점이어서, 가정과 결론을 구분하고 입장의 강도를 가늠해야 걸러진다. D는 Text 2가 작업 묘사에 기대어 논지를 펴므로 사실상 동의하는 부분이다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Fiction about institutional wrongdoing often fails at the very moment it seems to succeed. When a novelist exposes a scheme and then hands the blame to a single scheming individual, readers close the book relieved, and that relief is the problem. The most honest stories of this kind show harm living inside ordinary procedures—forms, schedules, habits no one questions—so that removing one person changes nothing essential.

Text 2
In Lorna Achterberg's novel The Long Route, Della Voss reads electric meters for a rural cooperative and slowly realizes that the households on the poorest roads are billed for power they never used. The novel's finest stretch follows Della as she matches her handwritten logs against the printed bills until the trail leads to one office: that of billing supervisor Harlan Pruitt. His dismissal in the final chapter delivers a resolution as earned as it is satisfying, rewarding the reader's patience with justice.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the final chapter of The Long Route that is praised in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:

The most honest stories of this kind show harm living inside ordinary procedures—forms, schedules, habits no one questions—so that removing one person changes nothing essential.

Text 2
In Lorna Achterberg's novel The Long Route, Della Voss reads electric meters for a rural cooperative and slowly realizes that the households on the poorest roads are billed for power they never used. The novel's finest stretch follows Della as she matches her handwritten logs against the printed bills until the trail leads to one office: that of billing supervisor Harlan Pruitt. His dismissal in the final chapter delivers a resolution as earned as it is satisfying, rewarding the reader's patience with justice.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the final chapter of The Long Route that is praised in Text 2?
options: As a strength, because Della's careful comparison of logs and bills makes the supervisor's eventual dismissal feel deserved rather than arbitrary
As a weakness, because tracing the overbilling to one man's office lets readers believe the cooperative's ordinary practices are sound once he is gone
As a weakness, because Della's slow investigation is convincing but the punishment given to Pruitt is too mild to count as real justice
As a weakness, because a meter reader would be unlikely to have access to the printed bills needed to uncover the scheme
problem.explanation:
정답 B: Text 1 저자의 기준은 '부정이 일상적 절차 속에 있음을 보여 주어, 한 사람을 제거해도 본질이 바뀌지 않게 하는 것'이며, 한 개인에게 책임을 돌려 독자에게 안도감을 주는 결말을 실패로 본다. Text 2가 칭찬하는 Pruitt 해고 결말은 바로 그 유형이므로 Text 1 저자는 이를 약점으로 평가할 것이다.
A: Text 2 저자의 기준(차근차근 쌓아 얻은 만족스러운 정의)으로 평가한 것이다.
C: 조사 과정 칭찬과 '처벌이 약하다'는 불만을 섞은 것으로, Text 1은 처벌 수위가 아니라 한 개인에게 책임을 돌리는 것 자체를 문제 삼는다.
D: 현실성이라는 일반 상식적 기준으로, 두 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: The author of Text 1 judges this kind of fiction by one standard: it should show that the harm is built into ordinary procedures, so that removing one person changes nothing essential. Text 1 calls stories that pin the blame on a single individual a failure because they leave readers feeling relieved. The ending Text 2 praises, Pruitt's dismissal, does exactly that, so the author of Text 1 would see it as a weakness.
A judges the ending by Text 2's standard, a hard-earned and satisfying sense of justice. The author of Text 1 rejects that standard.
C combines praise for the investigation with a complaint that the punishment is too mild. Text 1 doesn't care how harsh the punishment is. Its objection is to blaming one person at all.
D judges the plot by whether it's realistic, which is a common-sense standard. Neither text supports it.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 기준(한 개인에게 책임을 돌려 독자에게 안도감을 주는 결말은 실패; 절차 속 부정을 보여야 함)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2의 Pruitt 해고 결말은 정확히 그 유형이므로 B가 유일하게 Text 1 관점에서 도출된다. A는 Text 2 평자의 기준, C는 조사 과정 칭찬(Text 2)과 처벌 수위 불만(어느 지문에도 없음)을 섞은 혼합 오답, D는 외부 상식. 정답이 Text 1의 핵심 문구("removing one person changes nothing essential")를 패러프레이즈해 본문 명시 없는 반응 추론과 관점 유지 평가를 요구한다. 가상의 소설·작가라 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: Text 1의 기준(한 개인에게 책임을 돌려 안도감을 주면 실패)을 Text 2의 Pruitt 해고 결말에 그대로 적용하면 B가 나온다. A는 Text 2의 기준, C는 두 관점을 섞은 것, D는 근거 없는 현실성 기준이다. 다만 Text 1의 기준이 꽤 직접적으로 드러나 있어서, 대응 관계는 비교적 쉽게 찾을 수 있다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In a novel, conservation biologist Mara Elling shows a slide of plover nests mapped across the dunes where a marina will be built. Later, her funders cancel her grant before the study is published. The narrator says Mara's mistake was presenting too early: if she had kept her findings private until the paper appeared in print, the data would have been safe, and the cancellation could not have buried it.

Text 2
A critic writing about the same novel argues that the grant's cancellation shows how institutions shape knowledge long before anything is published. In the book, the funders control the boat access, the field permits, and the lab where Mara's samples are stored. The critic notes that a paper's arrival in print depends at every step on resources the funders could take away whenever they chose.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the narrator's claim in Text 1 about when Mara should have shared her findings?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In a novel, conservation biologist Mara Elling shows a slide of plover nests mapped across the dunes where a marina will be built. Later, her funders cancel her grant before the study is published. The narrator says Mara's mistake was presenting too early: if she had kept her findings private until the paper appeared in print, the data would have been safe, and the cancellation could not have buried it.

Text 2
A critic writing about the same novel argues that the grant's cancellation shows how institutions shape knowledge long before anything is published. In the book, the funders control the boat access, the field permits, and the lab where Mara's samples are stored. The critic notes that a paper's arrival in print depends at every step on resources the funders could take away whenever they chose.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the narrator's claim in Text 1 about when Mara should have shared her findings?
options: By agreeing that sharing her findings early was what led the funders to cancel the grant before publication
By arguing that the cancellation proves institutions shape knowledge before anything is published
By objecting that holding back her findings would not have protected them, since the funders could still cut off what publication required
By claiming that Mara should have looked for other funders whose interests had nothing to do with the marina
problem.explanation: 정답 C: Text 2에 따르면 출판까지 가는 모든 단계(배 접근, 허가, 시료 보관 연구실)가 후원자에게 달려 있다. 그러니 비공개로 버텼더라도 후원자는 출판에 필요한 자원을 끊을 수 있었고, 이 전제에서 Text 1의 '출판 때까지 숨겼으면 안전했다'는 주장은 성립하지 않는다는 반응이 나온다. A: Text 1의 인과 설명을 그대로 되풀이할 뿐, Text 2의 관점과는 반대다. B: Text 2의 결론을 다시 말할 뿐, 공개 시점에 관한 주장에는 답하지 않는다. D: 다른 후원자를 찾는 문제는 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
problem.explanationEn: Choice C is correct. Text 2 says that every step toward publication (boat access, permits, the lab storing the samples) depends on the funders, and they can take these away at any time. From that point, it follows that keeping the findings private would not have kept them safe, because the funders could still block publication. That undercuts the narrator's claim in Text 1. Choice A just repeats Text 1's explanation, which Text 2's view contradicts. Choice B restates Text 2's own conclusion but doesn't address the claim about when Mara should have shared her findings. Choice D brings in a different issue, finding other funders, which Text 2 never discusses.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 소설만 언급하고 Text 1 화자의 주장은 직접 다루지 않음. 정답 C는 Text 2의 전제(출판까지의 모든 자원이 후원자 통제하에 있음)를 Text 1의 '비공개로 버텼으면 안전' 주장에 적용해야만 도출됨. A는 Text 1 인과 반복, B는 Text 2 결론만 재진술하여 시점 주장에 응답하지 않음(기능/내용 혼동 함정), D는 본문 밖 쟁점. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 모순 없이 뒷받침함. 가상 소설 기반이라 저작권·사실 오류 없음.

advisory.note: Text 2는 공개 시점을 직접 다루지 않는다. 그래서 '출판에 필요한 자원은 언제든 끊길 수 있다'는 전제에서 Text 1의 주장이 틀렸다는 반응을 독자가 추론해야 한다. B는 Text 2의 결론을 되풀이하는 매력적인 함정으로, 질문의 초점(공개 시점)과 어긋나 hard 수준에 맞는다. 다만 C의 표현이 Text 2의 마지막 문장과 상당히 겹쳐서 실제 난이도는 다소 낮아질 수 있다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Achebe-Reyes's novel The Quiet Ward, records clerk Ines Okafor watches through the glass of a late-shift office as her supervisor, Mr. Halvorsen, rewrites medication dosages in charts for patients whose treatment has already been given. Ines files the charts without a word. Critic Dana Whitcomb argues that this silence is the novel's moral center: because Ines plainly grasps that the new figures are falsifications, her choice to stay silent makes her complicit. The book therefore indicts institutions that reward quiet compliance.

Text 2
Critic Rafael Moynihan points to a scene that readers often skip over. On Ines's first day, Halvorsen tells her that charts are routinely "reconciled" against pharmacy logs after the fact, and the narrator notes that Ines, hired from a shipping company, "could not have told a milligram from a microgram." When she later watches the charts being changed, Moynihan observes, the text gives no sign that she reads the changes as anything but the reconciliation she was told to expect. Her silence, he argues, is real, but it may not be a choice to look away.

Based on the texts, which part of Whitcomb's reading as described in Text 1 would Moynihan most likely dispute?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Marisol Achebe-Reyes's novel The Quiet Ward, records clerk Ines Okafor watches through the glass of a late-shift office as her supervisor, Mr. Halvorsen, rewrites medication dosages in charts for patients whose treatment has already been given. Ines files the charts without a word. Critic Dana Whitcomb argues that this silence is the novel's moral center: because Ines plainly grasps that the new figures are falsifications, her choice to stay silent makes her complicit. The book therefore indicts institutions that reward quiet compliance.

Text 2
Critic Rafael Moynihan points to a scene that readers often skip over. On Ines's first day, Halvorsen tells her that charts are routinely "reconciled" against pharmacy logs after the fact, and the narrator notes that Ines, hired from a shipping company, "could not have told a milligram from a microgram." When she later watches the charts being changed, Moynihan observes, the text gives no sign that she reads the changes as anything but the reconciliation she was told to expect. Her silence, he argues, is real, but it may not be a choice to look away.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which part of Whitcomb's reading as described in Text 1 would Moynihan most likely dispute?
options: The claim that the novel ultimately indicts institutions that reward quiet compliance
The claim that the late-shift office setting separates Ines from the scene she watches
The claim that Ines files the altered charts without saying anything to anyone
The claim that Ines understands the revised figures to be falsifications
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Whitcomb은 Ines가 수정된 수치를 조작으로 '분명히 알아차렸다'는 가정 위에서 침묵을 공모로 해석한다. Moynihan은 첫날 들은 '사후 대조' 설명과 Ines에게 약학 지식이 없다는 점을 근거로, Ines가 그 변경을 일상적인 대조 작업으로 보았을 수 있다고 지적한다. 그러므로 Moynihan이 직접 공격하는 것은 Ines가 상황을 이해했다는 이 전제다.
A: Whitcomb의 결론이다. Moynihan은 그 결론이 기대는 전제를 흔들 뿐, 소설이 제도를 비판하는지 여부는 다루지 않는다.
B: 장면 배경에 관한 부수적 세부다. Text 2는 이 점을 언급하지 않는다.
C: Moynihan도 "Her silence ... is real"이라며 동의하는 부분이다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. Whitcomb's reading rests on the assumption that Ines plainly understands the new figures to be falsifications. That is why she can call Ines's silence complicity. Moynihan cites the "reconciliation" explanation Ines heard on her first day and her lack of pharmacological knowledge. He argues that she may have taken the changes for routine corrections, which directly undermines this assumption.
A is wrong because it is Whitcomb's conclusion. Moynihan challenges what that conclusion depends on, not whether the novel criticizes institutions.
B is wrong because it is a minor detail about the setting, and Text 2 never mentions it.
C is wrong because Moynihan agrees with it: he says her silence "is real."

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(제도 비판)과 근거(Ines가 조작임을 분명히 앎 → 침묵은 공모)가 구분됨. Text 2는 '앎' 전제만 공격하며 침묵 자체(C)에는 동의. Moynihan이 Whitcomb의 어느 부분을 공격할지 명시되지 않아 추론 필요. A는 결론을 공격한다고 오해하면 끌리는 함정으로 적절. B는 다소 약한 오답이나 문항 전체 기능엔 문제 없음. 가상 소설·비평가로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞다. Moynihan은 Ines가 상황을 이해했다는 전제를 공격하고, 결론(A)은 다루지 않으며, 침묵(C)에는 동의한다. 다만 Moynihan의 입장이 'may not be a choice'로 비교적 분명히 드러나서 추론하는 부담은 중간을 약간 넘는 정도다. B는 Text 1에 없는 주장이라 너무 쉽게 소거된다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Priya, a software tester, has found three serious security flaws in a banking app that is set to launch on Friday.

Priya's manager read her report and slid it back across the desk. "Hold this until after launch," he said. "Nobody outside this room needs to know yet." Priya returned to her cubicle. She opened the report again, checked every detail, and then saved a second copy, dated and signed, in a folder only she could access. Her decision to make that extra copy suggests that she ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Priya, a software tester, has found three serious security flaws in a banking app that is set to launch on Friday.

Priya's manager read her report and slid it back across the desk. "Hold this until after launch," he said. "Nobody outside this room needs to know yet." Priya returned to her cubicle. She opened the report again, checked every detail, and then saved a second copy, dated and signed, in a folder only she could access. Her decision to make that extra copy suggests that she ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: wants a record proving she found the flaws before the launch.
wants the flaws repaired before her manager reads the report.
wants her manager to see a neater version of the report.
wants the launch moved up so that the app reaches users sooner.
problem.explanation: Priya의 상사는 출시 후까지 보고를 미루라고 지시했고, 그녀는 날짜와 서명을 넣은 사본을 자기만 접근할 수 있는 곳에 저장했다. 이는 자신이 결함을 일찍 발견했다는 증거를 남기려는 행동이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 틀렸다. 상사는 이미 보고서를 읽었다. C는 틀렸다. 사본은 상사에게 보여 주려는 것이 아니라 자신만 볼 수 있는 곳에 숨겨져 있다. D는 틀렸다. 출시를 앞당기고 싶어 한다는 단서는 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Priya's manager tells her to hold the report until after launch, and she then saves a dated, signed copy in a folder only she can access. That is a way of keeping proof that she found the flaws early, so A is correct. B is wrong because the manager has already read the report. C is wrong because the copy is hidden where only Priya can see it, not prepared for her manager. D is wrong because nothing in the text suggests she wants the launch to happen sooner.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A software quality assurance tester documents critical security vulnerabilities in a financial app but is instructed by management to delay reporting them

hardJudge.note: 단서(날짜·서명 사본, 본인만 접근 가능한 폴더, 상사의 보류 지시)가 지문에 직접 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 A 도출. B는 '상사가 이미 읽었다'와, C는 '자기만 접근 가능'과 모순, D는 근거 없음. 오답은 전형적 오개념 수준으로 그럴듯함. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 단서(dated, signed, only she could access)가 지문에 직접 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 A가 도출된다. B·C는 지문과 바로 모순되고 D는 근거가 없어 쉽게 배제된다. easy 수준에 적합하다. 다만 B·D는 다소 약한 오답이다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Marisol Ortega, a building inspector, is examining a new office building whose final certification review is scheduled for the next morning.

Marisol pointed her flashlight at the open panel. Three of the breakers were wired to cables far too thin for the load, a clear violation of the electrical code. Behind her, the contractor, Dale Whitcomb, cleared his throat. "The review board meets at nine," he said. "If your signature isn't on that form tonight, my crew loses a month of work." Marisol kept her eyes on the wires. Her pen stayed in her pocket. A student reading the story claims that Marisol is determined not to approve work she knows is unsafe, no matter how much Whitcomb pushes her.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
