Later in the story, Marisol tells Whitcomb that the review board has recently become stricter about deadlines for paperwork.
Later in the story, Marisol writes "FAILED: undersized wiring" on the form and hands it back to Whitcomb as he protests.
problem.explanation: 학생의 주장은 마리솔이 압박에도 불구하고 안전하지 않은 작업을 승인하지 않으려 한다는 것이다. D는 휘트컴이 항의하는 중에도 불합격 판정을 적어 돌려주는 행동을 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 휘트컴에 대한 과거의 존경일 뿐 승인 거부와 무관하다. B는 건물의 외관 묘사로 결정과 관련이 없다. C는 심사위원회의 마감 규정에 관한 것으로 안전하지 않은 작업을 거부한다는 점을 보여 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The student claims that Marisol refuses to approve unsafe work even under pressure. Choice D shows her marking the form as failed because of the wiring while Whitcomb protests, which directly supports that claim. Choice A only shows past admiration for Whitcomb, which says nothing about whether she will approve the work. Choice B describes the building's appearance, not her decision. Choice C concerns paperwork deadlines and does not show her refusing to approve unsafe work.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A construction site inspector finds that electrical work fails to meet code but the contractor pressures her to sign off before certification review

hardJudge.note: 지문이 위반 사실·압박·펜을 꺼내지 않는 행동을 명시하고, D는 항의 중에도 불합격 판정을 내리는 직접 증거로 주장을 뒷받침한다. A/B/C는 각각 과거 감정, 외관, 마감 규정으로 주장과 무관하나 표면적으로 그럴듯한 전형적 오답. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음. easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: D만 압박 속 불합격 판정을 직접 보여 줌. 오답 B는 다소 무관해 보이지만 A·C는 그럴듯한 오답이라 easy 난이도에 맞음.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In this scene from a novel, freelance journalist Mara Quint reads her published profile of a local baker and finds a quote she never recorded: "Bread is my whole life." Her editor, Dev, shrugs it off. "It's what he would have said," Dev tells her. "Readers want a voice, and nobody gets hurt by a harmless line."

Text 2
Later in the same novel, Mara calls the baker to apologize. He is upset. "I never said that," he tells her. "My customers now think I care about nothing but the shop. My daughter asked why I said it. Words you put in a person's mouth do not stay small."

Based on the texts, how would the baker in Text 2 most likely respond to Dev's claim in Text 1 about the invented quote?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In this scene from a novel, freelance journalist Mara Quint reads her published profile of a local baker and finds a quote she never recorded: "Bread is my whole life." Her editor, Dev, shrugs it off. "It's what he would have said," Dev tells her. "Readers want a voice, and nobody gets hurt by a harmless line."

Text 2
Later in the same novel, Mara calls the baker to apologize. He is upset. "I never said that," he tells her. "My customers now think I care about nothing but the shop. My daughter asked why I said it. Words you put in a person's mouth do not stay small."
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the baker in Text 2 most likely respond to Dev's claim in Text 1 about the invented quote?
options: He would reject it, pointing out that the made-up line has changed how people close to him see him.
He would accept it, pointing out that the made-up line matches what he would probably have said anyway.
He would accept it, pointing out that the made-up line gave readers the lively voice they wanted.
He would reject it, pointing out that the made-up line was too dull to interest readers.
problem.explanation: Text 1에서 Dev는 꾸며낸 인용문이 아무에게도 해가 없다고 주장한다. Text 2에서 제빵사는 손님들과 딸이 자신을 다르게 보게 되었다고 말하며 그 말이 "작게 남지 않는다"고 하므로, 해가 없다는 주장을 반박할 것이다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 제빵사가 "그런 말을 한 적 없다"며 화를 내므로 틀렸다. C는 Dev의 관점일 뿐 제빵사의 관점이 아니고, D는 제빵사가 문장이 지루하다고 불평한 적이 없으므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: In Text 1, Dev claims the invented quote is harmless. In Text 2, the baker says his customers and even his daughter now see him differently, and that such words "do not stay small," so he would reject the idea that no harm was done. That makes A correct. B is wrong because the baker is upset and insists he never said it. C reflects Dev's view, not the baker's, and D is wrong because the baker never complains that the line was dull.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A freelance journalist discovers her editor routinely adds false attribution quotes to sources who never actually said them in published articles

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 직접 진술("customers now think…", "My daughter asked…", "do not stay small")이 Dev의 '해가 없다'는 주장을 명시적으로 반박하므로 A가 정답. B·C는 Dev의 관점을 제빵사에게 잘못 귀속시키는 전형적 오개념, D는 반대(reject)이지만 근거가 지문에 없어 배제 가능. 추론 한 단계, 어휘 평이 — easy 적합. 두 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 창작 지문으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 단서(customers, daughter, do not stay small)가 직접 드러나 easy에 적합. D는 다소 약한 오답이나 허용 범위. 'people close to him'은 손님까지 포괄하기엔 약간 느슨하지만 딸 포함으로 무리 없음.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Reyes's short story "Second Helping," lunch coordinator Dana Pruitt finds a district memo showing that schools in low-income neighborhoods now receive cheaper meals with fewer vegetables. When she shows it to her principal, he shrugs and says the change probably makes no real difference to the children, since most of them would throw the vegetables away anyway.

Text 2
In a review of "Second Helping," critic Owen Hale writes that the story's quiet strength lies in its later scenes. Dana watches the same children grow tired and unfocused by early afternoon, and the nurse's office fills with students complaining of headaches. Hale argues that these details make clear the cut is hurting the students in visible ways.

Based on the texts, how would Hale (Text 2) most likely respond to the principal's claim in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Marisol Reyes's short story "Second Helping," lunch coordinator Dana Pruitt finds a district memo showing that schools in low-income neighborhoods now receive cheaper meals with fewer vegetables. When she shows it to her principal, he shrugs and says the change probably makes no real difference to the children, since most of them would throw the vegetables away anyway.

Text 2
In a review of "Second Helping," critic Owen Hale writes that the story's quiet strength lies in its later scenes. Dana watches the same children grow tired and unfocused by early afternoon, and the nurse's office fills with students complaining of headaches. Hale argues that these details make clear the cut is hurting the students in visible ways.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Hale (Text 2) most likely respond to the principal's claim in Text 1?
options: He would agree with it, since the story shows that students rarely ate the vegetables they were served.
He would reject it, since the story shows the students suffering effects that can be seen after the change.
He would agree with it, since the story suggests that the nurse's visits were unrelated to the meals.
He would reject it, since the story shows that the memo was written by the principal himself.
problem.explanation: 교장은 식단 변경이 아이들에게 실질적 차이가 없다고 주장한다. Text 2의 Hale은 아이들이 오후에 지치고 두통을 호소하는 장면이 식단 감축의 눈에 보이는 피해를 보여 준다고 말하므로 교장의 주장에 반대할 것이고, 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 학생들이 채소를 먹었는지는 다루지 않으며 Hale이 동의하지도 않으므로 틀리다. C는 Hale이 보건실 방문을 오히려 식단 감축과 연결하므로 틀리다. D는 메모를 교장이 썼다는 내용이 어느 글에도 없으므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The principal claims the meal change makes no real difference to the children. Hale points to scenes where students grow tired and visit the nurse with headaches, and he says these details show the cut is hurting them in visible ways, so he would reject the claim. That makes B correct. A is wrong because Text 2 doesn't discuss whether students ate the vegetables, and Hale doesn't agree with the principal. C is wrong because Hale actually links the nurse's visits to the cuts. D is wrong because neither text says the principal wrote the memo.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A school lunch coordinator learns her district deliberately reduced nutrition standards for schools serving predominantly low-income student populations

hardJudge.note: Text 2에서 Hale이 "the cut is hurting the students in visible ways"라고 명시하므로 교장의 "no real difference" 주장을 거부한다는 결론이 한 단계 추론으로 도출된다. B는 Hale의 주장을 정확히 재진술. A·C는 '동의' 방향이 틀리고 근거도 지문에 없음, D는 지문에 없는 내용으로 배제됨. 오답은 전형적 오개념(교장 발언의 일부를 가져오거나 관계를 뒤집음)이며 터무니없지 않음. 가상의 작가·작품·비평가로 저작권 문제 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 선택지 참조가 일치함. easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: Text 2의 'hurting the students in visible ways'가 교장의 'no real difference' 주장과 직접 대립해 한 단계로 풀린다. 오답 A·C는 동의 방향, D는 근거 없는 내용으로 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 easy 수준에 적합하다. 다만 정답 B가 지문 표현을 거의 그대로 옮겨 다소 쉬운 편이다.

problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Marisol directs a small wildlife rehabilitation center. Late one night, she opens the annual ledgers the board has never asked her to read.

Ledger summary (in thousands of dollars)
Year | Gifts designated for animal care | Spending on animal care | Executive salaries
2021 | 410 | 405 | 180
2022 | 520 | 390 | 240
2023 | 610 | 370 | 335

For months the board had told her that the empty medicine shelves and the owl enclosure left unrepaired were the price of a "lean period." Marisol turned that explanation over in her mind. A lean period, she reasoned, would cut the care budget only if the gifts meant for the animals had also shrunk; if those gifts grew while care spending fell, the missing money had not vanished but gone somewhere else. Running her finger across the page, she decided that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Marisol directs a small wildlife rehabilitation center. Late one night, she opens the annual ledgers the board has never asked her to read.

Ledger summary (in thousands of dollars)
Year | Gifts designated for animal care | Spending on animal care | Executive salaries
2021 | 410 | 405 | 180
2022 | 520 | 390 | 240
2023 | 610 | 370 | 335

For months the board had told her that the empty medicine shelves and the owl enclosure left unrepaired were the price of a "lean period." Marisol turned that explanation over in her mind. A lean period, she reasoned, would cut the care budget only if the gifts meant for the animals had also shrunk; if those gifts grew while care spending fell, the missing money had not vanished but gone somewhere else. Running her finger across the page, she decided that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the figures for executive salaries, which nearly doubled over three years, proved on their own that the board's raises had been undeserved.
the figures for designated gifts must have been falling, since a lean period was the only thing that could explain the bare medicine shelves.
the figures for 2021, when designated gifts exceeded care spending, offered the clearest proof that money had been redirected.
the figures for 2023, when designated gifts climbed by 90 while care spending dropped by 20, exposed the "lean period" as a cover for diversion.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Marisol의 추론은 '지정 기부금이 늘었는데 돌봄 지출이 줄었다면 돈이 다른 곳으로 갔다'는 것이다. 2023년에 지정 기부금은 520→610으로 90 늘었고, 돌봄 지출은 390→370으로 20 줄었다. 바로 그녀의 기준에 들어맞으므로 '긴축기'라는 설명은 전용을 가리기 위한 핑계라는 결론이 나온다.
A(표만 보고 추론을 무시): 급여가 늘었다는 사실은 표에 있지만, Marisol의 판단 기준은 기부금과 돌봄 지출의 관계다. 또 '부당한 인상'은 그녀가 세운 논리에서 나오지 않는다.
B(추론만 보고 표를 무시): 이사회의 '긴축기' 설명을 받아들인 것이다. 하지만 표에서 지정 기부금은 해마다 늘었다.
C(다른 항목과 잘못 연결): 2021년에는 비교할 전년도 수치가 없어 '증가와 감소'를 확인할 수 없다. 기부금이 지출을 넘은 차이도 5에 불과하다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: Marisol's test is this: if gifts meant for the animals grew while care spending fell, the money must have gone somewhere else. In 2023, designated gifts went up by 90 (520 to 610), and care spending went down by 20 (390 to 370). That fits her test exactly, so the "lean period" story looks like a cover for diverting the money.
A takes the salary column by itself and ignores her reasoning. Her test compares gifts with care spending, and nothing in it supports calling the raises "undeserved."
B accepts the board's story and ignores the table, where designated gifts rose every year.
C points to the wrong row. 2021 has no earlier year to compare it with, so you can't see a rise in gifts alongside a drop in spending. The gap that year is also only 5.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 2022→2023 지정 기부금 520→610(+90), 돌봄 지출 390→370(−20) — D의 수치 정확. Marisol의 조건문(기부금 증가+지출 감소→전용)에 정확히 부합. A는 급여 180→335(약 1.86배, '거의 두 배' 타당)라는 표 수치만 사용하고 그녀의 기준 및 '부당' 판단은 텍스트에 근거 없음. B는 텍스트 설명만 수용해 표(기부금 매년 증가)와 모순. C는 2021년 수치를 잘못 연결(전년 비교 불가, 차이 5). 참고로 2022년도 동일 기준 충족(+110/−15)하나 선택지에 없어 정답 유일성에 문제 없음. 허구 단편 각색으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D를 검산함: 2023년 지정 기부금은 520에서 610으로 90 늘었고, 돌봄 지출은 390에서 370으로 20 줄었다. Marisol이 세운 조건부 기준에 들어맞는다. 오답은 레시피 유형(표만 사용, 텍스트만 사용, 다른 항목과 잘못 연결)에 각각 정확히 대응한다. 다만 오답을 지우기가 너무 쉽다. B는 표와 바로 충돌하고, A는 'on their own'이라는 표현이 드러나게 과하며, C는 비교할 전년도 수치가 없어 바로 탈락한다. 조건문 하나를 표의 한 행에 적용하는 수준이라 추론의 방향을 뒤집는 함정이나 증거 충분성을 따지는 판단이 없다. 따라서 hard가 아니라 medium 수준으로 본다.

problem.passage:
In the novel's third chapter, Ruth Okafor, night manager at the Harlow Freight warehouse, begins to suspect the floor supervisors. Customers are billed by the declared weight printed on each manifest, but the carrier Harlow pays to haul the crates charges by the weight logged on the warehouse's own scale. Ruth notices that on Tuesdays, when supervisor Dennis Prue runs the loading dock, the scale tickets for outgoing crates come in consistently lighter than the manifests, while customer invoices still list the full manifest figures. She reasons that if Prue is deliberately recording false weights to cut the company's hauling bill while customers keep paying full rates, then the gap should not be explainable by the scale itself. Her suspicion would therefore be strengthened most directly if she found that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In the novel's third chapter, Ruth Okafor, night manager at the Harlow Freight warehouse, begins to suspect the floor supervisors. Customers are billed by the declared weight printed on each manifest, but the carrier Harlow pays to haul the crates charges by the weight logged on the warehouse's own scale. Ruth notices that on Tuesdays, when supervisor Dennis Prue runs the loading dock, the scale tickets for outgoing crates come in consistently lighter than the manifests, while customer invoices still list the full manifest figures. She reasons that if Prue is deliberately recording false weights to cut the company's hauling bill while customers keep paying full rates, then the gap should not be explainable by the scale itself. Her suspicion would therefore be strengthened most directly if she found that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the same crates, reweighed on the carrier's certified scale at the depot, matched their manifest weights rather than Prue's tickets.
the crates loaded on Tuesdays came mostly from customers who had used Harlow Freight for more than a decade.
the warehouse scale, when tested with standard weights, read about as low as Prue's tickets did on every shift.
the company's hauling bill had risen steadily over the past year as fuel surcharges increased.
problem.explanation: Ruth의 가설의 핵심 조건은 '무게 차이가 저울 탓이 아니라 Prue가 일부러 낮게 기록한 결과'라는 것이다. A: 같은 화물을 독립적인 인증 저울로 다시 쟀더니 매니페스트 무게와 일치했다면, 실제 무게는 정상이고 Prue의 티켓만 낮다는 뜻이므로 조작 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다(정답). B: 화요일 고객이 오래된 고객이라는 사실은 표면적으로 관련 있어 보이지만 무게 기록이 정확한지와는 무관하다. C: 지지하는 사실처럼 보이지만, 저울이 모든 근무조에서 낮게 나온다면 차이가 저울 오류로 설명되므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. D: 운송비가 올랐다는 것은 비용 절감 동기의 배경처럼 보이지만, 화요일 티켓이 거짓인지는 전혀 보여주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Ruth's hypothesis depends on one key condition: the gap comes from Prue deliberately recording false weights, not from the scale itself. A satisfies that condition directly. If an independent, certified scale shows that the same crates match their manifest weights, then the crates really weigh what the manifests say, and only Prue's tickets are low. That points to deliberate falsification, so A is correct. B sounds related because it involves Tuesday shipments, but how long customers have used the company says nothing about whether the weights were recorded accurately. C may look like support, but it actually pushes the other way. If the warehouse scale reads low on every shift, a faulty scale explains the gap, and that weakens the case against Prue. D is background that looks like a motive. A rising hauling bill does not show that Prue's tickets are false.

hardJudge.note: 가설(Prue의 고의 기록, 저울 탓 아님)이 명확히 제시되고, A는 독립 인증 저울로 실제 무게가 매니페스트와 일치함을 보여 티켓이 거짓임을 직접 뒷받침한다. C는 지지처럼 보이지만 모든 근무조에서 저울이 낮게 읽힌다는 사실은 차이를 저울 오류로 설명해 가설을 약화하는 반대 방향 함정으로 잘 설계됨. B는 관련 있어 보이는 무관 사실, D는 동기 배경처럼 보이지만 티켓의 진위와 무관. 사소한 점: A만으로 창고 저울 오류 가능성을 완전히 배제하진 않으나, 지문이 '화요일/Prue 근무 시에만' 차이가 난다고 이미 한정하므로 정답 판별에 모호성은 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 논리가 일관됨.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 독립된 인증 저울로 다시 잰 결과를 통해 저울 오류라는 대안 설명을 배제하므로 가설을 직접 지지한다. C는 저울이 모든 근무조에서 낮게 나오는 계통 오류를 보여 주므로 오히려 가설을 약화하고, 지지처럼 위장한 반대 방향 함정이라는 레시피 조건을 충족한다. B는 무관한 사실이고, D는 동기처럼 보이는 배경 정보에 그친다. 대안 설명을 배제하는 추론이 필요하므로 medium보다는 어렵지만, 정답이 비교적 분명해 hard 문항 중에서는 하위 수준이다.

problem.passage:
In 1494, envoys of Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, which drew a north-south line roughly 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands and assigned newly encountered lands east of it to Portugal and those west of it to Spain. The agreement is often remembered as a bold carving-up of the globe, but its authors understood remarkably little of what they were dividing. No one in 1494 could reliably measure longitude at sea, so neither crown could say exactly where the line fell, and the treaty itself left the matter to a future joint expedition that never took place. Within a few years, Portuguese navigators reached the coast of what is now Brazil and argued it lay on their side; decades later, the two kingdoms quarreled over whether the Moluccas, the prized spice islands, fell within Portugal's or Spain's sphere once the line was extended around the far side of the world. Thus a treaty meant to settle rivalry instead supplied the vocabulary in which new rivalries were argued.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: In 1494, envoys of Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, which drew a north-south line roughly 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands and assigned newly encountered lands east of it to Portugal and those west of it to Spain. The agreement is often remembered as a bold carving-up of the globe, but its authors understood remarkably little of what they were dividing. No one in 1494 could reliably measure longitude at sea, so neither crown could say exactly where the line fell, and the treaty itself left the matter to a future joint expedition that never took place. Within a few years, Portuguese navigators reached the coast of what is now Brazil and argued it lay on their side; decades later, the two kingdoms quarreled over whether the Moluccas, the prized spice islands, fell within Portugal's or Spain's sphere once the line was extended around the far side of the world. Thus a treaty meant to settle rivalry instead supplied the vocabulary in which new rivalries were argued.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Treaty of Tordesillas succeeded in preventing conflict between Spain and Portugal because it relied on a precise north-south line that both crowns accepted.
The Treaty of Tordesillas mattered mainly because it gave Portugal a legal claim to Brazil, which became the most valuable of its overseas territories.
The Treaty of Tordesillas, though intended to resolve competing claims, was so imprecise in practice that it became a framework for further disputes between Spain and Portugal.
The Treaty of Tordesillas was abandoned soon after it was signed because Spain and Portugal refused to send the joint expedition needed to measure longitude.
problem.explanation: 지문은 조약이 경쟁을 끝내려 했지만 경도 측정이 불가능해 경계선 위치가 불분명했고, 그 결과 브라질과 몰루카 제도를 둘러싼 새 분쟁의 틀이 되었다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '정확한 선'이라는 표현으로 지문의 핵심(부정확성)과 정반대이다. B는 브라질이라는 세부 사례 하나만 다루고, 브라질이 가장 가치 있는 영토였다는 내용도 지문에 없다. D는 공동 탐사가 실현되지 않았다는 세부 사실은 맞지만, 지문은 조약이 폐기됐다고 하지 않으며 오히려 수십 년 뒤에도 분쟁의 기준으로 쓰였다고 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the treaty was meant to settle rivalry, but because no one could measure longitude, the line's location stayed uncertain, and it ended up framing new disputes over Brazil and the Moluccas. That makes C correct. A says the line was "precise," which contradicts the text's central point about how imprecise it was. B focuses on a single example, Brazil, and adds a claim about its value that the text never makes. D is built on a true detail (the joint expedition never happened), but the text doesn't say the treaty was abandoned; in fact, it was still being used to argue claims decades later.

quality.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Tordesillas 1494 and Portuguese-Spanish division of colonial exploration territories

hardJudge.note: C correctly captures the main idea (treaty meant to settle rivalry, imprecise, became framework for new disputes). Historical content is accurate (1494, ~370 leagues west of Cape Verde, Brazil claim ~1500, Moluccas dispute in 1520s). A contradicts the text; B elevates a detail and adds unsupported claim; D uses a true detail but draws an unsupported conclusion. Korean and English explanations align in conclusion and letter references; English is natural with no Hangul. Two distractors (B, D) are partially text-based, A is plausible on a skim—fits medium.

advisory.note: 역사적 사실(1494년, 카보베르데 서쪽 370레구아, 실행되지 않은 공동 측량 조항, 브라질, 몰루카 분쟁)이 정확함. B·D는 지문 세부에 부분적으로 근거하고 있어 비교가 필요함. A는 쉽게 배제되지만 medium 기준 안에 들어감.

problem.passage:
Historians once attributed the French defeat in Saint-Domingue largely to yellow fever, which killed thousands of soldiers sent by Napoleon in 1802. Recent scholarship, however, emphasizes that the disease's impact was shaped by revolutionary strategy. Toussaint Louverture and his officers understood that newly arrived European troops had no immunity to tropical illnesses, so during the spring campaign they avoided decisive battles, burned coastal towns, and withdrew into the mountainous interior. This approach forced French columns to remain in the lowlands during the rainy season, when mosquito-borne fever spread fastest, while the revolutionary forces preserved their own strength. By the time Jean-Jacques Dessalines led the final offensive in 1803, the French army had been so weakened that it could no longer hold the colony.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Historians once attributed the French defeat in Saint-Domingue largely to yellow fever, which killed thousands of soldiers sent by Napoleon in 1802. Recent scholarship, however, emphasizes that the disease's impact was shaped by revolutionary strategy. Toussaint Louverture and his officers understood that newly arrived European troops had no immunity to tropical illnesses, so during the spring campaign they avoided decisive battles, burned coastal towns, and withdrew into the mountainous interior. This approach forced French columns to remain in the lowlands during the rainy season, when mosquito-borne fever spread fastest, while the revolutionary forces preserved their own strength. By the time Jean-Jacques Dessalines led the final offensive in 1803, the French army had been so weakened that it could no longer hold the colony.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Revolutionary leaders deliberately prolonged the conflict in ways that made illness far more damaging to French forces than it otherwise might have been.
Yellow fever killed so many French soldiers in 1802 that the revolutionary forces had little need to fight major battles.
Revolutionary leaders burned coastal towns mainly to deny French troops the supplies needed to march into the mountains.
Dessalines's offensive in 1803, rather than earlier campaigns, was the decisive factor in ending French control of the colony.
problem.explanation: 지문은 황열병만으로 프랑스 패배를 설명하던 기존 견해를 수정하며, 투생 루베르튀르 측이 결전을 피하고 내륙으로 후퇴해 프랑스군을 우기 저지대에 묶어 두는 전략으로 질병의 피해를 키웠다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 반박하는 옛 견해, 즉 질병만이 원인이라는 관점을 반복한다. C는 지문에 나온 도시 방화를 언급하지만 보급 차단이라는 목적은 지문에 없고, 이는 전체 요지가 아닌 세부 사항이다. D는 1803년 공세를 언급하지만, 지문은 그 공세가 앞선 전략으로 이미 약해진 군대를 상대로 성공했다고 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct because the text revises the older view that yellow fever alone defeated the French: it argues that Louverture's strategy of avoiding battle and retreating inland kept French troops in the lowlands during the rainy season, which magnified the disease's toll. B restates the older view that the text pushes back against, treating disease as the only cause. C mentions the burning of towns, but the text never says the goal was to cut off supplies, and this detail isn't the main point anyway. D refers to the 1803 offensive, but the text says it succeeded because earlier strategy had already weakened the French army.

quality.seed: history and civics — Haitian Revolution 1791-1804 and Toussaint Louverture's military strategy defeating French forces

hardJudge.note: 지문 구조(기존 견해 → 수정된 견해 → 전략의 구체적 메커니즘 → 결과)를 정확히 종합한 A가 유일하게 요지를 포괄한다. B는 "Historians once attributed"의 옛 견해를 반복하고 "little need to fight major battles"는 지문의 의도적 회피와 인과를 뒤집는다. C는 지문의 세부(도시 방화)를 쓰되 목적(보급 차단)을 지문에 없는 내용으로 바꾼 세부·왜곡 오답이다. D는 마지막 문장만 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉬우나 "so weakened that"이 앞선 전략을 결정 요인으로 지목하므로 배제된다. 역사적 사실(1802년 르클레르 원정, 황열병, 루베르튀르의 초토화·내륙 후퇴, 1803년 데살린의 최종 공세)도 통설과 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 두 단계 판단(견해 전환 인식 + 세부와 요지 구분)이 필요하고 B·D가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: A는 '질병의 영향이 혁명 전략에 의해 형성되었다'는 수정주의 요지를 정확히 바꿔 말한다. 지문의 '결전 회피·후퇴'가 'deliberately prolonged'를 뒷받침한다. B는 지문이 반박하는 옛 견해를 그대로 반복해 훑어 읽는 응시자를 끌어들인다. C는 지문에 나온 세부 사항에 근거 없는 목적을 덧붙인 선택지이고, D는 마지막 문장을 잘못 읽게 만드는 선택지다. 오답이 모두 지문 요소에 기대고 있어 medium 난이도에 맞다. 1802년 봄 루베르튀르의 초토화·내륙 후퇴 전략과 1803년 데살린의 공세는 역사적 사실과 대체로 일치한다.

problem.passage:
After the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new leaders sought to close the industrial gap with Western powers as quickly as possible. Because private investors at the time had little capital and less experience with modern machinery, the government itself built model factories, such as the Tomioka silk mill, and staffed them with hired foreign engineers. Many historians once treated these enterprises as proof that state ownership drove Japan's growth. Yet most of the model factories lost money, and in the 1880s the government sold many of them to private firms at low prices. Historian Thomas C. Smith argued that the factories' real contribution was not their output but the trained workers, technical knowledge, and proven methods they passed on to the private companies that later expanded Japanese industry.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: After the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new leaders sought to close the industrial gap with Western powers as quickly as possible. Because private investors at the time had little capital and less experience with modern machinery, the government itself built model factories, such as the Tomioka silk mill, and staffed them with hired foreign engineers. Many historians once treated these enterprises as proof that state ownership drove Japan's growth. Yet most of the model factories lost money, and in the 1880s the government sold many of them to private firms at low prices. Historian Thomas C. Smith argued that the factories' real contribution was not their output but the trained workers, technical knowledge, and proven methods they passed on to the private companies that later expanded Japanese industry.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Japan's early model factories succeeded mainly because the foreign engineers who staffed them produced goods more efficiently than private firms could.
Japan's early model factories mattered less for what they produced than for the skills and methods they handed on to later private industry.
Japan's early model factories were sold in the 1880s because private investors had finally gathered enough capital to run them profitably.
Japan's early model factories show that state ownership, rather than private enterprise, was the main force behind the country's industrial growth.
problem.explanation: 지문은 정부 모범 공장이 대부분 손실을 냈지만, Smith에 따르면 진짜 기여는 생산량이 아니라 민간 기업에 전수된 숙련 노동자·기술·방법이었다는 점을 핵심으로 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 외국인 기술자 언급을 활용했지만, 공장이 효율적으로 성공했다는 주장은 손실을 냈다는 진술과 모순된다. C는 1880년대 매각이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 매각 이유를 민간 자본 축적으로 설명하는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 과거 역사가들의 견해일 뿐, 지문은 'Yet' 이후 이 견해에 반박한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text's key point is that most of the government's model factories lost money. According to Smith, their real value was the trained workers, technical knowledge, and methods they passed on to private firms, not their output. That makes B correct. A uses the detail about foreign engineers, but saying the factories succeeded through efficiency contradicts the fact that most of them lost money. C uses the detail about the 1880s sales, but the text never says the factories were sold because private investors had gathered enough capital. D repeats the view historians "once" held, and the text pushes back on that view starting with "Yet."

quality.seed: history and civics — Meiji Restoration 1868 and Japan's rapid industrialization through government-directed modernization policy

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산 완료: 지문 마지막 문장(Smith의 주장)이 'not their output but the trained workers, technical knowledge, and proven methods'로 B와 정확히 대응. A는 '손실' 진술과 모순, C는 매각 이유가 지문에 없음, D는 'once'·'Yet'으로 반박된 과거 견해. 오답 셋 모두 지문 세부를 활용해 비교가 필요하며 D가 훑어 읽기 함정으로 작동해 medium에 적합. 역사적 사실(Tomioka 제사장, 외국인 기술자 고용, 1880년대 관영공장 불하, Thomas C. Smith의 논지) 오류 없음. 지문은 창작 요약문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: B는 지문 마지막 문장을 바꿔 쓴 것으로 정답이 명확함. A, C, D는 각각 지문 세부(외국인 기술자, 1880년대 매각, 과거 역사가들의 견해)를 활용한 그럴듯한 오답이고, 특히 D는 'Yet' 앞뒤의 전환을 파악해야 배제할 수 있어 medium 난이도에 맞음.

problem.passage:
When Tsar Alexander II issued the Emancipation Manifesto in 1861, roughly twenty-three million privately owned serfs gained personal freedom: they could marry, own property, and bring cases to court without a landlord's permission. The economic terms of the reform, however, were far less generous. Land was not handed to former serfs outright; instead, peasants received allotments that were often smaller than the plots they had farmed before, and they were required to pay for them through "redemption payments" stretched over forty-nine years. Because these payments were frequently set above the land's market value, many households fell into chronic debt. Moreover, the allotments were usually assigned to the village commune, or mir, rather than to individual families, so peasants could not easily sell their share or leave to seek work elsewhere. Historians therefore argue that although the edict ended the legal bondage of serfdom, it left much of the peasantry tied to the land by financial obligation and communal control for decades afterward.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: When Tsar Alexander II issued the Emancipation Manifesto in 1861, roughly twenty-three million privately owned serfs gained personal freedom: they could marry, own property, and bring cases to court without a landlord's permission. The economic terms of the reform, however, were far less generous. Land was not handed to former serfs outright; instead, peasants received allotments that were often smaller than the plots they had farmed before, and they were required to pay for them through "redemption payments" stretched over forty-nine years. Because these payments were frequently set above the land's market value, many households fell into chronic debt. Moreover, the allotments were usually assigned to the village commune, or mir, rather than to individual families, so peasants could not easily sell their share or leave to seek work elsewhere. Historians therefore argue that although the edict ended the legal bondage of serfdom, it left much of the peasantry tied to the land by financial obligation and communal control for decades afterward.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The 1861 reform granted former serfs new legal rights, which allowed most peasant households to leave their villages and find better-paying work.
The 1861 reform transferred land to the village commune, which historians regard as the main reason peasants gained personal freedom.
The 1861 reform freed serfs in law, but its land and payment terms kept many peasants economically constrained long after.
The 1861 reform set redemption payments below market value, but peasants resented them because the payments lasted for forty-nine years.
problem.explanation: 지문은 1861년 칙령이 법적 자유(결혼, 재산 소유, 소송)를 주었다고 인정한 뒤 '그러나' 토지 분배·상환금·공동체 소유 조건 때문에 농민이 수십 년간 경제적으로 묶여 있었다고 결론짓는다. C는 이 두 측면을 모두 담는다. A는 법적 권리 부여는 맞지만, 농민이 떠나기 어려웠다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. B는 토지가 공동체(mir)에 배정되었다는 세부는 맞지만, 그것이 개인 자유의 원인이라는 인과는 근거가 없고 오히려 제약 요인이었다. D는 49년이라는 기간은 맞지만, 상환금은 시장가치보다 '높게' 책정된 경우가 많았다고 지문은 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text grants that the 1861 edict gave serfs legal freedoms (marriage, property, court access), then turns with "however" to show how the land allotments, redemption payments, and communal control kept peasants bound for decades. C captures both halves of that argument. A is right about the new legal rights, but the text says peasants could not easily leave their villages, so it contradicts the passage. B correctly notes that land went to the commune, but the text presents this as a restriction, not as the source of personal freedom. D gets the forty-nine-year term right, but the text says payments were often set above market value, not below it.

quality.seed: history and civics — Serfdom abolition in Russia 1861 and emancipation edict's economic consequences for peasant society

hardJudge.note: 지문의 양보(법적 자유)→'however'(경제적 구속) 구조를 C가 정확히 요약. A는 '떠나기 어려웠다'와 모순, B는 인과 역전, D는 '시장가치보다 높게'를 '낮게'로 뒤집음. 세 오답 모두 부분적 사실 근거를 가져 비교 필요. 역사적 사실(1861, 약 2,300만 명, 49년 상환, mir) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 사실관계(약 2,300만 사유 농노, 49년 상환, 미르)가 정확하다. 오답 A·B·D는 모두 지문의 맞는 세부를 일부 담고 있으면서 하나씩 왜곡이 있다(이동 가능, 인과 오류, 시장가치보다 낮음). 따라서 비교해야 배제할 수 있어 medium에 맞다. C는 'however' 앞뒤 구조를 정확히 요약한다. 다만 C만 양면 구조를 갖고 있어 다소 쉽게 보일 수도 있다.

problem.passage:
The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 is often described as the meeting where European powers carved up Africa with rulers and maps. Historians such as Matthew Craven argue that this image overstates what the delegates actually did. The conference's General Act drew few borders; instead, it set out procedural rules, most notably the principle that a power claiming African coastline had to notify the other signatories and demonstrate "effective occupation" through some administrative presence. These rules did not divide the continent on their own, but they changed how claims were made: by rewarding visible control, they encouraged rival states to rush agents, treaties, and garrisons into the interior over the following two decades. In this view, the partition of Africa was less a single act performed in Berlin than a competitive process that the conference set in motion.

Historians such as Matthew Craven argue that this image overstates what the delegates actually did. The conference's General Act drew few borders; instead, it set out procedural rules, most notably the principle that a power claiming African coastline had to notify the other signatories and demonstrate "effective occupation" through some administrative presence. These rules did not divide the continent on their own, but they changed how claims were made: by rewarding visible control, they encouraged rival states to rush agents, treaties, and garrisons into the interior over the following two decades. In this view, the partition of Africa was less a single act performed in Berlin than a competitive process that the conference set in motion.
problem.question: According to the text, what is Craven's view of the Berlin Conference's role in the partition of Africa?
options: The conference divided Africa among European powers directly, and the treaties signed afterward simply confirmed borders the delegates had already drawn.
The conference had little effect on the partition, since European states had already established firm control over most of the African interior before 1884.
The conference mainly addressed disputes over coastal territory, and its rules were largely ignored once European powers moved into the interior.
The conference shaped the partition chiefly by establishing rules for making claims, which in turn spurred a later scramble for control of territory.
problem.explanation: 지문은 회의가 국경을 직접 긋기보다 '통보'와 '실효적 점유' 같은 절차 규칙을 정했고, 이 규칙이 이후 내륙 쟁탈 경쟁을 촉발했다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 통념(지도로 대륙을 나눴다는 이미지)을 그대로 진술한다. B는 회의의 영향이 작았다고 하지만, 지문은 회의가 경쟁 과정을 '작동시켰다'고 하며 1884년 이전 내륙 장악도 언급하지 않는다. C는 해안선 관련 규칙이라는 부분적 근거를 쓰지만, 그 규칙이 무시되었다는 것은 지문과 반대이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the conference drew few borders and instead set procedural rules (notification and "effective occupation"), and that these rules encouraged rivals to rush into the interior afterward, so D is correct. A restates the popular image that the text says Craven rejects. B claims the conference had little effect, but the text says it set the partition process in motion, and it never says Europeans already controlled the interior before 1884. C picks up the real detail about coastline claims, but the text says the rules drove the later scramble, which is the opposite of being ignored.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 지문 3~5문장(절차 규칙 → 실효적 점유 보상 → 내륙 쟁탈 촉발 → '회의가 작동시킨 경쟁 과정')과 정확히 일치. A는 지문이 반박하는 통념, B는 '작동시켰다'와 모순, C는 해안선 규칙이라는 실제 세부를 쓰되 '무시되었다'가 지문과 반대 — 오답 설계가 기준 충족. problem.passage:
The Mexican Constitution of 1917 authorized the government to break up large haciendas and grant the land to rural communities as ejidos, holdings that villagers could farm but could not sell. For nearly two decades, however, redistribution proceeded slowly; presidents in the 1920s transferred land mainly to quiet unrest in particular regions, and many hacendados kept their best fields through legal delays. Under President Lázaro Cárdenas (1934–1940), the pace changed dramatically: his administration distributed roughly 18 million hectares, more than all of his predecessors combined, including productive commercial estates such as the cotton plantations of La Laguna. Historians note that this expansion did not by itself make ejidos prosperous. Many recipients received land without adequate credit, irrigation, or machinery, and the national ejido bank lacked the funds to supply them, so yields on numerous ejidos lagged behind those of remaining private farms.

problem.explanationEn: The text sets slow redistribution in the 1920s against the dramatic expansion under Cárdenas, then concludes that handing out land alone didn't make ejidos prosper. Choice A is the only option that captures both parts. Choice B builds on the detail about legal delays, but it contradicts the passage, which says Cárdenas redistributed productive estates such as La Laguna. Choice C takes the motive of calming regional unrest, which the text gives for the 1920s presidents, and wrongly applies it to Cárdenas. Choice D reverses the text: the ejido bank didn't have enough funds, and yields on many ejidos lagged behind those of private farms.

problem.passage:
Historians once described the Taiping Rebellion (1850–1864) chiefly as a peasant uprising sparked by famine and heavy taxation in southern China. Hong Xiuquan, the movement's leader, did draw followers from impoverished villages, but recent scholarship emphasizes that economic hardship alone cannot explain why the revolt grew so large or fought so relentlessly. Hong, after reading Christian missionary tracts, came to believe he was the younger brother of Jesus, sent to destroy the Qing "demons" and establish a Heavenly Kingdom on earth. This millenarian promise gave converts a reason to abandon their land, pool their property in common treasuries, and accept strict codes of conduct. Because followers saw the war as the prelude to a divinely ordained new age, compromise with Qing authorities seemed not merely unwise but sinful, and the conflict became one of the deadliest of the nineteenth century, devastating rural communities across the Yangzi valley.

problem.passage:
In the summer of 1947, British lawyer Cyril Radcliffe was given roughly five weeks to draw the borders dividing British India into India and Pakistan. He had never visited the subcontinent before, worked largely from outdated maps and census figures, and consulted few people with local knowledge. Historians have often focused on these constraints to explain why his lines cut through villages, farmland, and irrigation canals. Yet a number of recent scholars argue that the haste of the drawing explains less about the violence that followed than the decision of how to announce it. Although Radcliffe finished his work before independence on August 15, the final boundaries were withheld until two days afterward. During that gap, millions of people in Punjab and Bengal did not know which country they would live in, and rumors filled the silence. These scholars contend that this uncertainty, more than any particular flaw in where the line ran, allowed local militias to organize and helped turn fear into mass killing and flight.

According to the text, what do some recent scholars regard as the more important factor behind the violence that accompanied partition?

problem.passage:
Popular accounts of the Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 often portray it as a contest of nerves won by the side that refused to blink: the United States imposed a naval "quarantine" around Cuba, and the Soviet Union, facing the threat of escalation, withdrew its nuclear missiles from the island. Historians working with declassified records from both governments have complicated this picture. They note that the settlement included terms kept from the public at the time, most notably a private American assurance that Jupiter missiles stationed in Turkey would be removed within months. Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev and President John F. Kennedy, these documents show, also exchanged letters through intermediaries in which each sought a way for the other to retreat without appearing defeated. In this view, the crisis ended less because one leader outlasted the other than because both quietly accepted concessions that allowed each to claim success.

It then uses declassified records about a secret concession (the Jupiter missiles in Turkey) and face-saving letters to conclude that both sides quietly compromised, so D is correct. A just repeats the popular view that the text goes on to challenge. B picks up the Turkey detail, but the text never says that withdrawal mattered more than the one from Cuba. problem.passage:
The phrase "triangular trade" is often used to describe Atlantic commerce from the sixteenth to the nineteenth centuries: European manufactured goods shipped to West Africa, enslaved Africans carried across the Atlantic to the Americas, and sugar, tobacco, and cotton returned to Europe. The image is tidy, and it does capture how profits in one region depended on labor and markets in the others. Historians such as David Eltis, however, have argued that the triangle misrepresents how most voyages actually operated. Shipping records show that many vessels did not complete all three legs; ships that delivered captives to the Caribbean frequently sailed home with little cargo, while plantation goods crossed the ocean on separate, specialized ships. Moreover, a large share of the trade to Brazil ran directly between Brazilian and African ports, with tobacco and rum from Bahia exchanged for captives in Angola and the Bight of Benin, bypassing Europe entirely. For these historians, the system is better understood as a web of overlapping routes than as a single closed loop.

Based on the text, what do historians like David Eltis conclude about Atlantic commerce during this period?

problem.passage:
Accounts of the Boxer Rebellion (1899–1901) often present it as a simple outburst of hatred toward foreigners. Historian Joseph Esherick, however, traced the movement's origins to the drought-stricken villages of northwestern Shandong province. There, Christian converts sometimes relied on the legal protection of foreign missionaries to win local land and lawsuit disputes. Unemployed young men, idled by failed harvests, blamed both the drought and their worsening circumstances on these converts and their foreign patrons. Esherick argues that the Boxers' hostility toward outsiders, though real, grew out of specific local grievances rather than a long-standing, nationwide rejection of everything foreign.

According to the text, what does Esherick conclude about the Boxers' anti-foreign attitudes?

problem.passage:
Popular accounts of the end of World War One often credit Germany's surrender in November 1918 to a collapse on the home front, where food shortages and naval mutinies were said to have undermined an army that remained unbeaten in the field. Military historians who have examined the final months of fighting describe a different sequence. Beginning near Amiens in August 1918, Allied forces launched a series of coordinated attacks, later called the Hundred Days Offensive, that combined tanks, aircraft, and carefully timed artillery with infantry advances. Over the following weeks, German units lost ground steadily, and hundreds of thousands of soldiers surrendered or deserted. By late September, General Erich Ludendorff himself was urging the government to seek an armistice, weeks before the unrest in German ports and cities reached its peak.

According to the text, what do military historians conclude about the reasons Germany ended the war?

problem.passage:
Historians reconstructing the Armenian genocide of 1915 have often relied on the testimony of survivors and foreign diplomats, sources that Ottoman officials at the time dismissed as exaggerated or hostile. In recent decades, however, researchers such as Taner Akçam have turned to the Ottoman state's own records, including coded telegrams exchanged between the Interior Ministry and provincial governors. These documents show officials tracking the number of Armenians deported from each district and ordering that the deportees' share of the population in their destination regions be kept below a fixed percentage. __Such instructions are difficult to reconcile with the government's wartime claim that the deportations were merely a temporary security measure to move civilians away from the front lines.__ Instead, the records suggest a deliberate demographic policy, one whose execution through forced marches into the Syrian desert led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of civilians.
