problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 샤보프스키의 실수만을 원인으로 보는 통념에 몇 달간의 시위라는 배경을 덧붙여 그 설명을 복잡하게 만들고, 다음 문장의 역사가들의 대안적 해석(therefore)으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 문장이 통념을 확인하는 것이 아니라 제한하므로 틀리다. C는 국경 검문소 장면이 나오긴 하지만 문장의 핵심은 군중 반응이 아니라 장기적 원인이다. D는 결론이 실제로는 마지막 문장에 제시되며, 밑줄 문장은 그 근거를 준비하는 역할이므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and adds the background of months of protests, which complicates the popular view that Schabowski's mistake alone opened the Wall. It then sets up the historians' alternative reading, introduced by "therefore," so A is correct. B is wrong because the sentence limits the popular explanation instead of confirming it. C is wrong because, although the border crossing appears in the sentence, its focus is on long-term causes, not the crowds' reaction. D is wrong because the historians' conclusion actually appears in the final sentence; the underlined sentence lays the groundwork for it.

quality.seed: history and civics — Fall of Berlin Wall November 1989 and peaceful dissolution of communist East German state

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 통념(샤보프스키 실수 단일 원인)을 제한하고 다음 문장의 'therefore'로 이어지는 역사가들의 해석을 준비하므로 A가 정답. B는 반대(확인), C는 첫 문장의 내용(군중 반응), D는 마지막 문장의 내용(역사가 결론)으로 각각 배제 가능하며, C·D는 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요한 오답으로 적절함. 역사적 사실(1989.11.9 기자회견, Bornholmer Strasse 최초 개방, 라이프치히 시위, Sarotte의 해석) 모두 정확. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 문제 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 'Yet' 다음에 'therefore'가 오는 구조라서 A가 분명히 정답이다. D(결론과 근거를 구분해야 함)와 C(국경 장면을 언급함)는 그럴듯한 오답이고, B는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 사실관계는 대체로 맞다. 다만 사로트는 우연성도 강조하므로 'merely set the timing'은 그의 주장을 다소 단순화한 표현이다. 그래도 문항의 타당성을 해칠 정도는 아니다.

problem.passage:
When the International Military Tribunal convened in Nuremberg in November 1945, defense lawyers for the accused Nazi leaders raised a pointed objection: many of the charges, especially "crimes against peace," had not been clearly defined as crimes under international law when the acts were committed. Punishing defendants for them, the lawyers argued, amounted to applying law retroactively. __The tribunal answered that treaties such as the 1928 Kellogg-Briand Pact, which Germany had signed, had already renounced aggressive war, so the defendants could not claim they had acted without notice that such conduct was unlawful.__ Historians still debate whether this reasoning fully settled the matter, but its influence is clear: the principles the tribunal applied were affirmed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1946 and later shaped the statutes of courts such as the International Criminal Court.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: When the International Military Tribunal convened in Nuremberg in November 1945, defense lawyers for the accused Nazi leaders raised a pointed objection: many of the charges, especially "crimes against peace," had not been clearly defined as crimes under international law when the acts were committed. Punishing defendants for them, the lawyers argued, amounted to applying law retroactively. __The tribunal answered that treaties such as the 1928 Kellogg-Briand Pact, which Germany had signed, had already renounced aggressive war, so the defendants could not claim they had acted without notice that such conduct was unlawful.__ Historians still debate whether this reasoning fully settled the matter, but its influence is clear: the principles the tribunal applied were affirmed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1946 and later shaped the statutes of courts such as the International Criminal Court.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a criticism of the tribunal that historians later used to challenge its legitimacy.
It explains how the tribunal responded to a legal challenge described in the previous sentences.
It describes a treaty that the defense lawyers cited to show the charges were applied retroactively.
It identifies the main reason the United Nations later affirmed the tribunal's principles.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장들에서 변호인단이 제기한 소급 적용 반론에 대해 재판소가 켈로그-브리앙 조약을 근거로 내놓은 답변이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이 문장을 재판소에 대한 비판으로 보지만, 실제로는 재판소 측의 논리이고 역사가들의 논쟁은 그다음 문장에 나온다. C는 조약이 언급된다는 점은 맞지만, 그 조약을 인용한 것은 변호인이 아니라 재판소이며 소급 적용 반론을 반박하는 데 쓰였다. D는 마지막 문장의 UN 승인과 연결 짓지만, 지문은 밑줄 문장의 논리를 UN이 승인한 이유로 제시하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence gives the tribunal's reply to the defense's objection about retroactive law, which appears in the sentences before it, so B is correct. A treats the sentence as a criticism of the tribunal, but it is actually the tribunal's own reasoning, and the historians' debate only comes up in the next sentence. C is right that a treaty is mentioned, but it was the tribunal, not the defense, that cited it, and it was used to counter the retroactivity claim. D ties the sentence to the UN's affirmation in the last sentence, but the text never says this reasoning is why the UN affirmed the principles.

quality.seed: history and civics — Nuremberg Trials 1945-1946 and prosecuting Nazi war crimes establishing international law precedent

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "The tribunal answered that..."로 앞선 변호인단 반론에 대한 응답임이 명확하여 B가 정답. 사실 확인: 1945년 11월 뉘른베르크 개정, 1928년 켈로그-브리앙 조약 독일 서명, 1946년 UN 총회 결의 95(I)로 뉘른베르크 원칙 승인, ICC 규정에 영향 — 모두 정확. C(조약 언급은 맞으나 인용 주체 오류), D(마지막 문장과 연결하나 인과 미제시)는 부분적 근거를 가진 오답이고 A도 역사가 논쟁 언급 때문에 말이 됨. 해설 한·영 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 난이도 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 역사적 사실(1945년 11월 개정, 켈로그-브리앙 조약에 독일 서명, 1946년 UN 총회 결의 95(I)로 확인, ICC에 영향)은 정확함. 오답 A·C·D는 각각 역사가 논쟁, 조약 언급, UN 승인처럼 지문에 실제로 있는 요소를 끌어와 구성되어 있어 정독하지 않으면 헷갈릴 수 있음. 다만 C는 비교적 쉽게 배제될 수 있음. 전반적으로 medium 난이도에 적합함.

problem.passage:
In January 1968, Alexander Dubček became leader of Czechoslovakia's Communist Party and soon announced a program he called "socialism with a human face." Press censorship was relaxed, citizens openly debated the party's past abuses, and reformers drafted plans to allow greater economic independence for enterprises. Many historians have described these months, later known as the Prague Spring, as an attempt to abandon communism altogether. __Yet the party's own Action Program of April 1968 explicitly reaffirmed Czechoslovakia's membership in the Warsaw Pact and the Communist Party's leading role in society.__ Soviet leaders nonetheless viewed the reforms as a threat to their control of Eastern Europe, and in August 1968 Warsaw Pact troops invaded the country, ending the experiment within a single night.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In January 1968, Alexander Dubček became leader of Czechoslovakia's Communist Party and soon announced a program he called "socialism with a human face." Press censorship was relaxed, citizens openly debated the party's past abuses, and reformers drafted plans to allow greater economic independence for enterprises. Many historians have described these months, later known as the Prague Spring, as an attempt to abandon communism altogether. __Yet the party's own Action Program of April 1968 explicitly reaffirmed Czechoslovakia's membership in the Warsaw Pact and the Communist Party's leading role in society.__ Soviet leaders nonetheless viewed the reforms as a threat to their control of Eastern Europe, and in August 1968 Warsaw Pact troops invaded the country, ending the experiment within a single night.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that explains why Soviet leaders decided that a military invasion of Czechoslovakia was necessary.
It presents a detail illustrating how far the reforms of the Prague Spring extended beyond the relaxation of press censorship.
It presents a claim that historians have used to argue that the reformers intended to leave the Warsaw Pact.
It presents information that complicates a characterization of the reformers' goals described in the previous sentence.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 앞 문장에서 소개한 '프라하의 봄은 공산주의를 완전히 버리려는 시도였다'는 역사가들의 해석과 달리 개혁 강령이 바르샤바 조약과 공산당의 지도적 역할을 재확인했음을 보여 준다. 따라서 그 해석을 복잡하게 만드는 D가 정답이다. A는 소련의 침공을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 개혁이 체제에 충실했음을 보여 주며 침공 이유는 다음 문장에서 따로 제시된다. B는 개혁의 범위를 다루지만, 밑줄 문장은 개혁이 넓어졌음이 아니라 그 한계를 보여 준다. C는 바르샤바 조약을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장의 내용은 조약 탈퇴 의도와 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," which signals a contrast with the previous sentence, where historians describe the Prague Spring as an attempt to abandon communism. By showing that the Action Program reaffirmed Warsaw Pact membership and the party's leading role, it complicates that characterization, so D is correct. A mentions the invasion, but the underlined sentence actually shows the reformers staying loyal to the system; the Soviet reasoning comes in the next sentence. B is about the reach of the reforms, but the sentence shows their limits, not how far they went. C mentions the Warsaw Pact, but the sentence suggests the opposite of an intent to leave it.

quality.seed: history and civics — Prague Spring 1968 and Czechoslovak democratic reform crushed by Soviet military intervention

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞 문장의 역사가 해석(공산주의 전면 포기 시도)과 대비되어 그 특징짓기를 복잡하게 하므로 D가 명확히 정답. A는 다음 문장의 'nonetheless'와 연결해 그럴듯하게 보이고, B·C는 문장 속 세부(개혁 범위, 바르샤바 조약)를 부분적으로 참조하여 비교가 필요함. 역사적 사실(1968년 1월 둡체크 취임, 4월 행동강령의 바르샤바 조약·당 지도적 역할 재확인, 8월 침공) 모두 정확. "within a single night"은 침공 자체가 하룻밤에 이뤄진 점을 가리키는 수사적 단순화로 허용 범위. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 선택지 참조 일치.

advisory.note: D가 맞다. 'Yet'이 앞 문장의 역사가 해석과 대비됨을 보여 준다. 1968년 4월 행동강령의 바르샤바 조약 재확인, 공산당 지도적 역할 재확인, 8월 침공은 모두 사실이다. '많은 역사가가 공산주의를 완전히 버리려는 시도로 묘사했다'는 서술은 실제 사학계 주류 해석과는 다소 거리가 있다. 다만 글 안의 설정 진술로 쓰였으므로 허용 범위로 본다. C는 밑줄 문장과 정반대 내용이라 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. A는 바로 다음 문장(소련의 침공)과 이어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보여 매력적인 오답 역할을 한다. 중간 난이도에 대체로 맞다.

problem.passage:
In June 1215, rebellious English barons compelled King John to accept a written charter later known as Magna Carta. Many popular accounts celebrate the document as an early guarantee of liberty for all English people. Historian Ralph Turner and others, however, emphasize that most of its clauses addressed narrow baronial grievances, such as the fees the king could demand when an heir inherited land. __Yet even these self-interested provisions mattered beyond their immediate purpose, because by setting them down in writing, the barons established that the king's demands could be measured against a fixed text rather than left to his discretion.__ That principle, more than any single clause, is why later generations could invoke the charter against monarchs whom its authors never imagined.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In June 1215, rebellious English barons compelled King John to accept a written charter later known as Magna Carta. Many popular accounts celebrate the document as an early guarantee of liberty for all English people. Historian Ralph Turner and others, however, emphasize that most of its clauses addressed narrow baronial grievances, such as the fees the king could demand when an heir inherited land. __Yet even these self-interested provisions mattered beyond their immediate purpose, because by setting them down in writing, the barons established that the king's demands could be measured against a fixed text rather than left to his discretion.__ That principle, more than any single clause, is why later generations could invoke the charter against monarchs whom its authors never imagined.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It qualifies the historians' point by identifying a broader significance in the very clauses they characterize as narrow.
It rejects the historians' point by showing that the charter's clauses were written to protect all English people.
It supports the popular accounts by showing that the barons intended the charter to serve future generations.
It illustrates the historians' point by giving an example of a fee the king could demand from an heir.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 역사가들이 '좁은 귀족적 불만'이라 본 조항들을 인정하면서도, 그것을 문서로 고정했다는 점에서 더 넓은 의의가 있다고 덧붙이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 '역사가 주장을 부정'한다고 하지만 밑줄 문장은 조항이 자기이익적(self-interested)임을 인정하므로 틀리다. C는 넓은 의의를 언급한 점은 맞지만, 마지막 문장이 작성자들이 후대를 상상하지 못했다고 밝히므로 '의도'라는 부분이 틀리다. D는 상속 수수료 예시가 앞 문장에 이미 나왔고, 밑줄 문장은 예시가 아니라 의의를 제시한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," accepting the historians' view that the clauses were self-interested while adding that writing them down gave them a wider significance, so A is correct. B is wrong because the sentence concedes the provisions were self-interested rather than denying the historians' point. C notices the broader significance but wrongly claims the barons intended it; the final sentence says the authors never imagined later uses. D is wrong because the inheritance-fee example appears in the previous sentence, and the underlined sentence offers an interpretation, not an example.

quality.seed: history and civics — Magna Carta 1215 and English baronial constraints on royal authority through written charter

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 역사가들의 '좁은 조항' 평가를 수용하면서 문서화 자체의 더 넓은 의의를 덧붙이므로 A(한정·보완)가 정확하다. B는 자기이익성을 인정하는 문장을 '부정'으로 오독, C는 마지막 문장('never imagined')과 모순되는 '의도'를 주장, D는 예시가 앞 문장에 있음을 간과해야 선택되므로 세 오답 모두 비교 판단이 필요하다. 'Yet'의 양보 구조 파악 + 마지막 문장과의 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium에 적합. 역사적 사실(1215년 6월, 존 왕, 상속 시 부과금, Ralph Turner의 해석) 오류 없음. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 'Yet'으로 역사가들의 주장을 인정하면서 범위를 한정하는 구조이다. C는 마지막 문장과 연결해야 배제되고, B·D도 각각 그럴듯한 근거가 있어 medium 난이도에 맞다. 역사적 사실(1215년, 상속세 relief, Ralph Turner)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Historians often credit Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press, developed in Mainz around 1440, with placing books in the hands of ordinary Europeans for the first time. The claim has some basis: by 1500, presses across Europe had produced millions of volumes, and the cost of a book fell sharply compared with that of a hand-copied manuscript. __Yet surviving sales records show that most early printed books were Latin religious and legal texts, priced well beyond the means of the farmers and laborers who made up the majority of the population.__ For several generations, then, the press mainly enlarged the libraries of clergy, lawyers, and wealthy merchants. Only later, as cheap pamphlets and vernacular works multiplied, did printing begin to reach readers outside these groups.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Historians often credit Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press, developed in Mainz around 1440, with placing books in the hands of ordinary Europeans for the first time. The claim has some basis: by 1500, presses across Europe had produced millions of volumes, and the cost of a book fell sharply compared with that of a hand-copied manuscript. __Yet surviving sales records show that most early printed books were Latin religious and legal texts, priced well beyond the means of the farmers and laborers who made up the majority of the population.__ For several generations, then, the press mainly enlarged the libraries of clergy, lawyers, and wealthy merchants. Only later, as cheap pamphlets and vernacular works multiplied, did printing begin to reach readers outside these groups.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It supplies evidence that the cost of printed books fell more slowly than historians have generally assumed.
It introduces evidence that qualifies a widely held view of the press's immediate effects.
It identifies the kinds of texts that later made printing accessible to farmers and laborers.
It offers evidence that the number of books produced by 1500 has been overstated.
problem.explanation: 글은 구텐베르크 인쇄기가 곧바로 일반인에게 책을 보급했다는 통념을 제시하고 일부 근거를 인정한 뒤, 밑줄 문장(Yet)에서 초기 책이 라틴어 종교·법률서였고 가격도 높았다는 증거로 그 견해를 제한한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 가격 언급이 있어 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 가격 하락 자체를 인정하며 하락 속도를 문제 삼지 않는다. C는 나중에 접근성을 넓힌 것이 팸플릿과 자국어 저작이라 했으므로 밑줄 문장의 라틴어 문헌과 반대다. D는 생산량 수치를 반박하지 않으므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first presents the common view that Gutenberg's press immediately brought books to ordinary people and grants it some support. The underlined sentence, introduced by "Yet," then gives evidence that early books were Latin religious and legal texts priced too high for most people, which limits that view, so B is correct. A is tempting because price is mentioned, but the text accepts that prices fell sharply and never questions how fast they fell. C is wrong because the text says it was later pamphlets and vernacular works, not the Latin texts in the underlined sentence, that reached wider readers. D is wrong because the sentence never challenges the production figures.

quality.seed: history and civics — Gutenberg printing press invention circa 1440 and mass production of books democratizing knowledge

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해 앞서 인정한 통념(일반인에게 책 보급)을 판매 기록 증거로 제한하므로 B가 정확. A는 가격 하락 자체를 지문이 인정하므로 배제되고, C는 '나중에' 접근성을 넓힌 팸플릿·자국어 저작과 혼동을 유도하며, D는 생산량 수치를 반박하지 않음. 오답들이 지문의 세부 내용(가격, 수량, 후기 변화)을 부분적으로 차용해 비교가 필요하고 담화 표지+문맥 확인의 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(1440년경 마인츠, 1500년까지 수백만 권, 초기 인쇄물 다수가 라틴어 종교·법률서)에 오류 없음. 독창적 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 밑줄 문장은 Yet으로 시작해 앞에서 일부 인정한 통념을 제한한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 가격 언급을 근거로 삼고 C는 책의 종류를 근거로 삼아 부분적으로 그럴듯하지만, 지문과 비교하면 배제된다. D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 말은 된다. 지문의 통념은 '처음으로'라고 표현돼 있고, 'immediate effects'는 'For several generations'와 'Only later'를 통해 추론해야 한다. 두 단계 판단이 필요하므로 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
When the Philippine-American War began in 1899, many US commanders expected Filipino resistance to collapse once Emilio Aguinaldo's conventional army was defeated in open battle. By late 1899, Aguinaldo had indeed disbanded his regular units, and some American officials declared the war effectively over. __Yet Aguinaldo had ordered his forces not to surrender but to split into small guerrilla bands that could blend into villages and strike without warning.__ Over the following two years, these bands drew on local networks of support, prompting US forces to adopt harsher measures such as relocating rural populations into guarded zones. Historians therefore argue that the war's most consequential phase began, rather than ended, with the breakup of the Filipino regular army.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: When the Philippine-American War began in 1899, many US commanders expected Filipino resistance to collapse once Emilio Aguinaldo's conventional army was defeated in open battle. By late 1899, Aguinaldo had indeed disbanded his regular units, and some American officials declared the war effectively over. __Yet Aguinaldo had ordered his forces not to surrender but to split into small guerrilla bands that could blend into villages and strike without warning.__ Over the following two years, these bands drew on local networks of support, prompting US forces to adopt harsher measures such as relocating rural populations into guarded zones. Historians therefore argue that the war's most consequential phase began, rather than ended, with the breakup of the Filipino regular army.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a development that undercuts an earlier assumption and sets up the account of the conflict that follows.
It introduces a development that explains why US officials concluded that the conflict had come to an end.
It introduces a development that shows how US forces successfully adapted their tactics to Filipino resistance.
It introduces a development that historians cite to argue that Aguinaldo's army was defeated in open battle.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 미군 지휘관들이 기대했던 '정규군이 패하면 저항이 무너질 것'이라는 가정을 뒤집는다. 또한 이어지는 게릴라전과 미군의 강경책에 대한 서술, 그리고 결정적 국면이 정규군 해체와 함께 시작됐다는 결론으로 이어지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 반대이다. 관리들이 전쟁이 끝났다고 선언한 것은 밑줄 문장보다 앞에 나오며, 밑줄 문장은 그 결론을 반박한다. C는 미군의 대응을 언급하긴 하지만, 그 대응은 밑줄 다음 문장에 나오고 '성공'으로 평가되지도 않는다. D는 정규군 해체라는 앞부분 사실을 밑줄 문장의 기능과 혼동한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," and it overturns the commanders' assumption that resistance would collapse once the regular army was beaten. It also sets up the rest of the text: the guerrilla campaign, the harsher US measures, and the historians' conclusion that the key phase began when the regular army broke up. That makes A correct. B gets it backward: officials declared the war over before the underlined sentence, and that sentence challenges their conclusion. C points to the US response, but that response comes in the next sentence, and the text never calls it successful. D mixes up the earlier fact that the regular army was disbanded with what the underlined sentence actually does.

quality.seed: history and civics — Philippine-American War 1899-1902 and United States colonial counterinsurgency amid nationalist resistance

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞선 가정(정규군 패배=저항 붕괴)과 관리들의 종전 선언을 뒤집고, 이후 게릴라전·강경책·역사가 결론으로 이어지는 서술을 준비한다. A가 정확히 이 기능을 기술함. B는 인과 방향이 반대, C는 다음 문장 내용이며 '성공' 평가 없음, D는 앞부분 사실과 밑줄 기능을 혼동. 역사적 사실(1899년 개전, 1899년 말 정규군 해산 및 게릴라전 전환, 재집결 구역 정책) 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 정답·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 대조 인식+후속 전개 연결의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 B·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 'Yet'으로 시작하는 밑줄 문장이 앞선 가정을 뒤집고 이후 서술을 이끄는 구조이므로 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 앞뒤 문장의 내용을 끌어와 그럴듯해 보이고, D는 비교적 약하지만 말은 된다. 역사적 사실(1899년 11월 게릴라전 전환, 주민 집단 이주 정책)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Japan's victory over Russia in 1905 is often described as the first modern defeat of a European great power by an Asian nation, but historian Rotem Kowner cautions against treating the war's outcome as having ______ European imperial dominance. Russia lost a fleet and a war, yet it kept its vast territorial empire, and Britain, France, and other colonial powers held on to their Asian possessions for decades afterward. What the war did change, Kowner argues, was perception: nationalist writers from Cairo to Calcutta cited Japan's success as proof that European supremacy was not inevitable.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Japan's victory over Russia in 1905 is often described as the first modern defeat of a European great power by an Asian nation, but historian Rotem Kowner cautions against treating the war's outcome as having ______ European imperial dominance. Russia lost a fleet and a war, yet it kept its vast territorial empire, and Britain, France, and other colonial powers held on to their Asian possessions for decades afterward. What the war did change, Kowner argues, was perception: nationalist writers from Cairo to Calcutta cited Japan's success as proof that European supremacy was not inevitable.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: challenged
dismantled
inspired
questioned
problem.explanation: Kowner는 전쟁 결과를 어떤 식으로 보는 것을 경계하고, 바로 뒤에 러시아가 제국을 유지했고 식민 열강도 수십 년간 영토를 지켰다는 근거를 든다. 따라서 그가 부정하는 주장은 유럽 지배가 '해체되었다'는 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 지문 마지막 문장에서 전쟁이 유럽 우월성이 필연적이라는 인식을 흔들었다고 하므로 실제로 일어난 일에 해당하고, Kowner가 경계할 대상이 아니다. C는 전쟁이 유럽 지배를 '고무했다'는 뜻이 되어 Japan의 승리라는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Kowner warns against one particular reading of the war, and the text immediately backs him up: Russia kept its empire, and the colonial powers held their Asian territories for decades. So the claim he rejects is that the war dismantled European dominance, which makes B correct. A and D describe what the war actually did, since the last sentence says it shook the belief that European supremacy was inevitable, so Kowner would have no reason to caution against them. C would mean the war inspired European dominance, which makes no sense given that an Asian nation won.

quality.seed: history and civics — Russo-Japanese War 1904-1905 and Asian military victory over European imperial power

hardJudge.note: 검산: 'cautions against treating the outcome as having ___' 뒤에 러시아가 제국을 유지했고 식민 열강이 수십 년간 영토를 지켰다는 근거가 이어지므로, Kowner가 부정하는 것은 유럽 지배가 '해체되었다(dismantled)'는 해석이다. 마지막 문장이 전쟁이 인식을 흔들었다고 하므로 A(challenged)·D(questioned)는 실제로 일어난 일이 되어 '경계' 대상과 모순, C(inspired)는 의미 불합리. 정답 B 확정. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 선택지 참조가 일치하며 한글 혼입 없음. 'cautions against'의 부정적 틀 + 뒤 근거 문장 연결 + 마지막 문장과의 대비라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 A·D가 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이므로 medium 적합. Rotem Kowner는 실제 러일전쟁 연구 역사학자로 사실 오류 없음, 지문은 창작 서술로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: B가 정답임이 확인됨. 근거는 러시아가 영토 제국을 유지했고 식민 열강도 수십 년간 아시아 영토를 지켰다는 내용이며, 이는 유럽 지배가 '해체되었다'는 해석을 부정함. A(challenged)와 D(questioned)는 마지막 문장의 인식 변화와 부분적으로 맞아 그럴듯한 오답임. 이를 배제하려면 Kowner가 경계하는 대상(실제 지배의 종식)과 실제로 일어난 일(인식 변화)을 구분해야 하므로 medium 난이도에 적합함. C는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 말은 됨.

problem.passage:
In the final years of the Qing Dynasty, the official Zhao Erfeng led campaigns in the Kham region of eastern Tibet that went far beyond earlier imperial practice. Previous Qing administrators had generally been content to oversee the region's hereditary chieftains and the powerful monasteries allied with them. Zhao, by contrast, aimed to ______ these local rulers altogether: under the policy known as gaitu guiliu, he abolished their positions and installed magistrates appointed by the imperial court in their place.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the final years of the Qing Dynasty, the official Zhao Erfeng led campaigns in the Kham region of eastern Tibet that went far beyond earlier imperial practice. Previous Qing administrators had generally been content to oversee the region's hereditary chieftains and the powerful monasteries allied with them. Zhao, by contrast, aimed to ______ these local rulers altogether: under the policy known as gaitu guiliu, he abolished their positions and installed magistrates appointed by the imperial court in their place.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: discipline
restrain
supplant
counsel
problem.explanation: 지문은 Zhao가 지방 수장들의 직위를 폐지하고 그 자리에 조정이 임명한 관리를 앉혔다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '대체하다, 밀어내고 그 자리를 차지하다'는 뜻의 C(supplant)가 가장 정확하다. 또 'altogether'와 'by contrast'는 단순히 감독하던 이전 방식과 다르다는 점을 강조하는데, C가 이 대비에 맞는다. A(discipline)와 B(restrain)는 억압적 통치라는 분위기에는 맞지만, 수장들을 그 자리에 둔 채 통제한다는 뜻이어서 직위를 없앴다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. D(counsel)는 조언한다는 뜻이라 강경한 정책 전환과 어울리지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says Zhao abolished the chieftains' positions and put court-appointed magistrates in their place, so the blank needs a word meaning "replace." That is C (supplant). The words "by contrast" and "altogether" also set Zhao apart from earlier officials who only oversaw the chieftains, and C fits that contrast. A (discipline) and B (restrain) match the harsh tone, but each one means controlling the chieftains while they keep their posts, and the text says those posts were eliminated. D (counsel) means giving advice, which doesn't fit this forceful break from past practice.

quality.seed: history and civics — Qing Dynasty suppression of Tibetan autonomy and Chinese religious assimilation policies twentieth century

hardJudge.note: 지문 역사 사실(조이풍·캄·改土歸流) 정확. 콜론 뒤 '직위 폐지 + 조정 임명 관리로 교체'가 'supplant'를 명확히 지지하며, 'by contrast'·'altogether'로 이전의 단순 감독과 대비. A·B는 억압적 어조에 부분적으로 맞아 비교 배제 필요, D도 문법상 성립. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 표준 medium 적합.

advisory.note: Zhao Erfeng의 gaitu guiliu 정책은 역사적 사실과 맞다. 'altogether'와 'in their place'를 함께 봐야 supplant를 고를 수 있다. discipline과 restrain은 통제라는 뜻이 그럴듯해 보이는 함정이어서 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Beginning in 1791, William Wilberforce introduced bills in the British Parliament to abolish the transatlantic slave trade, and each time the bills were defeated. Supporters outside Parliament then gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures on petitions and organized a boycott of sugar grown by enslaved people, showing lawmakers how many ordinary Britons opposed the trade. In 1807, after years of this public pressure, Parliament finally passed the Slave Trade Act by a large majority. These events suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Beginning in 1791, William Wilberforce introduced bills in the British Parliament to abolish the transatlantic slave trade, and each time the bills were defeated. Supporters outside Parliament then gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures on petitions and organized a boycott of sugar grown by enslaved people, showing lawmakers how many ordinary Britons opposed the trade. In 1807, after years of this public pressure, Parliament finally passed the Slave Trade Act by a large majority. These events suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Wilberforce's early bills failed mainly because he stopped presenting them after 1791.
the petitions and the boycott had little connection to the eventual vote in Parliament.
the 1807 law passed because most lawmakers had supported abolition from the very beginning.
the campaign outside Parliament helped change lawmakers' votes on the slave trade.
problem.explanation: 지문은 법안이 반복적으로 부결된 뒤 청원과 불매운동으로 대중의 압력이 쌓였고, 그 결과 1807년 법안이 큰 표차로 통과되었다고 서술하므로 D가 가장 논리적인 결론이다. A는 법안을 '매번' 제출했다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다. B는 '수년간의 대중 압력 이후' 통과되었다는 연결을 부정한다. C는 초기 법안들이 부결되었다는 사실과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says Wilberforce's bills were defeated again and again, then public petitions and a boycott built pressure, and after that Parliament passed the act by a large majority, so D is the most logical conclusion. A contradicts the text, which says he introduced bills repeatedly and they were defeated each time. B ignores the text's link between years of public pressure and the final vote. C conflicts with the fact that the early bills failed, which shows most lawmakers did not support abolition at first.

quality.seed: history and civics — Abolitionist movement in nineteenth-century Britain and William Wilberforce's parliamentary campaigns ending transatlantic slave trade

hardJudge.note: 지문이 "after years of this public pressure"로 인과 관계를 직접 제시하므로 한 단계 추론으로 D 도출 가능. 오답 A·B·C는 각각 지문의 명시적 진술(매번 제출·부결, 압력 이후 통과, 초기 부결)과 직접 충돌하는 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯하되 배제 가능. 역사적 사실(1791 첫 법안, 1807 Slave Trade Act, 설탕 불매·청원)도 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: 역사적 사실(1791년 첫 법안 부결, 청원·설탕 불매운동, 1807년 압도적 가결)이 정확함. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나 있고, 오답들은 지문과 바로 모순되는 전형적 오독이라 easy 난이도에 맞음.

problem.passage:
On July 14, 1789, crowds in Paris stormed the Bastille, a fortress-prison long associated with the king's power to jail people without trial. When the crowd broke in, they found only seven prisoners inside, and none of them was being held for political reasons. Even so, the people of Paris spent the following months taking the building apart stone by stone, and some of its stones were carved into small models of the fortress and sent to towns across France. Because freeing a large number of prisoners clearly was not what made the event important, historians conclude that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: On July 14, 1789, crowds in Paris stormed the Bastille, a fortress-prison long associated with the king's power to jail people without trial. When the crowd broke in, they found only seven prisoners inside, and none of them was being held for political reasons. Even so, the people of Paris spent the following months taking the building apart stone by stone, and some of its stones were carved into small models of the fortress and sent to towns across France. Because freeing a large number of prisoners clearly was not what made the event important, historians conclude that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the event mattered mainly because it destroyed a symbol of the king's unchecked authority.
the event mattered mainly because it gave the crowd weapons it later used in battle.
the event mattered mainly because it emptied a prison that held many of the king's critics.
the event mattered mainly because it gave Paris valuable building stone for new projects.
problem.explanation: 지문은 바스티유가 왕의 재판 없는 투옥 권력과 연결된 장소였고, 안에 죄수가 7명뿐이었는데도 사람들이 건물을 허물고 그 돌로 모형을 만들어 전국에 보냈다고 설명한다. 따라서 이 사건이 중요했던 이유는 왕의 무제한 권력을 나타내는 상징을 무너뜨렸다는 데 있으므로 A가 정답이다. C는 정치범이 한 명도 없었다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다. B는 무기에 관한 정보가 지문에 전혀 없어 근거가 없다. D는 돌을 실용적인 건축 자재로 썼다는 뜻이지만, 지문에서 돌은 상징적인 모형으로 만들어졌으므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the Bastille stood for the king's power to jail people without trial. Even though only seven prisoners were inside, Parisians tore the building down and sent carved models of it across France. That shows the event mattered because it destroyed a symbol of the king's unchecked authority, so A is correct. C doesn't fit, because the passage says none of the prisoners was being held for political reasons. B has no support, since the passage never mentions weapons. D is wrong because the stones were turned into symbolic models rather than used for practical building.

quality.seed: history and civics — Storming of the Bastille July 1789 and French Revolutionary symbolic destruction of royal absolutist authority

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 완료: 지문이 바스티유를 왕의 재판 없는 투옥 권력의 상징으로 제시하고, 죄수 7명뿐·정치범 없음에도 건물을 허물고 돌로 모형을 만들어 전국에 보냈다는 단서가 직접 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 A 도출. B(무기)는 지문에 언급 없음, C(왕의 비판자 다수 수감)는 지문과 정면 모순, D(건축 자재)는 돌이 상징적 모형으로 쓰였다는 내용과 어긋남. 역사적 사실(1789.7.14, 죄수 7명, 비정치범, 돌로 모형 제작·각지 발송)도 통설과 일치. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 한글 혼입 없음. 오답들이 '돌', '감옥'이라는 지문 소재를 활용한 전형적 오개념이라 easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 역사적 사실(죄수 7명, 정치범 없음, 팔루아가 돌로 모형을 만들어 전국에 배포)은 정확하다. 실제로 군중은 화약을 얻으려고 바스티유에 갔으므로 B가 역사적으로 완전히 틀린 것은 아니다. 하지만 지문 근거가 없고 빈칸 앞 논리(상징성)와도 맞지 않아 오답으로 처리하는 데 문제가 없다. 한 단계 추론으로 풀리고 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나므로 easy에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In 1838 and 1839, the United States government forced thousands of Cherokee people to leave their homelands in the Southeast and move west to Indian Territory, a journey later called the Trail of Tears. Some historians argue that the removal was not simply the result of federal policy but was strongly pushed by people in Georgia who wanted Cherokee land, especially after gold was discovered there in 1829. According to this view, pressure from Georgia settlers and officials was a major force behind the removal.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' view?
problem.stimulus: In 1838 and 1839, the United States government forced thousands of Cherokee people to leave their homelands in the Southeast and move west to Indian Territory, a journey later called the Trail of Tears. Some historians argue that the removal was not simply the result of federal policy but was strongly pushed by people in Georgia who wanted Cherokee land, especially after gold was discovered there in 1829. According to this view, pressure from Georgia settlers and officials was a major force behind the removal.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' view?
options: Records show that many Cherokee families brought livestock, tools, and household goods with them on the journey west.
Letters from the 1830s show Georgia lawmakers repeatedly urging Congress to remove the Cherokee so the state could distribute their land to settlers.
Accounts show that the winter of 1838–1839 was unusually cold along parts of the route, causing many illnesses and deaths.
Documents show that after arriving in Indian Territory, the Cherokee Nation rebuilt its government and adopted a new constitution.
problem.explanation: 역사가들의 주장은 조지아 주민과 관리들의 땅에 대한 압력이 강제 이주의 주요 원인이었다는 것이다. B는 조지아 의원들이 땅을 얻으려고 의회에 이주를 반복해서 요구했다는 내용이라 그 압력을 직접 보여 주므로 정답이다. A와 C는 이주 과정에서 있었던 일(가져간 물건, 날씨)을 다룰 뿐 이주가 왜 일어났는지는 말하지 않는다. D는 이주 이후의 일이라 원인에 관한 주장과 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The historians claim that pressure from Georgia settlers and officials who wanted Cherokee land was a major cause of the removal. B directly shows that pressure: Georgia lawmakers repeatedly pushed Congress for removal so the state could hand out the land, so B is correct. A and C describe what happened during the journey (the goods people carried, the weather), but they don't explain why the removal happened. D is about events after the removal, so it has nothing to do with a claim about its cause.

quality.seed: history and civics — Trail of Tears 1838-1839 and forced Indian removal policy displacing Cherokee Nation westward

hardJudge.note: 지문의 주장(조지아 주민·관리의 토지 압력이 주요 원인)과 B(조지아 의원들이 토지 분배를 위해 의회에 이주를 반복 촉구)가 직접 대응함. 오답 A·C는 이주 과정, D는 이주 이후의 사실로 원인 주장과 무관하되 주제적으로 그럴듯함. 역사적 사실(1829년 조지아 금 발견, 1838–39년 이주, 서부 재건·헌법 채택)에 오류 없음. 한·영 해설 결론·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 지문의 주장과 바로 맞닿아 있다(조지아의 압력과 토지 욕구). 오답들은 이주 원인을 다루지 않아 그럴듯하지만 주장과 관계없는 관련 사실이다. 역사적 사실(1829년 다로네가 금 발견, 1838–39년 강제 이주)도 정확하다. 쉬운 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Between 1811 and 1817, groups of English textile workers known as Luddites broke into workshops at night and smashed stocking frames and other machines. The Luddites are often remembered as people who simply hated new technology. However, some historians argue that the Luddites were not against machines in general. Instead, these historians claim, the workers attacked machines mainly to protest employers who used the machines to cut wages and replace skilled workers with cheaper, less trained labor.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' claim?
problem.stimulus: Between 1811 and 1817, groups of English textile workers known as Luddites broke into workshops at night and smashed stocking frames and other machines. The Luddites are often remembered as people who simply hated new technology. However, some historians argue that the Luddites were not against machines in general. Instead, these historians claim, the workers attacked machines mainly to protest employers who used the machines to cut wages and replace skilled workers with cheaper, less trained labor.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' claim?
options: Records show that the Luddites carried out most of their attacks at night, when workshops were empty and guards were few.
Records show that the Luddites destroyed machines in many different towns, spread across several English counties.
Records show that the Luddites often left alone machines owned by employers who paid standard wages, while breaking machines owned by employers who had lowered pay.
Records show that the Luddites destroyed many more machines in 1812 than in any other single year of the rebellion.
problem.explanation: 역사가들의 주장은 러다이트가 기계 자체가 아니라 임금을 깎는 고용주에게 항의하려고 기계를 부쉈다는 것이다. C는 정상 임금을 주는 고용주의 기계는 그대로 두고 임금을 낮춘 고용주의 기계만 부쉈다고 하므로, 공격 대상이 기계가 아니라 고용주의 행태에 따라 정해졌음을 직접 보여 준다. A는 공격 시간과 방식만 말할 뿐 동기를 알려 주지 않는다. B는 반란이 넓은 지역에 퍼졌다는 것만 보여 주고, 왜 공격했는지는 드러나지 않는다. D는 공격이 가장 많았던 해를 말할 뿐 기계를 부순 이유와 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The historians claim the Luddites attacked machines to protest employers who cut wages, not because they hated machines in general. C supports this directly: the workers left alone machines owned by fair-paying employers and broke those owned by employers who lowered pay. That means their targets depended on how employers behaved, not on the machines themselves. A only describes when and how the attacks happened, not why. B shows that the rebellion was widespread but tells you nothing about its motive. D gives the busiest year of attacks, which also doesn't explain why the machines were destroyed.

quality.seed: history and civics — Luddite rebellion 1811-1817 and English textile workers' mechanized machinery destruction resisting industrial displacement

hardJudge.note: 지문 사실(1811~1817 러다이트, 스타킹 프레임 파괴, 임금·숙련공 대체 항의라는 역사학계 해석)은 정확. 정답 C는 '고용주 행태에 따라 표적 선택'이라는 직접 증거로 주장을 뒷받침하며, A·B·D는 시간·지역·연도 등 동기와 무관한 사실로 전형적 오답. 한·영 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 개념(주장-증거 직접 연결), 한 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: Luddite 시기(1811–1817)와 양말 직조기(stocking frame) 언급은 역사적 사실과 맞음. 오답 A/B/D는 모두 동기와 무관한 사실 진술로, 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯함. 단일 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합.

problem.passage:
Bdelloid rotifers, microscopic animals found in ponds and damp moss, have reproduced without males for tens of millions of years. Asexual lineages usually accumulate harmful mutations and lack the genetic variety that sexual reproduction provides, so biologists long puzzled over how bdelloids persisted. Part of the answer may lie in their ability to survive complete drying. When its habitat dries, a bdelloid curls into a dormant state, and its DNA breaks into fragments. Once water returns, the animal repairs its genome. Researchers have found that during this repair, the rotifer's cells appear to stitch in foreign DNA, including genes taken up from bacteria and fungi. Roughly a tenth of a bdelloid's active genes seem to have come from such sources, and some help break down unfamiliar compounds. By surviving repeated drying, bdelloids may thus gain a supply of new genetic material that partly makes up for the variety they lose by not mating.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Bdelloid rotifers, microscopic animals found in ponds and damp moss, have reproduced without males for tens of millions of years. Asexual lineages usually accumulate harmful mutations and lack the genetic variety that sexual reproduction provides, so biologists long puzzled over how bdelloids persisted. Part of the answer may lie in their ability to survive complete drying. When its habitat dries, a bdelloid curls into a dormant state, and its DNA breaks into fragments. Once water returns, the animal repairs its genome. Researchers have found that during this repair, the rotifer's cells appear to stitch in foreign DNA, including genes taken up from bacteria and fungi. Roughly a tenth of a bdelloid's active genes seem to have come from such sources, and some help break down unfamiliar compounds. By surviving repeated drying, bdelloids may thus gain a supply of new genetic material that partly makes up for the variety they lose by not mating.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Bdelloid rotifers survive drying mainly because genes from bacteria and fungi protect their DNA from breaking apart.
Bdelloid rotifers acquire foreign genes mainly to break down unfamiliar compounds in pond and moss habitats.
Bdelloid rotifers show that asexual animals face no real disadvantage from the harmful mutations biologists expected.
Bdelloid rotifers' recovery from drying may give them new genetic material that helps offset their lack of sexual reproduction.
problem.explanation: 지문은 무성생식하는 담륜충이 어떻게 오래 존속했는가라는 의문을 제시하고, 건조 후 DNA를 복구하는 과정에서 외래 유전자를 받아들여 짝짓기 부재로 잃는 다양성을 일부 보충할 수 있다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 인과를 뒤집었다. 외래 유전자가 DNA 파손을 막는 것이 아니라, DNA가 파손된 뒤 복구할 때 외래 유전자가 들어간다. B는 일부 유전자의 기능이라는 세부만 부풀려 획득의 목적처럼 진술한다. C는 지문이 무성생식의 불리함을 인정하고 '일부' 보충된다고만 말한다는 점과 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The text asks how asexual bdelloids have lasted so long. It answers that while repairing their DNA after drying out, they take in foreign genes, which may partly make up for the genetic variety they lose by not mating. That makes D correct. A reverses cause and effect: the foreign genes don't keep the DNA from breaking. They get inserted while broken DNA is being repaired. B blows up one detail (what some of the genes do) into the reason the genes are acquired. C conflicts with the text, which accepts that asexual reproduction has drawbacks and says they are only partly offset.

quality.seed: life science — Bdelloid rotifer desiccation tolerance and horizontal gene transfer from bacterial DNA acquisition

hardJudge.note: 지문의 의문 제기(무성생식의 존속)→건조·DNA 복구 중 외래 유전자 유입→다양성 일부 보충이라는 구조를 D가 정확히 요약함. A는 인과 역전, B는 세부 과장, C는 '일부' 보충이라는 한정과 모순되어 모두 배제 가능하며, A·B는 지문의 실제 요소를 담고 있어 비교가 필요한 medium 수준에 적합. 담륜충의 수평 유전자 전달(~10%), 건조 후 DNA 복구 가설 등 과학적 내용도 통설과 부합. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: 사실관계: 담륜충의 건조 내성, 외래 유전자 수평 전달(활성 유전자의 약 8~10%), 무성생식 역설은 실제 연구 결과와 일치함. A·B는 지문 세부 내용을 그럴듯하게 왜곡해 비교가 필요한 매력적 오답이고, C는 과장된 선택지임. 중간 난이도에 적합함.

problem.passage:
The Pacific lamprey, a jawless fish that spends part of its adult life at sea, feeds by fastening its round, tooth-lined oral disc to the side of a larger fish and rasping through the skin with its tongue. Such wounds would normally close quickly as the host's blood clotted, cutting off the meal. Researchers analyzing secretions from the lamprey's buccal glands, however, have identified a mix of proteins that interfere with several steps of the host's clotting process at once: some block platelets from clumping, others break down fibrinogen, and still others relax blood vessel walls. Because each compound targets a different stage, the host cannot easily compensate by strengthening any single defense, and blood keeps flowing for the hours or even days that the lamprey remains attached.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: The Pacific lamprey, a jawless fish that spends part of its adult life at sea, feeds by fastening its round, tooth-lined oral disc to the side of a larger fish and rasping through the skin with its tongue. Such wounds would normally close quickly as the host's blood clotted, cutting off the meal. Researchers analyzing secretions from the lamprey's buccal glands, however, have identified a mix of proteins that interfere with several steps of the host's clotting process at once: some block platelets from clumping, others break down fibrinogen, and still others relax blood vessel walls. Because each compound targets a different stage, the host cannot easily compensate by strengthening any single defense, and blood keeps flowing for the hours or even days that the lamprey remains attached.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Pacific lamprey relies mainly on its tooth-lined oral disc and rasping tongue, rather than chemical secretions, to keep its host's wounds open while it feeds.
The Pacific lamprey can feed on a host for long periods because its saliva contains several compounds that together disrupt clotting at multiple points.
The Pacific lamprey's saliva works chiefly by relaxing the host's blood vessel walls, which prevents platelets from forming clots at the wound.
The Pacific lamprey's hosts are able to resist its feeding by strengthening one of their clotting defenses, which limits how long the lamprey stays attached.
problem.explanation: 지문은 칠성장어가 상처를 내는 방식을 소개한 뒤, 침샘 분비물 속 여러 단백질이 응고 과정의 서로 다른 단계를 동시에 방해하여 숙주가 대응하지 못하고 오랫동안 피가 흐른다는 점을 중심으로 전개된다. 따라서 B가 핵심을 가장 잘 요약한다. A는 구강판과 혀를 언급한 점은 맞지만, 상처 유지의 주된 수단이 화학 분비물이라는 지문의 요지와 반대된다. C는 혈관 이완이라는 세부 사항을 단일한 주된 기전으로 과장하며, 여러 단계를 동시에 겨냥한다는 핵심을 놓친다. D는 지문에 나오는 '하나의 방어 강화'를 뒤집어, 숙주가 실제로 저항에 성공한다고 잘못 진술한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first describes how the lamprey makes a wound. It then focuses on how proteins in its gland secretions block different stages of clotting at the same time, so the host can't compensate and blood keeps flowing for a long time. That makes B the best summary. A mentions the disc and tongue correctly, but it says chemical secretions aren't the main way the wound stays open, which is the opposite of the text's point. C takes one detail, the relaxing of blood vessel walls, and treats it as the single main mechanism, so it misses the idea that several stages are targeted together. D turns the text's point upside down: the text says hosts cannot easily resist by strengthening a single defense, not that they succeed in doing so.

hardJudge.note: 지문의 중심 내용(여러 단백질이 응고의 서로 다른 단계를 동시에 방해하여 장시간 섭식 가능)을 B가 정확히 요약함. '침(saliva)'은 지문의 '협측샘 분비물'을 자연스럽게 바꿔 표현한 것으로 문제없음. A·C는 지문 세부(구강판·혀, 혈관 이완)를 부분적으로 반영하되 주된 기전을 잘못 설정해 비교가 필요하고, D는 마지막 문장을 뒤집은 그럴듯한 오답으로 medium 기준 충족. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조와 일치하며 영어 해설은 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 칠성장어 협측샘 분비물의 항응고·혈관확장·섬유소용해 작용은 알려진 사실과 부합함.

advisory.note: B는 지문의 흐름(상처 형성 → 다단계 항응고 → 장시간 섭식)을 정확히 요약한다. C는 지문의 세부 사항을 사용하지만 그 범위를 과장해 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답이다. A와 D는 지문 표현을 활용했지만 요지를 뒤집은 오답이다. 이 둘은 꼼꼼히 읽으면 비교적 쉽게 배제되므로 medium 하한에 가깝지만 허용 범위다. 지문은 '분비물'이라고 하고 B는 'saliva(침)'로 바꿔 말했는데, 이는 수용 가능한 패러프레이즈다.

problem.passage:
The bluestreak cleaner wrasse, a small fish found on Indo-Pacific reefs, sets up "cleaning stations" where larger fish come to have parasites picked from their skin and gills. The arrangement is usually described as a simple trade: the client fish gets rid of parasites, and the wrasse gets a meal. Field observations by behavioral ecologist Redouan Bshary, however, revealed a complication. __Wrasse actually prefer to eat the protective mucus that coats a client's skin rather than the parasites, and biting off mucus makes the client flinch.__ Bshary found that clients respond by chasing a wrasse that bites them or by swimming off to a different station, and that wrasse being watched by waiting clients bite less often. The partnership, in other words, holds together not because the two species' interests line up perfectly, but because clients can punish cheating.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

C는 고객이 왜 찾아오는지를 설명하지 않으며, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 고객이 겪는 비용을 보여 준다. D는 관찰될 때 무는 횟수가 줄어든다는 내용에 기대고 있지만, 지문에서는 선호가 사라진다고 하지 않고 무는 빈도가 줄어든다고만 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence shows a conflict of interest: the wrasse would rather eat the client's mucus, which hurts the client. The rest of the text then explains that the partnership stays stable because clients punish this cheating, so A is correct. B is wrong because the text complicates the usual "simple trade" view but never says the harm is greater than the benefit, and it concludes that the relationship holds together. C is wrong because the sentence describes a cost to clients, not a reason they visit stations. D is wrong because the text says wrasse bite less often when being watched, not that their preference goes away.

problem.passage:
The American pika, a small relative of the rabbit, lives on rocky alpine slopes in western North America. Because it does not hibernate and carries a dense coat suited to cold, the pika can die after only a few hours of exposure to temperatures around 25°C. Researchers have therefore long predicted that warming summers would push pikas upslope and eliminate low-elevation populations. __Yet surveys in parts of the Columbia River Gorge have found pikas thriving at sites barely above sea level, where summer afternoons regularly exceed that threshold.__ Investigating these sites, ecologist Johanna Varner found that the animals shelter in deep talus and moss-covered rock, where temperatures stay cool, and shift their foraging to early mornings and evenings. Such findings suggest that the pika's vulnerability to warming depends less on air temperature alone than on whether its local terrain offers cool refuges.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

It presents an observation that seems at odds with an expectation, prompting the investigation described afterward.
It identifies the specific temperature at which pikas begin to suffer harmful effects from overheating.

C is wrong because the threshold temperature is given in the earlier sentence, and the underlined sentence only refers back to it. D is wrong because the text never says pikas aren't sensitive to heat; it concludes that cool refuges let them cope with that sensitivity.

problem.passage:
Many tree frogs begin life as tadpoles in small ponds, where they breathe through gills and feed on algae. Researchers studying one species found that young tadpoles can survive fairly high levels of certain pollutants in the water. As the tadpoles approach metamorphosis, however, this tolerance drops sharply. During this stage, their bodies are rebuilding lungs, skin, and legs for life on land, and much of their energy goes into these changes rather than into defending against toxins. The researchers concluded that the weeks of transformation from water to land are the period when these frogs are most vulnerable to polluted water.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Many tree frogs begin life as tadpoles in small ponds, where they breathe through gills and feed on algae. Researchers studying one species found that young tadpoles can survive fairly high levels of certain pollutants in the water. As the tadpoles approach metamorphosis, however, this tolerance drops sharply. During this stage, their bodies are rebuilding lungs, skin, and legs for life on land, and much of their energy goes into these changes rather than into defending against toxins. The researchers concluded that the weeks of transformation from water to land are the period when these frogs are most vulnerable to polluted water.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tree frog tadpoles survive polluted water better than adult frogs because gills filter out toxins.
Tree frogs leave ponds early in life mainly to escape the pollutants found in the water.
Tree frogs are especially sensitive to water pollution while they are changing from tadpoles into land-dwelling frogs.
Tree frog tadpoles depend on algae for food, so pollution harms them chiefly by killing algae.
problem.explanation: 지문은 어린 올챙이는 오염물질에 잘 견디지만 변태가 가까워지면 내성이 급격히 떨어지며, 물에서 육지로 바뀌는 시기가 가장 취약하다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 C가 중심 내용이다. A는 성체 개구리와 비교하거나 아가미가 독소를 거른다는 내용이 지문에 없다. B는 개구리가 오염을 피하려고 연못을 떠난다는 근거 없는 인과를 제시한다. D는 조류를 먹는다는 세부 사항을 근거 없이 오염 피해의 원인으로 확대했다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says young tadpoles tolerate pollutants fairly well, but this tolerance drops sharply near metamorphosis, and it concludes that the change from water to land is the most vulnerable period. That makes C the main idea. A compares tadpoles with adult frogs and says gills filter toxins, but the text says neither of these things. B claims frogs leave ponds to escape pollution, which is a cause the text never gives. D takes a minor detail (eating algae) and turns it into an explanation for pollution harm that the text doesn't support.

problem.passage:
For many years, biologists assumed that female songbirds chose mates mainly by judging the quality of a male's song or the brightness of his feathers. Recent studies of species such as the great reed warbler and the house sparrow suggest that something less visible also matters. Females in these species often pair with males whose immune genes, known as major histocompatibility complex (MHC) genes, differ from their own. Researchers think females may detect these differences through scent. Chicks whose parents have different MHC genes tend to inherit a wider range of immune defenses, which can help them resist more kinds of disease.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Researchers think females may detect these differences through scent. Female songbirds pick mates whose immune genes match their own so that their chicks will stay healthy.
Female songbirds use scent mainly to locate food and safe nesting sites for their chicks.

problem.explanationEn: The text says that besides song and feathers, females often choose males whose MHC immune genes differ from their own, and that this gives chicks wider disease protection, so D is correct. A restates the older assumption the text introduces only to move beyond it. B says females prefer matching genes, but the text says they prefer different ones. C changes the role of scent to finding food and nests, which the text never mentions.

problem.passage:
Each winter, a team of herpetologists surveying a cluster of vernal pools in northern California reported that Pacific chorus frogs (Pseudacris regilla) at the site were thriving: on the first rainy nights of the season, hundreds of males gathered and called in near-perfect synchrony, and females laid thousands of eggs within a span of about ten days. The team's annual summary described this explosive breeding as "a reliable sign of a healthy population." Yet the same summaries also noted, almost in passing, that in four of the past six years the pools had dried out in early spring, weeks before tadpoles could complete metamorphosis, and that in those years few or no juvenile frogs were found leaving the pools.

Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the team's characterization of the frog population?
problem.stimulus: Each winter, a team of herpetologists surveying a cluster of vernal pools in northern California reported that Pacific chorus frogs (Pseudacris regilla) at the site were thriving: on the first rainy nights of the season, hundreds of males gathered and called in near-perfect synchrony, and females laid thousands of eggs within a span of about ten days. The team's annual summary described this explosive breeding as "a reliable sign of a healthy population." Yet the same summaries also noted, almost in passing, that in four of the past six years the pools had dried out in early spring, weeks before tadpoles could complete metamorphosis, and that in those years few or no juvenile frogs were found leaving the pools.
problem.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the team's characterization of the frog population?
options: It is supported by the team's observation that hundreds of males called in near-perfect synchrony on the first rainy nights of the season.
It may be overly optimistic, because the breeding activity it relies on does not by itself indicate that new frogs are actually being added to the population.
It may be overly pessimistic, because the early drying of the pools shows that the frogs have adapted to complete development more quickly than expected.
It reflects the general principle that amphibian populations are healthiest in habitats with permanent, year-round sources of water.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 연구팀은 동시 번식을 '건강한 개체군의 신호'라 했지만, 6년 중 4년은 웅덩이가 변태 전에 말라 어린 개구리가 거의 나오지 않았다. 번식 행동(산란)과 실제 개체 보충 사이의 어긋남으로 보아 그 평가는 지나치게 낙관적일 수 있다.
A: 지문에 나온 관찰을 그대로 가져왔을 뿐, 그 관찰이 결론을 뒷받침하지 못한다는 핵심 어긋남을 놓쳤다.
C: 어긋남을 반대로 해석했다. 어린 개구리가 거의 없었다는 것은 빠른 적응이 아니라 번식 실패를 보여 준다.
D: 영구 수원에 관한 일반 상식일 뿐 지문에 근거가 없다. 오히려 이 종은 계절성 웅덩이에서 번식한다.
problem.explanationEn:
B is correct. The team calls the explosive breeding "a reliable sign of a healthy population," but its own summaries report that in four of the past six years the pools dried out before tadpoles could finish metamorphosis, and few or no juveniles came out. A lot of egg-laying doesn't show that new frogs are actually joining the population, so the team's verdict may be too optimistic.
A is wrong because it just repeats an observation from the text. It ignores that this observation doesn't support the team's conclusion.
C is wrong because it reads the mismatch backward. Few or no juveniles points to failed breeding, not to faster development.
D is wrong because it's a general claim about amphibians that the text never makes. In fact, these frogs breed in seasonal pools.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 연구팀의 표면적 평가("healthy population")와 '거의 지나가듯' 언급된 실제 결과(6년 중 4년 변태 전 건조, 어린 개구리 거의 없음)를 병치하며, 정답 B는 번식 활동과 실제 개체 보충(recruitment)의 어긋남을 인식해야만 도출된다. A는 지문 관찰을 그대로 옮긴 오답, C는 방향을 뒤집은 오답, D는 지문 밖 일반론으로 적절히 설계됨. 사실 관계(Pseudacris regilla의 vernal pool 폭발적 번식)도 타당하며, 부분적 근거(4/6년)를 바탕으로 평가의 신뢰성을 가늠해야 하므로 hard 특성에 부합한다.

advisory.note: 팀이 내세운 평가('건강한 개체군')와, 지나가듯 언급된 번식 실패 데이터 사이의 어긋남을 알아채야 풀린다. 다만 지문이 'almost in passing', 'Yet' 같은 표현으로 어긋남을 꽤 드러내 놓고 있고, C와 D는 쉽게 걸러진다. 그래서 hard 문항으로서는 아래쪽 경계에 있다.

problem.passage:
Most frogs lay their eggs in water, where they hatch into swimming tadpoles that later turn into adults. The coqui frog of Puerto Rico skips that stage entirely. Females lay clutches of about two dozen eggs on land, often in curled leaves or the bases of bromeliads. Each embryo develops fully inside its egg, breathing through a thin tail full of blood vessels, and after roughly three weeks a tiny froglet breaks out using a temporary egg tooth. Because coquis do not need ponds or streams to breed, they avoid the fish and insect larvae that eat tadpoles, and they can reproduce far from standing water. Land, however, has its own dangers. Eggs laid out of water can dry out quickly, so a male coqui stays with each clutch for most of its development, pressing his moist body against the eggs and fending off egg-eating invertebrates. In experiments where researchers removed the guarding males, many clutches dried out or were eaten.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Because coquis do not need ponds or streams to breed, they avoid the fish and insect larvae that eat tadpoles, and they can reproduce far from standing water. Land, however, has its own dangers. Eggs laid out of water can dry out quickly, so a male coqui stays with each clutch for most of its development, pressing his moist body against the eggs and fending off egg-eating invertebrates. problem.explanation:
정답 C: 지문은 육상 직접발생 덕분에 물속 포식자를 피하고 물이 없는 곳에서도 번식할 수 있다는 이점을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 'however' 이후에는 알이 마르기 쉬워 수컷이 알을 지켜야 한다는 새로운 위험을 설명한다. 이 두 흐름을 모두 포괄하는 것이 C이다.
A(과잉축소): 꼬리로 호흡한다는 것은 발생 과정을 보여 주는 세부사실 하나일 뿐 전체 요지가 아니다.
B(과잉확장): 지문은 코키 한 종만 다루며, 열대 개구리 전반이나 연못 번식 종과의 경쟁은 언급하지 않는다. 또 알이 마를 위험이 있어 물기에 여전히 의존하므로 '물이 필요 없어졌다'는 말도 지문과 어긋난다.
D(범위 혼합): 넓은 주장(물속 포식자 회피)과 세부사실(수컷의 알 보호)을 잘못 연결했다. 수컷이 지키는 이유는 알의 건조와 알을 먹는 무척추동물 때문이며, 물고기나 곤충 유충은 코키가 피하는 위험이다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct. The text first explains what coquis gain by developing on land: they avoid the fish and insect larvae that eat tadpoles, and they can breed away from water. Then, starting with "however," it describes a new danger. Eggs on land can dry out, so males have to guard them. C is the only choice that covers both halves of the text.
A narrows the scope too much. Breathing through the tail is just one detail about how the embryo develops.
B stretches the scope too far. The text is about one species, not tropical frogs in general, and it never compares coquis with pond-breeding frogs. Also, coqui eggs can still dry out, so the frogs haven't fully escaped their need for water.
D mixes up the broad claim and the details. Males guard the eggs to keep them from drying out and to drive off egg-eating invertebrates. Fish and insect larvae are the dangers the coquis avoid by breeding on land, not the reason males stand guard.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 이점(물속 포식자 회피, 물 없는 곳 번식) → 'however' 전환 → 새로운 위험(건조, 무척추동물) → 수컷 보호 → 실험 근거의 구조를 가지며, C가 이 전환 구조 전체를 정확히 포괄한다. A는 세부사실 과잉축소, B는 '열대 개구리 전반'·'경쟁'·'물 필요 없음'으로 과잉확장(건조 위험과도 모순), D는 보호 이유를 잘못 연결한 매력적 오답으로 기능한다. 생물학적 사실(코키 직접발생, 약 3주, 수컷 보호, 난치, 제거 실험)도 알려진 내용과 부합. 정답을 얻으려면 단순 사실 찾기가 아니라 'however' 전후의 대조 구조와 D의 인과 오류를 구별해야 하므로 medium을 넘는다.

advisory.note: 'however'를 기준으로 이점에서 새로운 위험으로 넘어가는 구조를 통합해야 정답 C를 고를 수 있다. D는 앞부분의 위험(물고기·유충)과 뒷부분의 대응(수컷의 보호)을 잘못 이은 그럴듯한 함정이고, C는 추상적으로 바꿔 말해 범위를 맞추는 판단이 필요하다. 오답 B가 지나치게 넓혀 말한 것은 비교적 쉽게 걸러진다.

problem.passage:
During its development, the tiny soil worm Caenorhabditis elegans produces 1,090 cells, but exactly 131 of them die on schedule before the worm reaches adulthood. Biologist H. Robert Horvitz found that a gene called ced-3 is required for these deaths: in worms with a working copy of ced-3, the 131 cells die as expected. A researcher studying a new strain of worms observes that all 131 of these cells survive into adulthood. Based on Horvitz's finding, the researcher can reasonably conclude that the worms in the new strain most likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: During its development, the tiny soil worm Caenorhabditis elegans produces 1,090 cells, but exactly 131 of them die on schedule before the worm reaches adulthood. Biologist H. Robert Horvitz found that a gene called ced-3 is required for these deaths: in worms with a working copy of ced-3, the 131 cells die as expected. A researcher studying a new strain of worms observes that all 131 of these cells survive into adulthood. Based on Horvitz's finding, the researcher can reasonably conclude that the worms in the new strain most likely ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produce far fewer than 1,090 cells during development.
have an extra working copy of the ced-3 gene.
lose additional cells beyond the usual 131 before adulthood.
lack a working copy of the ced-3 gene.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 131개 세포가 죽으려면 ced-3 유전자가 필요하다. 새 계통에서는 131개 세포가 모두 살아남았으므로, 그 계통에는 제대로 작동하는 ced-3가 없을 가능성이 가장 높다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 세포 생존과 관련이 없는 전체 세포 수 이야기이고, B는 ced-3가 작동하면 세포가 죽어야 하므로 관찰과 반대다. C는 세포가 더 많이 죽는다는 뜻이라 관찰 결과와 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says ced-3 is required for the 131 cells to die. In the new strain, all 131 cells survive, so the most likely explanation is that these worms lack a working ced-3 gene, which makes D correct. A is about the total number of cells produced, which doesn't explain why the scheduled deaths didn't happen. B can't be right because a working ced-3 would cause the cells to die. C says even more cells die, which is the opposite of what the researcher observed.

quality.seed: life science — Soil nematode Caenorhabditis elegans programmed cell death and apoptosis genetic pathway model organism

hardJudge.note: Single explicit premise (ced-3 required for the 131 deaths) + one observation (all 131 survive) → one-step inference to D. Horvitz/ced-3 facts are accurate (1,090 cells, 131 deaths, ced-3 required). Distractors are plausible misconceptions (B reverses causation; C contradicts observation; A shifts to total cell count) but readily eliminated. Korean and English explanations agree on conclusion and letter references, no Korean in English explanation. Original wording, no copyright concern.

advisory.note: ced-3가 세포 사멸의 필요조건이므로 세포가 모두 살아남았다면 ced-3가 제대로 작동하지 않을 가능성이 가장 높다. 'most likely'라는 표현이 엄밀한 역추론 부담을 덜어 준다. 1,090개 중 131개 세포 사멸과 Horvitz의 ced-3 연구는 사실과 맞다. 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy 난이도에 맞다. B는 관계를 거꾸로 읽은 학생이 고를 만한 오답이다.

problem.passage:
When a honey bee worker returns to the hive after finding food, she often performs a "waggle dance" on the vertical surface of the honeycomb. The angle of her waggle run relative to straight up on the comb matches the angle between the food source and the sun's position in the sky. For example, a run pointing straight up tells other bees to fly directly toward the sun. Because the sun moves across the sky during the day, a researcher reasoned that if a bee danced for the same flower patch in the morning and again in the late afternoon, the angle of her waggle run would ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: When a honey bee worker returns to the hive after finding food, she often performs a "waggle dance" on the vertical surface of the honeycomb. The angle of her waggle run relative to straight up on the comb matches the angle between the food source and the sun's position in the sky. For example, a run pointing straight up tells other bees to fly directly toward the sun. Because the sun moves across the sky during the day, a researcher reasoned that if a bee danced for the same flower patch in the morning and again in the late afternoon, the angle of her waggle run would ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: shift between the two dances, since the direction of the food compared with the sun would have changed.
stay exactly the same between the two dances, since the flower patch itself would not have moved.
shift between the two dances, since bees in the hive would have forgotten the earlier dance by afternoon.
stay exactly the same between the two dances, since the dance shows only how far away the food is.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 춤의 각도는 먹이 방향과 태양 위치 사이의 각도와 같다. 태양은 하루 동안 움직이므로, 꽃밭이 그대로여도 태양 기준 각도가 달라져 춤의 각도도 바뀐다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 각도가 태양 기준이라는 규칙을 무시하고 꽃밭이 고정된 것만 본다. C는 각도가 바뀐다는 결론은 맞지만 지문에 없는 '기억 상실'을 이유로 든다. D는 춤이 거리만 나타낸다고 하지만 지문은 춤의 각도가 방향을 전달한다고 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the angle of the waggle run matches the angle between the food and the sun. The sun moves during the day, so even though the flower patch stays put, the food's angle relative to the sun changes, and the dance angle changes with it. That makes A the answer. B ignores the rule that the angle is measured from the sun and looks only at the fact that the patch hasn't moved. C correctly says the angle shifts, but it gives a reason that's not in the passage: bees forgetting the earlier dance. D says the dance shows only distance, but the passage explains that the dance angle tells other bees which direction to fly.

quality.seed: life science — Honey bee waggle dance navigation and solar compass directional communication symbolic language evolution

hardJudge.note: 지문이 '각도 = 먹이와 태양 사이 각도', '태양은 하루 동안 이동'이라는 두 단서를 명시적으로 제공하여 한 단계 추론으로 A가 도출된다. B·D는 태양 기준 규칙을 간과한 전형적 오개념, C는 결론은 맞지만 근거가 지문 밖이라 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 벌의 춤 사실관계(von Frisch)와 일치하며, 해설 한·영 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 자연스러움. 저작권 의심 없음. easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 태양 기준 각도라는 규칙 하나만 알면 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. B는 그럴듯한 오개념이다. C는 결론은 맞지만 이유가 틀린 선택지이고, D는 지문과 직접 모순된다. 지문 속 사실(태양 기준 각도, 위쪽=태양 방향)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
For decades, climate models treated Arctic permafrost largely as a passive store of carbon, frozen soil that would thaw gradually and release its methane and carbon dioxide at a slow, predictable pace. Field research led by ecologist Merritt Turetsky has complicated that picture. Her team found that in ice-rich permafrost, thawing does not simply proceed downward a few centimeters each year; instead, melting ground ice can cause the land surface to collapse abruptly, forming slumps and ponds known as thermokarst. These waterlogged depressions create oxygen-poor conditions in which microbes produce methane, a greenhouse gas far more potent than carbon dioxide over short periods.

Because the warming caused by this methane can in turn thaw more permafrost, abrupt thaw strengthens a feedback loop that models built around gradual thaw tend to underestimate. Turetsky and her colleagues estimate that although abrupt thaw is likely to affect less than a fifth of the permafrost region, it could roughly double the climate impact projected from gradual thaw alone. Their conclusion is not that the Arctic has already passed a point of no return, but that projections ignoring sudden ground collapse may substantially understate how much permafrost will contribute to future warming.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus:
For decades, climate models treated Arctic permafrost largely as a passive store of carbon, frozen soil that would thaw gradually and release its methane and carbon dioxide at a slow, predictable pace. Field research led by ecologist Merritt Turetsky has complicated that picture. Her team found that in ice-rich permafrost, thawing does not simply proceed downward a few centimeters each year; instead, melting ground ice can cause the land surface to collapse abruptly, forming slumps and ponds known as thermokarst. These waterlogged depressions create oxygen-poor conditions in which microbes produce methane, a greenhouse gas far more potent than carbon dioxide over short periods.

Because the warming caused by this methane can in turn thaw more permafrost, abrupt thaw strengthens a feedback loop that models built around gradual thaw tend to underestimate. Turetsky and her colleagues estimate that although abrupt thaw is likely to affect less than a fifth of the permafrost region, it could roughly double the climate impact projected from gradual thaw alone. Their conclusion is not that the Arctic has already passed a point of no return, but that projections ignoring sudden ground collapse may substantially understate how much permafrost will contribute to future warming.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because thermokarst ponds lack oxygen, microbes in permafrost regions now emit more methane than carbon dioxide, making methane the main driver of Arctic warming.
Because abrupt thaw affects less than a fifth of the permafrost region, its contribution to Arctic warming is likely to remain minor compared with that of gradual thaw.
Because permafrost has begun collapsing abruptly, the Arctic has likely passed a point beyond which further warming cannot be prevented.
Because sudden ground collapse can intensify a self-reinforcing cycle of thaw and warming, models assuming only slow thaw probably underestimate permafrost's climate effect.
problem.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 얼음이 많은 영구동토층의 급격한 붕괴(thermokarst)가 메탄 방출을 늘려 되먹임 고리를 강화하므로, 점진적 해빙만 가정한 모델이 영구동토층의 기후 영향을 과소평가한다는 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 산소 부족 환경에서 메탄이 생성된다는 세부는 맞지만, 메탄이 이산화탄소보다 많이 배출된다거나 북극 온난화의 주된 원인이라는 주장은 지문에 없다. B는 '5분의 1 미만'이라는 수치를 인용하지만, 지문은 그럼에도 영향이 약 두 배가 될 수 있다고 하므로 결론이 반대이다. C는 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 '돌이킬 수 없는 지점'을 주장하므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The text's central point is that abrupt collapse of ice-rich permafrost (thermokarst) boosts methane release and strengthens a feedback loop, so models that assume only gradual thaw likely understate permafrost's contribution to warming. That makes D correct. A gets the detail about oxygen-poor ponds producing methane right, but the text never says methane emissions exceed carbon dioxide emissions or that methane is the main driver of Arctic warming. B cites the "less than a fifth" figure but reaches the opposite conclusion, since the text says abrupt thaw could roughly double the projected impact. C claims a point of no return has been passed, which the text explicitly says is not the researchers' conclusion.

hardJudge.note: D는 지문 2문단의 결론(급격한 붕괴 → 되먹임 강화 → 점진적 해빙 모델의 과소평가)을 정확히 요약함. A는 산소 부족·메탄 세부는 맞으나 '메탄>CO2 배출' 및 '주된 원인'은 지문에 없음, B는 '5분의 1 미만' 수치를 인용하나 '약 두 배' 결론과 반대, C는 지문이 명시 부정한 주장. 세 오답 모두 지문 요소를 부분적으로 차용해 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합. Turetsky et al. 2020(Nature Geoscience)의 '<20% 지역, 영향 약 2배' 추정과 사실관계 일치. 한·영 해설 결론·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: D는 지문의 결론 문장과 되먹임 고리 내용을 함께 종합한 선택지다. A와 B는 지문의 실제 세부 내용(산소 부족 상태에서의 메탄 생성, '5분의 1 미만' 수치)에 근거하고 있어 결론과 대조해 봐야 배제된다. C는 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 내용이라 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 그럴듯한 오답이다. Turetsky 등(2020)의 급격한 해빙 연구 내용(영구동토 지역의 20% 미만에 영향, 점진적 해빙만 고려한 예측 대비 영향 약 2배)과도 일치한다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
When lava cools into basalt, tiny grains of magnetite inside the rock lock in the direction of Earth's magnetic field at that moment. In the mid-twentieth century, geologists sampling stacked lava flows in places such as Iceland and Hawaii noticed that some layers recorded a field pointing roughly north, as it does today, while others recorded one pointing south. At first, some researchers suspected that certain minerals simply magnetized themselves backward as they cooled, a chemical quirk unrelated to the planet's field. That explanation weakened when scientists dated the flows using the slow decay of radioactive potassium into argon. Rocks of the same age from distant continents turned out to share the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. By matching polarity to age across many sites, researchers assembled a timeline of alternating normal and reversed intervals—the geomagnetic polarity timescale—which later helped confirm that the seafloor spreads outward from mid-ocean ridges.

According to the text, what led researchers to doubt that reversed magnetization in basalt was caused by a chemical quirk of certain minerals?
