That explanation weakened when scientists dated the flows using the slow decay of radioactive potassium into argon. Rocks of the same age from distant continents turned out to share the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. By matching polarity to age across many sites, researchers assembled a timeline of alternating normal and reversed intervals—the geomagnetic polarity timescale—which later helped confirm that the seafloor spreads outward from mid-ocean ridges.
problem.question: According to the text, what led researchers to doubt that reversed magnetization in basalt was caused by a chemical quirk of certain minerals?
options: Basalt layers from Iceland and Hawaii showed that reversed layers formed only in lava that cooled especially slowly.
Basalt layers that recorded a southward field turned out to be much older than layers that recorded a northward field.
Basalt layers of matching age from widely separated locations shared a polarity, and reversed layers were not mineralogically distinct.
Basalt layers dated by potassium-argon decay showed that magnetite grains lose their recorded direction over time.
problem.explanation: 지문은 연대 측정 결과 멀리 떨어진 대륙의 같은 나이 암석이 같은 극성을 보였고, 역전된 층이 정상 층과 광물 구성이 일관되게 다르지 않았다고 말하므로 정답은 C이다. A는 아이슬란드·하와이라는 실제 지명을 쓰지만 냉각 속도는 지문에 언급되지 않는다. B는 극성과 나이를 연결한다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 정상·역전 구간이 번갈아 나타난다고 할 뿐 역전 층이 더 오래되었다고 하지 않는다. D는 칼륨-아르곤 연대 측정을 언급하지만, 자철석이 기록된 방향을 잃는다는 내용은 지문에 없고 오히려 방향을 고정한다고 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The correct answer is C. The text says that once the flows were dated, rocks of the same age from distant continents had the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. A names real sampling sites from the text, but the text never mentions how fast the lava cooled. B sounds reasonable because it links polarity to age, but the text describes normal and reversed intervals alternating over time, not reversed layers being older. D mentions potassium-argon dating, but the text says magnetite locks in the field direction, not that the grains lose it over time.

quality.seed: earth and space science — Magnetic field reversal records in volcanic basalt columns documenting geomagnetic polarity timescale

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 지문의 "Rocks of the same age from distant continents turned out to share the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals"를 정확히 재진술. A(냉각 속도), B(역전층이 더 오래됨), D(자철석이 방향 상실)는 모두 지문에 없는 내용이며, 각각 지문의 지명·연대측정·K-Ar 요소를 차용해 그럴듯함을 갖춤. 지자기 역전·K-Ar 연대측정·해저확장 확인 등 과학사 내용도 사실에 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 오답 근거가 일치하고 한글 혼입 없음. 두 정보(연대 측정 → 극성 일치 + 광물 비차이)를 연결해야 하므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 지문의 두 근거(동일 연대·동일 극성, 광물 구성 차이 없음)를 결합해야 하는 바꿔 말하기 문항이다. 오답들은 지문 요소(지명, 연대 측정, 극성-나이 연결)를 차용해 그럴듯하다. 다만 C만 두 근거를 모두 담고 있어 비교적 쉽게 고를 수 있으나 medium 범위 안에 있다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that carries warm surface water northward and returns cold, dense water southward at depth.
- Direct measurements from the RAPID instrument array show that the AMOC's average strength from 2004 to 2012 was lower than its average from 2004 to 2008.
- In a 2023 statistical analysis of sea-surface temperature records, Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen estimated that the AMOC could collapse sometime between 2025 and 2095.
- They reported this range with 95 percent confidence and noted that it depends on assumptions about how early-warning signals behave.
- A separate modeling study by René van Westen and colleagues found that a collapse, if it occurred, would cool northwestern Europe by several degrees Celsius per decade.

The student wants to present the Ditlevsens' finding with the degree of confidence the researchers themselves attached to it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that carries warm surface water northward and returns cold, dense water southward at depth.
- Direct measurements from the RAPID instrument array show that the AMOC's average strength from 2004 to 2012 was lower than its average from 2004 to 2008.
- In a 2023 statistical analysis of sea-surface temperature records, Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen estimated that the AMOC could collapse sometime between 2025 and 2095.
- They reported this range with 95 percent confidence and noted that it depends on assumptions about how early-warning signals behave.
- A separate modeling study by René van Westen and colleagues found that a collapse, if it occurred, would cool northwestern Europe by several degrees Celsius per decade.
problem.question: The student wants to present the Ditlevsens' finding with the degree of confidence the researchers themselves attached to it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: According to Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen's 2023 analysis, the AMOC will collapse between 2025 and 2095, an outcome their sea-surface temperature records establish.
According to RAPID array data, the AMOC may possibly have been weaker from 2004 to 2012 than from 2004 to 2008, though this decline remains a tentative estimate.
According to Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen's 2023 analysis, an AMOC collapse, if it occurred, would likely cool northwestern Europe by several degrees Celsius per decade.

According to Peter and Susanne Ditlevsen's 2023 analysis, the AMOC could collapse between 2025 and 2095, an estimate given at 95 percent confidence and resting on assumptions about early-warning signals.
problem.explanation: 정답 D: 디틀레우센 부부의 결과는 'could', 95% 신뢰구간, 조기경보 신호에 대한 가정 의존이라는 잠정적 성격을 지닌다. D는 이 확실성 수준을 그대로 전달한다. A: 'will collapse', 'establish'라고 써서 잠정적 추정을 확정된 사실처럼 과장했다. B: RAPID 관측 자료는 직접 측정한 확정적 사실인데 'may possibly', 'tentative'를 붙여 불필요하게 약화했고, 디틀레우센 연구 내용도 아니다. C: 조건부·잠정적 어조는 맞지만, 유럽 냉각 결과는 반 베스턴 연구진의 연구이므로 디틀레우센 연구로 잘못 귀속했다.
problem.explanationEn: D is correct. The Ditlevsens' result is tentative: the collapse "could" happen, the range comes with 95 percent confidence, and it depends on assumptions about early-warning signals. D keeps all of these qualifications. A turns the estimate into a certainty by saying the AMOC "will" collapse and that the records "establish" it, which overstates the finding. B hedges something that was actually measured: the RAPID array directly recorded the weaker AMOC, so calling it "possibly" true and "tentative" understates it. B also isn't about the Ditlevsens. C uses the right cautious tone, but the cooling of Europe comes from van Westen and colleagues' study, not from the Ditlevsens' work.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정적 진술(AMOC 정의, RAPID 직접 측정)과 잠정적 진술(Ditlevsen 95% 신뢰구간·가정 의존 추정)이 공존. D는 'could', 95% 신뢰도, 가정 의존을 모두 그대로 반영해 목표(연구자 자신의 확신 수준으로 제시)에 정확히 부합. A는 'will/establish'로 과잉 확정, B는 직접 측정 자료를 'may possibly/tentative'로 과소 확신(동시에 대상 연구도 아님), C는 van Westen 연구 결과를 Ditlevsen에 오귀속. 수험자는 확실성 수준 판별과 출처 귀속을 동시에 수행해야 하므로 medium 이상. 사실관계(RAPID 2004–2012 약화, Ditlevsen 2023 2025–2095 95% CI, van Westen 유럽 냉각 수 °C/10년)도 실제 연구와 부합. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 모순 없이 설명.

advisory.note: 확정적 노트(RAPID 직접 측정)와 잠정적 노트(Ditlevsen의 could·95%·가정 의존)가 함께 있음. A는 과잉 일반화, B는 확실성 과소화, C는 출처를 잘못 귀속한 함정. 정답 D는 노트 두 개를 합쳐 확실성 수준을 정확히 전달함. B와 C는 대상 연구가 달라 쉽게 소거될 수 있어 난도가 다소 낮아질 수 있으나, hard 수준으로 인정할 만함.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines released about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere.
- In the year after Pinatubo erupted, average global surface temperature fell by roughly 0.5°C.
- The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington State released about 1 million tons of sulfur dioxide, much of it into the lower atmosphere.
- Mount St. Helens produced no measurable drop in average global surface temperature.

The student wants to suggest why two eruptions had different effects on the planet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Large volcanic eruptions can inject sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, where it forms sulfate aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.
- The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines released about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere.
- In the year after Pinatubo erupted, average global surface temperature fell by roughly 0.5°C.
- The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington State released about 1 million tons of sulfur dioxide, much of it into the lower atmosphere.
- Mount St. Helens produced no measurable drop in average global surface temperature.
problem.question: The student wants to suggest why two eruptions had different effects on the planet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Mount Pinatubo sent about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere and was followed by a global cooling of roughly 0.5°C, whereas Mount St. Helens released only about 1 million tons, largely into the lower atmosphere, and caused no measurable global cooling.
Mount Pinatubo sent about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, where it formed sulfate aerosols, and was followed by a global cooling of roughly 0.5°C in the following year.
Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines in 1991, whereas Mount St. Helens erupted in Washington State in 1980, about eleven years earlier.

Mount Pinatubo sent about 15 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere and cooled the planet by roughly 0.5°C for a decade, whereas Mount St. Helens released about 1 million tons and slightly warmed the planet.
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 두 화산의 이산화황 양·주입 고도(원인)와 기온 영향(결과)을 대조해 효과 차이의 이유를 제시한다. B: 피나투보 한쪽 사실만 담아 비교가 없으므로 목표의 절반만 달성한다. C: 두 분화를 결합했지만 장소·연도만 대조해 효과 차이의 이유와 무관하다. D: '10년간 냉각', '약간의 온난화'는 노트에 없는 내용으로 사실을 왜곡한다(노트는 이듬해 0.5°C 하강, 측정 가능한 변화 없음).
problem.explanationEn: A is correct: it contrasts the two eruptions' sulfur dioxide amounts and injection heights (the likely cause) with their temperature effects (the result), suggesting why the outcomes differed. B covers only Pinatubo, so with no comparison it accomplishes only half the goal. C combines both eruptions but contrasts only location and date, which does not explain the different effects. D adds claims not in the notes: a decade of cooling and slight warming. The notes say the cooling happened in the year after the eruption and that St. Helens caused no measurable change.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 두 분화의 SO2 양·주입 고도(원인)와 기온 반응(결과)을 모두 대조하여 '효과 차이의 이유'라는 목표를 충족한다. B는 피나투보 한쪽만, C는 두 분화를 비교하되 장소·연도라는 목표와 무관한 축으로 비교(목표 초점 오판 유도), D는 '10년간 냉각'·'약간 온난화' 등 노트에 없는 왜곡 내용 포함. 노트 수치(피나투보 약 15백만 톤·약 0.5°C 하강, 세인트헬렌스 약 1백만 톤)는 실제 과학적 기록과 부합. 네 가지 사실 조합(양·고도·결과×2)을 인과 방향에 맞게 통합해야 하고, 비교 형식만으로는 정답 판별이 안 되므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구한다.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞고 해설도 일관된다. 다만 오답의 결함이 모두 표면적이다. B는 한쪽 사실만 담았고, C는 무관한 정보를 대조하며, D는 노트에 없는 수치·주장을 넣었다. 그래서 정답을 고르는 데는 '두 대상 비교 + 원인 정보'를 확인하는 정도의 판단만 필요하고, 이는 전형적인 medium 수준이다. A만 유일하게 두 화산을 비교하면서 원인까지 담고 있어 바로 정답으로 드러난다. 확실성 수준이나 범위 조정을 겨냥한 그럴듯한 오답(예: 비교는 하지만 원인 정보가 빠진 선택지)이 없다. 또 A는 St. Helens가 냉각을 '일으키지 않았다(caused no)'고 인과적으로 표현해 노트와 미세한 차이가 있지만 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tallgrass prairie plants such as big bluestem can grow roots reaching more than 3 meters deep.
- Much of the carbon these plants absorb is moved underground into roots and soil rather than kept in leaves and stems.
- Carbon held deep in prairie soil can remain there for centuries, whereas carbon in aboveground plant matter is often released within a few years through decay or fire.
- Because of this durable underground storage, some climate researchers view prairie restoration as a promising way to help offset greenhouse gas emissions.
- Prairies also provide habitat for pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
- Restored prairie plots at Minnesota's Cedar Creek research station have been monitored for several decades.

The student wants to emphasize why prairies matter for addressing climate change. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tallgrass prairie plants such as big bluestem can grow roots reaching more than 3 meters deep.
- Much of the carbon these plants absorb is moved underground into roots and soil rather than kept in leaves and stems.
- Carbon held deep in prairie soil can remain there for centuries, whereas carbon in aboveground plant matter is often released within a few years through decay or fire.
- Because of this durable underground storage, some climate researchers view prairie restoration as a promising way to help offset greenhouse gas emissions.
- Prairies also provide habitat for pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
- Restored prairie plots at Minnesota's Cedar Creek research station have been monitored for several decades.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize why prairies matter for addressing climate change. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Tallgrass prairie plants such as big bluestem can send roots more than 3 meters into the ground, deeper than many other grassland species.
By locking absorbed carbon deep in the soil for centuries rather than releasing it within a few years, prairies offer a durable way to help offset greenhouse gas emissions.
Prairies are complex ecosystems with deep-rooted plants, pollinator habitat, long-studied research plots, and soils that hold carbon.
Beyond their role in the soil, restored prairies provide valuable habitat for pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 기후 변화 대응에서 프레리가 중요한 이유를 강조하려면 탄소가 토양 깊이 수 세기 동안 저장된다는 점(지상부는 수년 내 방출)과 그 결과 온실가스 상쇄에 도움이 된다는 점을 연결해야 한다. B만 이 인과를 담는다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 뿌리 깊이라는 세부 사실만 제시하고 탄소 저장이나 기후와의 연결이 없다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 여러 항목을 나열한 개관이라 기후 측면의 중요성을 강조하지 못하고 초점이 흐려진다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 수분 매개자 서식지는 기후 완화와 무관한 생태적 가치다.
problem.explanationEn:
B is correct. To emphasize why prairies matter for climate change, a sentence has to connect long-lasting carbon storage (deep soil carbon stays for centuries, while aboveground carbon is released within a few years) to the climate benefit of offsetting emissions. B is the only choice that makes this connection.
A is too narrow. It gives only the root-depth detail and never links it to carbon or climate.
C is too broad. It lists many features like an overview, so the climate point gets lost.
D focuses on a note that doesn't serve the goal. Pollinator habitat is an ecological benefit, but it has nothing to do with climate mitigation.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 노트 2·3·4(지하 이동, 수 세기 저장 vs 수년 내 방출, 온실가스 상쇄)를 인과 사슬로 통합해 목표에 정확히 부합한다. A는 세부 사실만, C는 나열식 개관, D는 무관 항목으로 오답 구조가 명확하다. 사소한 지적: (1) A의 "deeper than many other grassland species"는 노트에 없는 정보로, SAT 관례상 선택지는 노트 내용에 한정되는 것이 바람직하다. (2) B는 노트의 "some climate researchers view ... as a promising way"를 "prairies offer a durable way"로 다소 확정적으로 바꿨으나 "help offset"의 완화 표현이 있어 정답 판정에 지장은 없다. 전체적으로 hard 수준의 다중 노트 통합과 범위 조정을 실제로 요구한다.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 노트 2~4를 종합하므로 타당하다. 다만 오답이 너무 쉽게 걸러진다. A와 D에는 기후 관련 내용이 전혀 없고, C는 단순 나열이라 바로 탈락한다. 결국 '기후'라는 키워드만 맞춰도 B를 고를 수 있어 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 확실성 구분(claim_certainty_discrimination)을 실제로 시험하지도 않는다. 오히려 B가 노트 4의 'some researchers… promising'이라는 잠정적 주장을 단정적으로 바꿔 놓았다. A에는 노트에 없는 비교 정보가 섞여 있다.

problem.passage:
When companies extract natural gas from shale, they often use hydraulic fracturing: water is pumped underground at high pressure to crack the rock and release the gas. This process produces thousands of tiny earthquakes, called microseismic events, that are far too weak for people to feel. Geologists in western Canada studied records from several fracturing sites and found that, in a small number of cases, these swarms of tiny quakes were followed by larger earthquakes strong enough to be felt at the surface. The researchers concluded that the larger quakes happened mainly where the injected fluid reached faults that were already under stress, which suggests that companies could reduce the risk by mapping such faults before choosing where to drill.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: When companies extract natural gas from shale, they often use hydraulic fracturing: water is pumped underground at high pressure to crack the rock and release the gas. This process produces thousands of tiny earthquakes, called microseismic events, that are far too weak for people to feel. Geologists in western Canada studied records from several fracturing sites and found that, in a small number of cases, these swarms of tiny quakes were followed by larger earthquakes strong enough to be felt at the surface. The researchers concluded that the larger quakes happened mainly where the injected fluid reached faults that were already under stress, which suggests that companies could reduce the risk by mapping such faults before choosing where to drill.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Hydraulic fracturing usually causes earthquakes strong enough to be felt, so it should not be used anywhere in western Canada.
Microseismic events are too weak to detect, so researchers cannot tell whether fracturing affects the ground.
Fracturing occasionally leads to noticeable earthquakes, mostly where fluid reaches stressed faults, so locating those faults may lower the danger.
Shale gas is released mainly by natural earthquakes, so fracturing adds little to the amount of gas companies collect.
problem.explanation: 지문은 수압 파쇄가 작은 미소지진을 일으키지만, 드물게 이미 응력을 받은 단층에 유체가 닿으면 느낄 수 있는 지진이 발생하며, 단층을 미리 파악하면 위험을 줄일 수 있다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '드물게(a small number of cases)'를 '대개'로 바꾸고 전면 금지라는 지문에 없는 결론을 덧붙였다. B는 미소지진이 사람이 느끼기엔 약할 뿐 연구자들이 기록을 분석했다는 내용과 모순된다. D는 가스가 자연 지진으로 방출된다는, 지문에 없는 주장이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that fracturing causes tiny quakes, that only in a few cases larger felt quakes followed, mostly where fluid reached already-stressed faults, and that mapping those faults could reduce risk, so C is correct. A changes "a small number of cases" into "usually" and adds a ban the text never proposes. B contradicts the text, since the quakes are only too weak for people to feel—researchers did study their records. D makes a claim about natural earthquakes releasing gas that the text never makes.

quality.seed: earth and space science — Microseismicity swarms and induced seismicity from hydraulic fracturing operations in shale gas extraction

hardJudge.note: C는 지문 전체(미소지진→드물게 큰 지진→응력 단층→단층 지도화로 위험 저감)를 정확히 요약. A는 빈도 과장+지문에 없는 금지 결론, B는 '느끼기엔 약함'을 '탐지 불가'로 왜곡, D는 지문에 없는 주장으로 각각 전형적 오답 유형. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 지문은 원작 서술로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음. 어휘·문장 평이, 단서가 직접 드러나 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 지문 요지를 정확히 요약한다. 오답 A(과장), B(모순), D(지문에 없는 내용)는 전형적인 오답 유형이다. 지문이 다소 길지만 단서가 명시적이어서 easy 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
When a volcano erupts explosively, it sends a tall column of ash into the sky. Scientists use computer programs called dispersion models to predict where that ash will travel and how far from the volcano it will fall to the ground. These models combine information about the height of the ash column, the size of the ash particles, and the speed and direction of the wind at different altitudes. Large, heavy particles tend to drop out close to the volcano, while fine particles can be carried hundreds of kilometers away. By running these models, scientists can warn airports, farms, and towns about where ash is likely to land, giving people time to prepare.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: When a volcano erupts explosively, it sends a tall column of ash into the sky. Scientists use computer programs called dispersion models to predict where that ash will travel and how far from the volcano it will fall to the ground. These models combine information about the height of the ash column, the size of the ash particles, and the speed and direction of the wind at different altitudes. Large, heavy particles tend to drop out close to the volcano, while fine particles can be carried hundreds of kilometers away. By running these models, scientists can warn airports, farms, and towns about where ash is likely to land, giving people time to prepare.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Scientists have found that wind speed matters more than particle size when ash falls near a volcano.
Scientists have shown that explosive eruptions produce taller ash columns than other kinds of eruptions.
Scientists have learned that fine ash particles are more harmful to farms than large particles are.
Scientists use models built from eruption and weather data to forecast where volcanic ash will settle.
problem.explanation: 지문 전체는 과학자들이 기둥 높이, 입자 크기, 바람 정보를 결합한 분산 모델로 화산재가 어디에 떨어질지 예측하고 경고한다는 내용이므로 D가 중심 내용이다. A는 바람과 입자 크기의 중요도를 비교하지만 지문에는 그런 비교가 없다. B는 분출 유형 간 기둥 높이 비교로, 지문에서 언급되지 않는다. C는 입자 크기별 피해 정도를 말하지만 지문은 이동 거리만 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The whole text explains that scientists combine column height, particle size, and wind data in dispersion models to predict where ash will land and to warn people, so D states the main idea. A compares the importance of wind and particle size, but the text never makes that comparison. B compares column heights across eruption types, which the text doesn't discuss. C claims fine ash harms farms more, but the text only describes how far different particles travel, not how harmful they are.

quality.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric dispersion modeling of volcanic ash columns and tephra deposition distance predictions

hardJudge.note: 지문은 분산 모델이 기둥 높이·입자 크기·바람 자료를 결합해 화산재 낙하 위치를 예측하고 경고한다는 내용으로, D가 전체를 정확히 요약한다. A(바람 vs 입자 크기 중요도 비교), B(분출 유형별 기둥 높이 비교), C(입자별 농장 피해 비교)는 모두 지문에 없는 비교를 담은 전형적 세부사항 과장 오답이다. 한·영 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 평이한 어휘와 직접 제시된 단서로 easy 난이도에 적합하다.

advisory.note: 평이한 지문이고, 중심 내용이 직접 드러난다. 오답은 지문에 나온 요소(바람, 입자 크기, 기둥 높이, 농장)를 활용해 근거 없는 비교를 만든 전형적인 함정이다.

problem.passage:
In a 2019 field report on the Mammoth Cave system, hydrogeologist Ellen Marsh described how slightly acidic groundwater shapes limestone over geologic time. "Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide as it seeps through the soil," she wrote, "and the resulting carbonic acid ______ calcite along cracks in the bedrock, gradually widening them into passages large enough for a person to walk through."

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a 2019 field report on the Mammoth Cave system, hydrogeologist Ellen Marsh described how slightly acidic groundwater shapes limestone over geologic time. "Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide as it seeps through the soil," she wrote, "and the resulting carbonic acid ______ calcite along cracks in the bedrock, gradually widening them into passages large enough for a person to walk through."
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: dissolves
dissolved
dissolving
had dissolved
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 인용문 안에서 Marsh는 지금도 반복되는 일반적 과정을 현재 시제로 설명한다("absorbs," "seeps"). 'and'로 이어진 두 번째 독립절의 동사도 이와 맞춰 현재 시제 "dissolves"가 되어야 한다. B "dissolved"는 인용문을 둘러싼 주절의 과거 시제("described," "wrote")에만 맞춘 것이다. 그런데 인용문 안의 시제는 인용문 내부 문맥을 따라야 한다. C "dissolving"은 분사여서 주어 "the resulting carbonic acid"에 붙는 정동사가 없어지므로 병렬 구조 가운데 한 항목만 형태가 달라진다. D "had dissolved"(과거완료)는 'wrote'보다 앞선 일로 해석하면 주절과만 어울린다. 하지만 인용문의 현재 시제 일반 진술과 맞지 않고, 뒤에 오는 "gradually widening"이 나타내는 지속적 과정과도 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: Choice A is correct. Inside the quotation, Marsh describes a general process that keeps happening, and she uses the present tense to do it ("absorbs," "seeps"). The second independent clause joined by "and" needs a matching present-tense verb, so "dissolves" is right. Choice B, "dissolved," only matches the past-tense verbs in the frame around the quotation ("described," "wrote"). The tense inside a quotation follows the context of the quotation itself. Choice C, "dissolving," is a participle, so the subject "the resulting carbonic acid" would have no finite verb. That makes one item in the parallel structure a different form from the others. Choice D, "had dissolved," could fit "wrote" if you read it as something that happened earlier. But it clashes with the present-tense general statement in the quotation and with the ongoing process shown by "gradually widening."

hardJudge.note: 인용문 내부의 현재 시제(absorbs, seeps)와 외부 주절의 과거 시제(described, wrote)가 충돌하는 구조로, 수험생이 인용문 내부 문맥을 기준으로 시제를 판단해야 한다. 정답 A 'dissolves' 검산 결과 옳으며, B는 외부 시제 유인, C는 정동사 결여(단편), D는 과거완료로 일반 진술·'gradually widening'의 지속 과정과 불일치. 해설의 각 오답 설명도 정확하다. 석회암 용식 과정(탄산에 의한 방해석 용해)은 사실과 부합. 다만 인용문 내 동일 문장에 현재 시제 단서가 바로 인접해 있어 난이도는 hard 하한 수준.

advisory.note: 지문 바깥 문장의 과거 시제(described, wrote)가 B와 D로 유도하는 함정 역할을 한다. 정답을 고르려면 인용문 안의 현재 시제 일반 진술(absorbs, seeps)과 시제를 맞춰야 한다. 정답 A는 옳다. 난이도는 hard 하한선 근처이지만, 단순히 계산량이 많아서 생기는 어려움은 아니다.

problem.passage:
In March 1989, an intense geomagnetic storm collapsed the power grid of the Canadian province of Quebec within about ninety seconds. Analyzing ground magnetometer records from that night decades later, ______ that the planetary Kp index, which rates global geomagnetic disturbance on a scale from 0 to 9, had reached its maximum value as a series of auroral substorms suddenly released energy stored in Earth's magnetotail.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In March 1989, an intense geomagnetic storm collapsed the power grid of the Canadian province of Quebec within about ninety seconds. Analyzing ground magnetometer records from that night decades later, ______ that the planetary Kp index, which rates global geomagnetic disturbance on a scale from 0 to 9, had reached its maximum value as a series of auroral substorms suddenly released energy stored in Earth's magnetotail.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the magnetometer data revealed to geophysicist Ana Ruiz
geophysicist Ana Ruiz confirmed
the 1989 storm was shown by geophysicist Ana Ruiz
the work of geophysicist Ana Ruiz established
problem.explanation:
분사구문 'Analyzing ground magnetometer records...'의 의미상 주어, 즉 기록을 분석한 사람이 주절의 주어로 바로 와야 한다. 기록을 분석할 수 있는 행위자는 지구물리학자 Ana Ruiz뿐이므로 그녀를 주어로 둔 B가 정답이다.
A: 수식어구 바로 근처에 있는 무생물 명사(magnetometer records/data)를 주어로 삼았다. 그러면 데이터가 스스로 기록을 분석한 셈이 되므로 현수 수식어 오류다. Ruiz는 전치사 to의 목적어 자리에 묻혀 있다.
C: 앞 문장의 배경 명사(1989년 폭풍)를 주어로 삼았다. 폭풍은 기록을 분석할 수 없으며, 수동태 때문에 행위자가 by구 뒤로 밀려났다.
D: 행위자와 비슷해 보이는 'the work of ... Ruiz'를 주어로 삼았다. 문법상 주어는 사람이 아니라 work이므로, 연구 결과물이 분석을 한 꼴이 되어 여전히 현수 수식어 오류다.
problem.explanationEn:
An introductory participial phrase has to describe the subject that comes right after it. The phrase "Analyzing ground magnetometer records..." describes someone doing the analyzing, and only the geophysicist Ana Ruiz can do that. Choice B puts her in the subject position, so B is correct.
A: This makes "the magnetometer data" the subject, because it is the nonliving noun closest to the modifier. Data can't analyze records, so the modifier dangles. Ruiz is buried as the object of "to."
C: This makes the background noun "the 1989 storm" the subject. A storm can't analyze records either, and the passive voice pushes the real actor into a "by" phrase.
D: "The work of geophysicist Ana Ruiz" looks like it names the actor, but the grammatical subject is "work," not Ruiz. Work can't analyze anything, so the modifier still dangles.

hardJudge.note: 분사구문 'Analyzing ground magnetometer records...'의 의미상 주어는 기록을 분석한 사람이므로 B(geophysicist Ana Ruiz confirmed)만 적격. A는 'magnetometer data'로 앞 명사 반복을 통해 인접 일치 착각 유도, C는 배경 명사 'the 1989 storm' 수동태, D는 'the work of Ruiz'로 사람 이름이 포함되어 그럴듯하지만 문법적 주어가 work인 전형적 hard 오답. 사실 관계(1989년 3월 퀘벡 정전 약 90초, Kp 0–9 척도 최대치 도달, 서브스톰의 자기꼬리 에너지 방출) 모두 정확. 해설도 정답과 각 오답의 오류를 정확히 설명함.

advisory.note: B만 분사구문의 의미상 행위자(Ruiz)를 주절 주어로 둔다. D('the work of Ruiz')는 행위자를 겉으로 드러내지만 문법상 주어는 work라서, 형태만 맞추는 수준을 넘어 의미상 행위자를 가려내야 하는 함정이다. C는 수동태에 that절이 이어져 구조적으로도 어색하다. 1989년 퀘벡 정전 사건(약 90초, Kp 9)은 사실과 부합한다. 다만 전형적인 현수 수식어 문항에 가까워서 hard로서의 차별성은 크지 않다.

problem.passage:
Conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which copies DNA so that trace amounts can be detected, typically requires benchtop thermal cyclers and sample volumes measured in tens of microliters. Engineers developing microfluidic "lab-on-a-chip" devices have shown that splitting a sample into thousands of picoliter droplets, each heated and cooled as it moves through channels etched in a chip, can ______ this process: the same amplification occurs, but in a device small enough to hold in one hand and with each cycle finishing in seconds rather than minutes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which copies DNA so that trace amounts can be detected, typically requires benchtop thermal cyclers and sample volumes measured in tens of microliters. Engineers developing microfluidic "lab-on-a-chip" devices have shown that splitting a sample into thousands of picoliter droplets, each heated and cooled as it moves through channels etched in a chip, can ______ this process: the same amplification occurs, but in a device small enough to hold in one hand and with each cycle finishing in seconds rather than minutes.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: condense
replicate
supplant
complicate
problem.explanation: 콜론 뒤에서 같은 증폭이 일어나지만 손바닥 크기 장치에서 더 짧은 시간에 끝난다고 설명하므로, 과정을 동일하게 유지하면서 크기와 시간을 줄인다는 뜻의 A(condense)가 정확하다. B(replicate)는 같은 증폭이 일어난다는 부분과는 맞지만, 지문의 핵심인 소형화와 시간 단축을 담지 못한다. C(supplant)는 새로운 방식이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 같은 증폭 과정이 유지된다고 했으므로 PCR 자체를 다른 것으로 대체한다는 의미는 맞지 않는다. D(complicate)는 장치가 더 작고 빨라졌다는 설명과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: After the colon, the text says the same amplification happens, but in a handheld device and with cycles that take seconds instead of minutes. That means the process is kept the same while being shrunk in size and time, so A ("condense") is the precise choice. B ("replicate") matches the idea that the same amplification occurs, but it misses the key point about miniaturization and speed. C ("supplant") might seem plausible because the device is a new approach, but the text says the PCR process itself is kept, not replaced by something else. D ("complicate") goes against the description of a smaller, faster device.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Microfluidic lab-on-chip device droplet manipulation and PCR amplification miniaturization for diagnostics

hardJudge.note: 콜론 뒤 '같은 증폭이 일어나지만 더 작고 더 빠르다'는 설명이 '과정을 축소·단축한다'는 condense를 정확히 뒷받침함. replicate는 '같은 증폭' 부분만, supplant는 '새 장치' 부분만 포착해 비교·배제가 필요한 적절한 오답이고, complicate는 명백히 반대. 미세유체 액적 PCR(피코리터 액적, 초 단위 사이클) 서술은 실제 연구와 부합. 해설 한·영 모두 정답과 선택지 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. medium 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 콜론 뒤의 '같은 증폭'과 '작은 크기·짧은 시간'을 함께 읽어야 condense가 정답으로 확정된다. replicate와 supplant는 각각 부분적인 근거가 있어 매력적인 오답으로 작동한다. 다만 supplant는 the process를 목적어로 삼기에 다소 어색하다. 디지털 PCR이 피코리터 단위 액적을 쓴다는 설명은 사실에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Some modern buildings stay clean with very little scrubbing because their windows and walls are covered with an extremely thin layer of titanium dioxide. This coating is far thinner than a human hair and cannot be seen. When sunlight strikes it, the ultraviolet part of the light energizes the titanium dioxide, which then breaks down dirt, grease, and other materials made of carbon that have stuck to the surface. The coating also causes rainwater to spread out in a smooth sheet instead of forming droplets, so the rain rinses away whatever has been broken down. In this way, sunlight and rain together do much of the cleaning work that people would otherwise have to do.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Some modern buildings stay clean with very little scrubbing because their windows and walls are covered with an extremely thin layer of titanium dioxide. This coating is far thinner than a human hair and cannot be seen. When sunlight strikes it, the ultraviolet part of the light energizes the titanium dioxide, which then breaks down dirt, grease, and other materials made of carbon that have stuck to the surface. The coating also causes rainwater to spread out in a smooth sheet instead of forming droplets, so the rain rinses away whatever has been broken down. In this way, sunlight and rain together do much of the cleaning work that people would otherwise have to do.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A titanium dioxide coating keeps buildings clean mainly by blocking rain from ever reaching windows and walls.
A titanium dioxide coating helps surfaces clean themselves by using sunlight to break down grime that rain then washes off.
A titanium dioxide coating keeps buildings clean mainly by making surfaces too smooth for dirt to stick in the first place.
A titanium dioxide coating helps surfaces stay clean only when people scrub them regularly after rainstorms.
problem.explanation: 지문은 이산화티타늄 코팅이 자외선을 받아 오염물을 분해하고, 빗물이 넓게 퍼져 분해된 것을 씻어 내어 햇빛과 비가 청소를 대신한다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 코팅이 빗물을 막는다고 하지만, 지문에서는 오히려 빗물이 표면에 얇게 퍼져 씻어 낸다. C는 먼지가 애초에 붙지 않는다고 하지만, 지문은 표면에 붙은 먼지를 분해한다고 말한다. D는 사람이 정기적으로 문질러야 한다고 하지만, 지문은 거의 문지르지 않아도 된다고 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that the coating uses the ultraviolet part of sunlight to break down dirt, and that rain spreads into a sheet and rinses that material away, so B is correct. A is wrong because the coating does not block rain; it makes rain spread across the surface so it can rinse it. C is wrong because the text says dirt does stick to the surface and is then broken down, not that dirt never sticks. D is wrong because the text says these buildings need very little scrubbing, since sunlight and rain do most of the work.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Self-cleaning titanium dioxide nanocoating photocatalytic decomposition under UV radiation exposure

hardJudge.note: 지문 전체 요지(자외선으로 오염물 분해 + 빗물이 씻어 냄)를 B가 정확히 포착. A는 '빗물이 퍼진다'를 '빗물을 막는다'로 오독, C는 '붙은 먼지를 분해'를 '애초에 안 붙음'으로 오독, D는 첫 문장 '거의 문지르지 않음'과 직접 모순되는 전형적 오답. 과학 사실(TiO2 광촉매·초친수성)도 정확. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. easy 수준 적합.

advisory.note: 광촉매 분해와 친수성 세척에 대한 설명은 과학적으로 정확하다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나므로 한 단계로 풀린다. 오답은 그럴듯한 오개념이다(C는 흔히 하는 오해이다). D는 'only'와 'regularly' 때문에 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 easy 범위 안이다.

problem.passage:
Composite laminates are made by stacking thin layers of fiber-reinforced material and bonding them together. One common weakness of these materials is delamination, in which the layers begin to separate. To measure how well a laminate resists this kind of failure, engineers often use a test called the double cantilever beam test. A small crack is placed between two layers at one end of a sample, and the two arms of the sample are slowly pulled apart. By recording the force needed to make the crack grow, engineers can calculate a value that shows how much energy the material absorbs before the layers split further. Higher values mean that a laminate is better at holding its layers together.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Composite laminates are made by stacking thin layers of fiber-reinforced material and bonding them together. One common weakness of these materials is delamination, in which the layers begin to separate. To measure how well a laminate resists this kind of failure, engineers often use a test called the double cantilever beam test. A small crack is placed between two layers at one end of a sample, and the two arms of the sample are slowly pulled apart. By recording the force needed to make the crack grow, engineers can calculate a value that shows how much energy the material absorbs before the layers split further. Higher values mean that a laminate is better at holding its layers together.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Engineers use a pulling test to make composite laminates stronger by adding extra layers to each sample.
Engineers have found that the double cantilever beam test causes composite laminates to fail more often than other tests do.
Engineers use a specific test to measure how well composite laminates resist the separation of their layers.
Engineers prefer composite laminates to other materials because their layers never separate under force.
problem.explanation: 지문은 복합 적층재의 약점인 층 분리(delamination)를 소개한 뒤, 이 분리에 대한 저항을 측정하는 이중 외팔보 시험의 방법과 의미를 설명하므로 C가 중심 내용이다. A는 시험이 재료를 더 강하게 만든다고 하지만, 지문에서 시험은 측정 수단일 뿐이다. B는 이 시험이 다른 시험보다 파손을 더 많이 일으킨다는 비교를 말하지만 지문에 그런 비교는 없다. D는 층이 절대 분리되지 않는다고 하지만, 지문은 층 분리를 흔한 약점으로 제시한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text introduces delamination, a common weakness of composite laminates, and then explains how the double cantilever beam test measures resistance to it, so C states the main idea. A says the test makes laminates stronger, but the text presents the test only as a way to measure strength. B makes a comparison with other tests that the text never makes. D claims the layers never separate, which contradicts the text's description of delamination as a common weakness.
